prompt: In December 2025, Stage IV of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) was invoked in Delhi-NCR. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It was invoked after Delhi's Air Quality Index breached 450 and slid into the 'Severe+' band.
Construction and demolition were halted across Delhi-NCR, with public works included in the halt.
Offices were pushed to have roughly 50% of staff work from home.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: Stage IV followed AQI breaching 450 in the 'Severe+' band, halted all construction and demolition including public works, and pushed offices to roughly 50% work from home. Stage IV, the toughest curbs under GRAP, also barred non-essential trucks and many diesel goods vehicles from Delhi.
source: All construction and demolition across Delhi-NCR stops, including public works.

prompt: In December 2025, after a deadly fire at a nightclub in Arpora, north Goa, investigators said the village panchayat had failed to use its power to seal the illegally operating premises. Under which law is the local body empowered to seal such premises?
explain: Investigators cited Section 72-A of the Goa Panchayat Raj Act, which empowers the local body to seal premises such as the nightclub, which lacked a valid construction licence and occupancy certificate. Its trade licence had expired in March 2024, yet the panchayat did not seal it before the fire on 6 December 2025 that killed 25 people.
source: “Under Section 72-A of the Goa Panchayat Raj Act, the local body is empowered to seal such premises.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Anjor Vision 2047, a development roadmap unveiled in December 2025:
items: It was unveiled by Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai on the opening day of the state Assembly's winter session.
The document identifies 13 priority sectors and 10 missions.
Chhattisgarh, the state that released it, was carved out of Bihar in 2000.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000, not Bihar. Sai unveiled the roadmap on 14 December 2025 while the Congress boycotted the session's opening day.
source: Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Amrit Bharat Express trains:
items: They are air-conditioned premium trains aimed at long-distance business travellers.
In January 2026, the Prime Minister flagged off five Amrit Bharat Express services across Assam and West Bengal.
Amrit Bharat trains have been running since December 2023.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. Amrit Bharat trains are non-air conditioned, long-distance trains built for the bulk of rail travellers, with better basics like CCTV, charging points and modular toilets. Thirty such trains have run since December 2023, and the January 2026 launch is the next expansion wave.
source: These are non-air conditioned, long-distance trains built for the bulk of Indian rail travellers.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of origin and destination for Amrit Bharat Express services flagged off in January 2026:
items: Guwahati — Rohtak
Howrah — Delhi
Santragachi — Chennai
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three routes were among the five services launched. Two start from Assam (Guwahati–Rohtak and Dibrugarh–Lucknow), while three start from West Bengal (Howrah–Delhi, Sealdah–Varanasi and Santragachi–Chennai).
source: Two services start from Assam (Northeast India)—Guwahati–Rohtak and Dibrugarh–Lucknow, while three launch from West Bengal (East India): Howrah–Delhi, Sealdah–Varanasi, and Santragachi–Chennai.

prompt: Consider the following statements about institutional responses to drinking water contamination in India in January 2026:
items: The National Green Tribunal took action over reports of sewage contamination in drinking water across parts of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
The National Human Rights Commission issued a notice over a typhoid surge in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, linked to contaminated supply.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct. The NGT acted on sewage contamination reports across three states, and the NHRC separately issued a notice over the Gandhinagar typhoid surge. These responses followed a diarrhoea outbreak in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, that killed at least nine and hospitalised over 200 people.
source: Separately, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) issued a notice over a typhoid surge in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, tied to contaminated supply on January 8.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the “Will for Peace 2026” naval exercise held in January 2026:
items: It was held off Cape Town, with South Africa as host.
Iran was among the participating countries.
India's Ministry of External Affairs described it as a regular, institutionalised BRICS activity.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. On 17 January 2026 the MEA called the exercise entirely a South African initiative, not a regular or institutionalised BRICS activity, and noted that not all BRICS members joined. Iran's participation drew US-side criticism, and Pretoria launched an inquiry into it.
source: South Africa’s “Will for Peace 2026” naval exercise ran from January 10–16, 2026 off Cape Town, after warships began arriving around January 9.

prompt: In January 2026, explaining its absence from a South African-hosted naval exercise, India's Ministry of External Affairs cited IBSAMAR as its standing maritime format. IBSAMAR brings together India with which two countries?
explain: IBSAMAR is the India–Brazil–South Africa maritime format, last held in October 2024. The MEA pointed to it while stating that India had not taken part in previous South African-led drills of the Will for Peace kind.
source: pointed to IBSAMAR (India–Brazil–South Africa) as its standing maritime format (last held October 2024).

prompt: Consider the following statements in the context of political developments in January 2026:
items: In the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) elections, the BJP won an outright majority of the corporation's 227 seats.
Mamata Banerjee has run West Bengal since 2011, winning three straight mandates.
Puducherry was among the places with assembly elections due within a few months.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. The BJP won 89 of the BMC's 227 seats, a strong showing but short of a majority. Assembly elections were due in Assam, West Bengal, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, and Mamata Banerjee had governed West Bengal since 2011.
source: Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is riding momentum after a strong showing in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), Mumbai’s powerful municipal body, where it won 89 of 227 seats.

prompt: In January 2026, US President Donald Trump invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi to join the 'Board of Peace'. Consider the following statements about the Board:
items: The mandate approved by the UN Security Council in 2025 is limited to Gaza.
The UN Security Council mandate runs until 2030.
Its executive board includes Ajay Banga of the World Bank.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Security Council mandate runs only until 2027, not 2030. The Board, with Trump at the helm, will oversee a technocratic Palestinian committee governing Gaza, and around 60 countries had been invited.
source: The UN Security Council approved the board’s mandate in 2025, but it’s limited to Gaza and only until 2027.

prompt: In January 2026, the President of the UAE, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, visited New Delhi and met PM Narendra Modi. Consider the following statements about the deliverables listed in the joint statement:
items: The two sides aimed to push bilateral trade to USD 200 billion by 2032.
The two sides concluded a 20-year LNG supply agreement.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The LNG supply agreement runs for 10 years, not 20. The deliverables also covered AI and supercomputing cooperation and payments connectivity, during a visit scheduled to last less than two hours.
source: The MEA joint statement is packed with deliverables, including pushing trade to USD 200bn by 2032, investment promotion (including Gujarat’s Dholera project), cooperation on AI and supercomputing, payments connectivity, and a 10-year LNG supply agreement.

prompt: In January 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh flagged off the first tranche of guided Pinaka rockets for export. To which country were they sent?
explain: The first tranche of guided Pinaka rockets was bound for Armenia, which signed its Pinaka deal in September 2022. Singh said India's defence exports have climbed to ₹24,000 crore (USD 2.9 billion).
source: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh flagged off the first tranche of guided Pinaka rockets bound for Armenia.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Pinaka rocket system, as reported in January 2026:
items: It was developed by DRDO's Armament Research and Development Establishment (ARDE).
It was first deployed during the 1999 Kargil War.
The batch of guided rockets exported to Armenia was produced at a public-sector ordnance factory in Pune.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. The batch was produced at Solar Defence and Aerospace's facility in Nagpur, a private firm, which reflects the growing private role in India's defence supply chain. The system has been upgraded since Kargil to extend range and precision beyond its original 37.5 km.
source: The current batch was produced at Solar Defence and Aerospace’s Nagpur facility, underscoring the growing role of private firms in India’s defence supply chain.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of countries and their reported interest in India's Pinaka rocket system as of January 2026:
items: France — Running evaluation trials
Indonesia — Expressed interest
Nigeria — Expressed interest
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correct. France is running evaluation trials, while Indonesia and Nigeria have expressed interest. Armenia is the first buyer and signed its deal in September 2022.
source: France is running evaluation trials, while Indonesia and Nigeria have expressed interest.

prompt: In January 2026, the environment ministry notified rules creating a statutory Environmental Protection Fund that pools penalties imposed under certain laws. Consider the following pairs of those laws and their years:
items: Environment Protection Act — 1986
Air Act — 1981
Water Act — 1974
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The fund collects penalties under the Environment Protection Act (1986), the Air Act (1981) and the Water Act (1974), so all three pairs are correct. It recycles these penalties into cleanup and compliance.
source: The fund will collect penalties imposed under the Environment Protection Act (1986), Air Act (1981), and Water Act (1974).

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Environmental Protection Fund notified by India's environment ministry in January 2026:
items: The Centre retains 75% of the penalties collected.
States and Union Territories must set up Project Management Units, with periodic audits mandated.
Eligible spending spans 11 categories, including remediation of environmental damage.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first statement is wrong. 75% of penalties go to the state where the violation occurred, and the Centre keeps 25%. TBB notes that penalty proceeds previously often sat idle, with no common rules on sharing, reporting or oversight.
source: Of every rupee collected, 75% will be remitted to the state where the violation occurred.

prompt: Consider the following statements about a proposal made by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in January 2026:
items: It seeks to link BRICS members' central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to ease cross-border trade and tourism payments.
The RBI recommended that it be placed on the agenda of the 2026 BRICS Summit, which Brazil will host.
The RBI favours private stablecoins over CBDCs because stablecoins strengthen capital controls.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 2 and 3 are wrong: India, not Brazil, will host the 2026 BRICS Summit, and the RBI prefers CBDCs to private stablecoins, citing risks of de-facto dollarisation and weakened capital controls. The idea flows from the 2025 BRICS declaration in Rio de Janeiro, which called for greater interoperability between member countries' payment systems.
source: It has recommended that the government place the proposal on the agenda for the 2026 BRICS Summit, which India will host later this year.

prompt: In January 2026, the Uttar Pradesh government signed a Memorandum of Understanding with AM Group on the sidelines of Davos to build an AI compute hub. Consider the following statements about the proposed hub:
items: It is to be built in Greater Noida.
It aims to reach 1 gigawatt of compute capacity by 2028.
It is designed to run on carbon-free power blending solar, wind and pumped storage.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The second statement is wrong. Phase One is slated for 2028, and the 1 gigawatt compute target is set for 2030. The roughly USD 25 billion staged project is meant to cut India's dependence on offshore compute capacity.
source: By 2030, the facility aims to hit 1 gigawatt of compute capacity, positioning it among India’s largest digital infrastructure bets.

prompt: In January 2026, Stage IV of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) was invoked and then revoked in Delhi-NCR. Which body triggers these pollution restrictions across Delhi and neighbouring cities?
explain: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) is the federal panel that triggers GRAP restrictions across Delhi and neighbouring cities. It turned on Stage IV on 17 January 2026 and switched it off three days later as AQI improved to 378.
source: a federal panel that triggers pollution restrictions across Delhi and neighbouring cities

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi-NCR in January 2026:
items: Stage IV was invoked on 17 January 2026 and revoked three days later.
Since November 2025, several GRAP measures have been moved into earlier stages.
With the revocation of Stage IV, Stage III restrictions on older vehicles were also lifted.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. Easing covered only Stage IV add-ons such as truck-entry curbs and hybrid schooling for senior students, while Stage III limits, including those on older vehicles, still apply. The November 2025 tightening means Stages I to III now carry heavier curbs than before.
source: Stage III limits still apply, including restrictions on older vehicles

prompt: In January 2026, GoodEnough Energy announced the commissioning of a 7 GWh battery storage system, which it claimed was India's largest. In which state is it located?
explain: GoodEnough Energy commissioned the 7 GWh system in Uttar Pradesh. The story presents it as a sign that batteries are moving from a niche add-on to the backbone of the grid, as renewables struggle to meet peak-hour demand.
source: A day later, GoodEnough Energy announced that it had commissioned a 7 GWh battery storage system in Uttar Pradesh, claiming it to be India’s largest.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–European Union trade relations, as of January 2026:
items: Negotiations on an EU-India free trade agreement first began in 2007 and restarted in June 2022 after collapsing.
The EU is India's largest trading partner, with goods trade of about USD 130 billion in 2024.
India ranks ninth among the EU's trading partners.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: talks began in 2007 and restarted in June 2022, the EU is India's largest trading partner at USD 130 billion in goods in 2024, and India ranks ninth for the EU. The proposed agreement would link a market of nearly 2 billion people covering roughly a quarter of global GDP.
source: The EU is India’s largest trading partner (USD 130 billion in goods in 2024). India ranks ninth for the EU.

prompt: Who were the chief guests at India's Republic Day parade on 26 January 2026?
options: The Presidents of the European Commission and the European Council
The President of France and the Chancellor of Germany
The President of the European Parliament and the EU foreign policy chief
The UN Secretary-General and the WTO Director-General
explain: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa were the chief guests. Their visit was timed ahead of the 27 January EU-India summit, where the free trade agreement was expected to be signed.
source: She and European Council President Antonio Costa will also attend India’s Republic Day (January 26) parade as chief guests.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Bangladesh developments in January 2026:
items: India designated Bangladesh a "non-family posting" and decided to withdraw the families and dependents of its officials there ahead of Dhaka's general elections.
The Bangladesh general elections will be the first since the ouster of Sheikh Hasina's government in July 2024.
The ICC rejected Bangladesh's request to move its 2026 Men's T20 World Cup matches away from India.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: India declared Bangladesh a non-family posting ahead of polls that are the first since Sheikh Hasina's ouster in July 2024, and the ICC rejected Bangladesh's request to shift its T20 World Cup matches away from India. The non-family posting status is rare in the Indian Foreign Service and is applied where security concerns make it unsafe for dependents to stay.
source: The ICC rejected Bangladesh’s request to move its 2026 Men’s T20 World Cup matches away from India, citing risks to teams and staff.

prompt: As of January 2026, former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, sheltered in India since her ouster, had been convicted in absentia of which of the following?
explain: Hasina was convicted in absentia of crimes against humanity after her government fell in 2024 following widespread protests. India's decision to shelter her has angered many Bangladeshis and strained bilateral ties.
source: who was later convicted in absentia of crimes against humanity by the interim government

prompt: In November 2025, the Supreme Court defined an Aravalli hill as any landform rising above the surrounding terrain by more than:
explain: The court's November 20, 2025 ruling set the threshold at more than 100 metres above surrounding terrain. Environmental groups warned that this definition was so narrow it could exclude large parts of the range from protection.
source: The move follows the court’s own November 20 ruling that defined an Aravalli hill as any landform rising more than 100 metres above surrounding terrain.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's handling of the Aravalli range between November 2025 and January 2026:
items: On December 29, 2025, the court stayed its own November 2025 judgment defining an Aravalli hill.
The high-powered panel the court will constitute is to be made up of officials nominated by the Aravalli states.
The panel is tasked with defining the Aravalli range and laying down what activities are permitted there.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the court said the panel will consist of independent experts, not state nominees. The court also directed states to stop unauthorised activity in the region after staying its earlier ruling following protests from conservationists.
source: said it will constitute a high-powered panel of independent experts to formally define the Aravalli range and lay down what activities are permitted.

prompt: The Aravalli range, described as the "green lungs" of northwestern India, runs south of Delhi into which state?
explain: The Aravallis run south of Delhi into Gujarat. They slow desertification and support groundwater recharge, but they also sit atop mineral-rich land, which makes them commercially contested.
source: The Aravallis, running south of Delhi into Gujarat, are often described as the “green lungs” of northwestern India.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the draft Disturbed Areas Bill approved in Rajasthan in January 2026:
items: In localities notified as disturbed, buying or selling property may require prior clearance from the district administration.
In January 2026, the Bill was passed by the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly.
The draft contemplates imprisonment of 3 to 5 years plus fines for violations.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. On 21 January 2026 the Rajasthan cabinet only approved a draft, which had yet to go before the Assembly. Under the draft, property deals done without approval in disturbed areas could be cancelled, and the state cites demographic imbalance and distress sales as its justification.
source: In those pockets, selling or buying property may require prior clearance from the district administration.

prompt: IndiGo's flight operations were disrupted in December 2025. Consider the following statements about the regulatory action that followed, as reported in January 2026:
items: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) levied a record penalty of INR 22.2 crore on IndiGo.
The DGCA demanded a bank guarantee of INR 100 crore from the airline.
IndiGo accounts for more than 80% of India's domestic air traffic.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The DGCA demanded a bank guarantee of INR 50 crore, not INR 100 crore, and IndiGo carries roughly 60-65% of domestic traffic, not over 80%. The Centre also told the Delhi High Court it had asked the airline to dismiss a senior vice-president from its operations control centre.
source: DGCA has already levied a record INR 22.2 crore (~USD 2.4 million) penalty and demanded a INR 50 crore (~USD 5.5 million) bank guarantee.

prompt: In January 2026, it was announced that Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's state visit to New Delhi in February 2026 would include the inauguration of an office of APEX. What is APEX?
options: Brazil's trade and investment promotion agency
explain: APEX is the Brazilian Trade and Investment Promotion Agency, and its New Delhi office was scheduled to open during Lula's 19-21 February 2026 visit, which also included the Brazil-India Business Forum. India and Brazil are aligning more closely inside groupings like BRICS and the G20.
source: The visit will also see the inauguration of Brazil’s APEX (Brazilian Trade and Investment Promotion Agency) office in New Delhi.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–EU Security and Defence Partnership (SDP) announced in January 2026:
items: It covers maritime security, cybersecurity and counterterrorism.
It was to be signed during a Delhi visit by the European Commission President and the European Council President.
It was to be signed at the 15th India–EU Summit held in Brussels.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. The pact was to be signed in New Delhi, where Ursula von der Leyen and Antonio Costa would co-chair the 16th India–EU Summit with Narendra Modi and attend Republic Day celebrations.
source: Brussels announced a new Security and Defense Partnership (SDP) with New Delhi, covering maritime security, cybersecurity, and counterterrorism.

prompt: The European Union's Security Action For Europe (SAFE) programme, discussed in January 2026 in the context of India–EU defence industrial cooperation, is best described as:
options: An EU financing tool for defence readiness
An EU naval mission for maritime surveillance
An EU network for cyber-incident response
An EU database for counterterrorism intelligence
explain: SAFE is a EUR 150 billion financing tool meant to speed up European defence readiness. The new India–EU defence partnership could let Indian firms tap into Europe's defence supply chains as the EU rearms.
source: including Indian firms accessing the EU’s Security Action For Europe (SAFE) programme, a EUR 150 billion financing tool to accelerate European defence readiness.

prompt: In January 2026, the Supreme Court denied tax treaty protection to Mauritius-based entities in the Tiger Global case. Which provisions of Indian tax law did the Court hold can override treaty benefits where a structure appears designed mainly to avoid tax?
explain: The Court held that India's general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) can override treaty benefits when a structure looks designed mainly to dodge tax. Startups fear this could see old investment structures reopened.
source: The Court said India’s general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) can override treaty benefits if a structure looks designed mainly to dodge tax, raising fears that old startup cap tables get reopened.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's January 2026 ruling in the Tiger Global case and the India–Mauritius tax relationship:
items: The Court held that Mauritius-based entities used by Tiger Global in its 2018 sale of a Flipkart stake to Walmart were conduits.
The India–Mauritius tax treaty dates from 1982.
Government data cited by Reuters showed Mauritius accounted for USD 171 billion of inflows over 23 years to 2023.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. On 15 January 2026, the Court ruled that the entities were conduits, which denied them treaty protection and allowed India to tax the gains. For two decades, Mauritius was the standard holding-company route for investing in India.
source: On 15 January 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that Mauritius-based entities used by Tiger Global in its 2018 Flipkart stake sale to Walmart were “conduits,” denying them treaty protection and allowing India to tax the gains.

prompt: With reference to the Nipah virus, which caused an outbreak in India in January 2026, consider the following statements:
items: There is no vaccine or cure for the disease it causes.
It is typically linked to spillover from bats through contaminated fruit.
Human-to-human transmission is its most common mode of spread.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because human transmission of Nipah is rare. The virus usually reaches people through bat spillovers via contaminated fruit. It has no vaccine or cure and sits on the WHO's high-risk list, with fatality rates of 40-75%.
source: Human transmission is rare, and the virus is typically linked to bat spillovers via contaminated fruit.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Nipah virus outbreaks in India:
items: In January 2026, India moved to contain a Nipah outbreak in West Bengal, with confirmed cases including doctors and nurses.
Kerala has reported Nipah repeatedly since 2018.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct. The January 2026 West Bengal outbreak had five confirmed cases, among them infected health workers. Nipah had surfaced in West Bengal before in 2001 and 2007, and India now has protocols for tracing, isolation and hospital control.
source: Nipah has surfaced before in West Bengal in 2001 and 2007, and repeatedly in Kerala since 2018.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, as of January 2026:
items: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar said the SIR will be extended to the remaining states.
The SIR had been conducted in 13 of India's 36 states and union territories.
The Election Commission described the SIR as a one-time exercise limited to poll-bound states.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. The Commission says the SIR is now firmly part of its nationwide approach to roll maintenance. Opposition parties and civil society groups have raised concerns over deletions and the risk of eligible voters being left out, especially in migrant-heavy constituencies.
source: The SIR has been conducted in 13 of India’s 36 states and union territories so far.

prompt: The foundation day of the Election Commission of India is observed as which of the following?
explain: The Election Commission's foundation day is observed as National Voters' Day. Speaking ahead of it in January 2026, CEC Gyanesh Kumar said the SIR had helped restore the sanctity and credibility of the voter list.
source: Speaking ahead of the Election Commission’s foundation day – observed as National Voters’ Day

prompt: In January 2026, bank unions gave notice of a nationwide strike to demand a five-day work week. Consider the following statements:
items: Since 2015, all Saturdays have been holidays for banks in India.
The United Forum of Bank Unions is a coalition of nine bank staff unions.
The Indian Banks' Association negotiates on behalf of banks in wage settlements.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. In 2015 banks moved to the 2nd and 4th Saturdays off, and the unions are still seeking all Saturdays off. They say the IBA agreed to this in a March 2024 wage settlement, but government sign-off is pending.
source: In 2015, banks shifted to 2nd and 4th Saturdays off.

prompt: In January 2026, the Drugs Controller General of India cleared Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy's and Alkem Laboratories to manufacture a generic version of which drug, the active ingredient in Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy?
explain: Semaglutide is the active ingredient in both Ozempic and Wegovy. Indian firms are moving early so they are ready when Novo Nordisk's Indian patent on Ozempic expires in March 2026.
source: Semaglutide is the active ingredient in Novo Nordisk’s Ozempic and Wegovy.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the semaglutide drugs in the news in January 2026:
items: Novo Nordisk's Indian patent on Ozempic expires in September 2026.
Ozempic and Wegovy contain different active ingredients, one approved for diabetes and the other for weight management.
India accounts for roughly one in ten diabetics globally.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the Indian patent on Ozempic expires in March, not September; both drugs contain semaglutide and differ only in dosage, delivery and approved indications; and India accounts for roughly one in five diabetics globally, not one in ten. Nomura expects generic semaglutide to cost around INR 3,600, less than half the current price of Ozempic in India.
source: Novo Nordisk’s Indian patent on Ozempic expires in March, and Indian firms are moving early to be ready on day one.

prompt: In January 2026, former IMF chief economist Gita Gopinath spoke about pollution at a Davos panel on India's growth. Consider the following statements about her remarks:
items: She said the economic damage from tariffs already outweighs that from pollution.
She cited a 2022 World Bank study estimating nearly 1.7 million pollution-linked deaths a year in India, about 18% of all deaths.
A 2021 study cited in the discussion estimated that air pollution costs Indian businesses about USD 95 billion annually, around 3% of GDP.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Gopinath said the reverse: pollution's economic damage already outweighs the impact of tariffs. The other two figures are as reported, and she called for treating pollution control as a national mission on par with deregulation.
source: Speaking at a panel on India’s growth trajectory, the former IMF chief economist said pollution’s economic damage already outweighs the impact of tariffs.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Canada relations, as reported in January 2026:
items: Ties froze in 2023 after then-PM Justin Trudeau alleged Indian involvement in the killing of Sikh separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar.
Narendra Modi attended the 2025 G7 summit held in Canada.
Mark Carney took office as Prime Minister of Canada in March 2024.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Carney took office in March 2025, not March 2024, and has pursued normalisation with India since then. India denies the Nijjar allegation, and Canadian ministers have visited New Delhi often since the 2025 G7.
source: Since taking office in March 2025, Carney has focused on normalisation, not closure.

prompt: In January 2026, India and Canada said formal negotiations on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) would restart in March after a two-year pause. Both governments say the pact could help more than double bilateral trade to what level by 2030?
explain: Both governments say CEPA could help bilateral trade reach USD 30 billion by 2030. The restart of talks was announced by Indian High Commissioner to Canada Dinesh Patnaik.
source: Both governments say the pact could help more than double bilateral trade to USD 30 billion by 2030.

prompt: In August 2025, the United States doubled tariffs on Indian goods to 50%. The additional 25% tariff was imposed over which of the following?
options: India's imports of Russian crude oil
India's levy of a digital services tax
India's high duties on US motorcycles
India's restrictions on US dairy imports
explain: The extra 25% tariff was tied to India's purchases of Russian crude, taking the total to 50%. In January 2026, a leaked recording had Senator Ted Cruz saying he was battling the White House to accept a trade deal with India.
source: In August 2025, Trump doubled tariffs on Indian goods to 50%, adding a 25% tariff over India’s Russian crude imports.

prompt: In January 2026, India and the European Union reached political consensus on a Free Trade Agreement. Consider the following statements about it:
items: India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on 96.6% of EU goods exports by value.
The EU will cut tariffs on 99.5% of imports from India over seven years.
Agricultural products and food are carved out of the deal.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The EU estimates India's cuts will save European firms about EUR 4 billion a year in duties, while its own cuts favour labour-heavy Indian exports such as textiles, leather and gems. The agriculture carve-out was meant to avoid the farmer backlash that stalled the EU's Mercosur pact.
source: The EU will cut tariffs on 99.5% of imports from India over 7 years, a clear boost for textiles, leather, chemicals, gems/jewellery, and other labour-heavy items.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the automobile provisions of the India–EU Free Trade Agreement, as reported in January 2026:
items: Tariffs on around 160,000 European internal combustion engine vehicles will fall to 10% within five years.
Tariff relief on the 90,000 European electric vehicles in the quota will come within five years.
Duties on auto components will fall to zero.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because EVs get delayed relief, with tariffs dropping only by year ten. The delay is meant to shield India's young EV market, while zero duty on components encourages European manufacturers to plug into India's parts ecosystem.
source: 90,000 EVs get delayed relief; tariffs only drop by year ten, shielding India’s young electric vehicle (EV) market.

prompt: Under the India–EU Free Trade Agreement, as reported in January 2026, reviews of the quota for European cars are tied to which sector, a core Indian priority?
explain: Quota reviews are linked to steel, which gives New Delhi a built-in pressure point in future negotiations. TBB argues this lets India open the door to European cars without surrendering control.
source: Quota reviews are tied to steel, a core Indian priority.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to European car imports under the India–EU Free Trade Agreement, as reported in January 2026:
items: Total European-made cars entering India at lower duties — up to 250,000
Annual quota of completely knocked down (CKD) kits — 75,000
Tariff on eligible CKD kits under the deal — 8.25%
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correct. Up to 250,000 cars get lower duties, and 75,000 CKD kits priced above USD 18,000 can be shipped each year at 8.25%, down from the existing 16.5%.
source: European carmakers can ship 75,000 completely knocked down (CKD) kits a year, priced above USD 18,000, with tariffs cut to 8.25% from the existing 16.5%.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Joint India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda endorsed in January 2026:
items: It identifies AI, quantum computing and semiconductors among the focus areas of technology cooperation.
It provides for institutional cooperation through biennial India-EU summits.
It seeks to streamline skills mobility and visa procedures between the partners.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the agenda provides for annual summits, not biennial ones, along with business and academic exchange platforms. The framework was endorsed on 27 January 2026 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and EU leadership and also covers green energy, defence and critical minerals.
source: the partners will streamline skills mobility and visa procedures while strengthening institutional cooperation through annual summits and dedicated business and academic exchange platforms.

prompt: In January 2026, the Joint India-EU Comprehensive Strategic Agenda prioritised strengthening connectivity through which corridor?
explain: The agenda names the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) as its connectivity priority. It also calls for coordinated leadership in multilateral forums on climate, health and trade governance.
source: The agenda prioritizes strengthening connectivity through the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor corridor and coordinated leadership in multilateral forums to drive global reforms in climate, health, and trade governance.

prompt: In January 2026, the Adani Group signed a Memorandum of Understanding with which aircraft manufacturer to explore a regional aircraft manufacturing venture in India?
explain: Adani signed the MoU with Brazil's Embraer to explore building regional aircraft in India, which pushes the group into commercial aviation production. The announcement came as President Lula was set to travel to India for the Brazil-India Business Forum.
source: India’s Adani Group and Brazil’s Embraer signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to explore a regional aircraft manufacturing venture in India

prompt: Consider the following statements in the context of the Adani–Embraer regional aircraft MoU of January 2026:
items: The Embraer jets in focus seat 70–140 passengers and are built for thin routes.
Navi Mumbai International, being built by the Adani Group, is India's largest greenfield airport.
The UDAN scheme subsidises wide-body aircraft operations on high-density trunk routes.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. UDAN subsidises regional connectivity to smaller cities, where wide-bodies make no sense and turboprops are hitting capacity limits. Embraer's 70–140 seat jets suit these routes, while IndiGo and Air India have ordered Airbus and Boeing planes for trunk routes.
source: That aligns with India’s regional connectivity scheme (UDAN), which subsidises regional connectivity to smaller cities where wide-bodies make no sense and turboprops are hitting capacity limits.

prompt: The Economic Survey 2025-26, released in January 2026, cited for the first time a Power Gap Index on which India scored -4.0, the lowest in Asia excluding Russia and North Korea. Which think tank publishes this index?
explain: The Survey cited the Power Gap Index of the Australia-based Lowy Institute. A score of -4.0 indicates that India operates below its strategic potential.
source: For the first time, the Survey cites Australia-based Lowy Institute’s Power Gap Index, noting that India operates below its strategic potential with a score of -4.0 – the lowest in Asia (excluding Russia and North Korea).

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26, released in January 2026:
items: It puts India's real GDP growth estimate for FY26 at 7.4%.
It notes that the fiscal deficit came in at 4.8%, better than the 4.9% budgeted.
It notes that India received three sovereign rating downgrades.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the Survey records three sovereign rating upgrades, not downgrades. Its central paradox is that the rupee weakened despite this strong domestic performance.
source: Fiscal consolidation outperformed (4.8% deficit vs 4.9% budgeted), and three sovereign rating upgrades followed.

prompt: The Economic Survey 2025-26 discussed the impact of US tariffs on India in 2025. Consider the following statements:
items: An additional 25% tariff imposed in August 2025 was added on top of a 25% reciprocal duty applied from April 2025.
Later India-US negotiations led to a reduction in these tariffs.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the later negotiations did not result in a reduction. The hope that India would win a quick exemption from the new US tariff regime did not materialise.
source: Instead of securing quick exemption, India was slapped with an additional 25% tariff in August – piling onto the 25% reciprocal duty from April.

prompt: According to the Economic Survey released in January 2026, the global economy is shifting from efficiency-driven multilateralism towards which of the following?
explain: The Survey says the world is moving to economic statecraft, where economic means are used to achieve political ends. It expects less trust, more shocks and thinner margins in this new order.
source: The global economy is shifting from efficiency-driven multilateralism to economic statecraft, economic means are used to achieve political ends.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the global scenarios and prescriptions in India's Economic Survey released in January 2026:
items: It assigns a 40–45% probability each to 'managed disorder' and 'disorderly multipolar breakdown'.
It describes a 'systemic shock cascade' as a financial rupture that would be milder than the 2008 crisis.
It recommends moving from import substitution to indispensability.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the Survey gives the systemic shock cascade a 10–20% probability and says it would be worse than 2008, driven by AI-infrastructure excess meeting a geopolitical shock. Its prescription also includes earning hard currency and diversifying trade and payments.
source: A financial rupture. Think AI-infrastructure excess meets geopolitical shock; worse than 2008.

prompt: Which approach to regulating artificial intelligence did the Economic Survey presented in January 2026 recommend for India?
options: Build ecosystems and regulatory capacity first, then impose binding rules
Impose binding rules first, then build ecosystems and regulatory capacity
Rely only on voluntary industry self-regulation, with no binding rules
Enact one comprehensive AI law immediately, before any ecosystem building
explain: The Survey backs sequenced regulation, with binding rules to come once risks are clear and enforceable. This fits its wider aim of reducing fragile dependence on foreign compute, capital and supply chains.
source: build ecosystems and regulatory capacity first, then impose binding rules once risks are clear and enforceable.

prompt: According to the Economic Survey released in January 2026, India's top 10 cities generate roughly what share of the country's GDP?
explain: The Survey says the top 10 cities generate nearly 28% of GDP while housing barely 9% of the population. It adds that none of them yet functions as a true global node like Singapore or London.
source: India’s top 10 cities generate nearly 28% of GDP with barely 9% of the population

prompt: Which of the following did the Economic Survey released in January 2026 identify as the single biggest bottleneck for Indian cities?
explain: The Survey names restrictive land use as the single biggest urban bottleneck, because existing rules keep cities short and wide. It says Indian cities have the talent, but the physical environment caps growth, so it calls for building up, not out.
source: Restrictive land use is the single biggest urban bottleneck.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the urban plan proposed in the Economic Survey released in January 2026:
items: It recommends that all million-plus cities adopt a 30-year statutory spatial-economic plan.
It proposes that such a plan be refreshed every five years.
Land-value capture is one of the plan's three non-negotiables.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the Survey recommends a 20-year statutory spatial-economic plan, not a 30-year one. The other two non-negotiables are transport-first design and annual housing targets, and land-value capture is meant to stop public infrastructure projects from creating private windfalls.
source: All million-plus cities should adopt a 20-year statutory spatial-economic plan, refreshed every five years, with three non-negotiables: transport-first design, annual housing targets, and land-value capture so public infrastructure projects don't create private windfalls while city budgets stay stressed.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey presented in January 2026 and its treatment of ultra-processed foods (UPFs):
items: It suggested moving UPFs to the highest GST slab along with a surcharge.
It proposed replacing front-of-pack warning labels with star-based health ratings.
It noted that obesity has doubled alongside a 150% jump in UPF consumption over 15 years.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The Survey proposed the reverse, replacing vague ratings with clear front-of-pack warning labels. Its toolkit also included banning UPF marketing during daytime and evening hours across media.
source: The Survey notes that obesity has doubled alongside a 150% jump in UPF consumption over 15 years and significantly increasing healthcare costs and decreasing productivity.

prompt: The Economic Survey presented in January 2026 flagged compulsive digital use as a productivity threat. Consider the following statements about its suggestions:
items: It floated age-based access limits for social media and gambling apps.
It suggested basic phones for children to curb early addiction.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both suggestions appear in the Survey, along with a proposed digital wellness curriculum in schools. It linked digital over-consumption to anxiety and sleep deprivation and warned that this could blunt India's demographic dividend.
source: It floats age-based access limits for social media and gambling apps, proposes a “digital wellness curriculum” in schools, and even suggests basic phones for children to curb early addiction.

prompt: In February 2026, US President Trump announced that the tariff on Indian goods would be cut from 50% to which rate?
explain: Trump announced the cut from 50% to 18% after a phone call with Prime Minister Modi on 2 February 2026. In return, India reportedly agreed to buy more US goods and stop buying Russian crude.
source: On Monday, US President Trump announced that tariffs on Indian goods would be cut from a staggering 50% to 18% after Prime Minister Modi reportedly agreed to buy a lot of stuff from the US and stop buying Russian crude.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the US tariff cut on Indian goods announced in February 2026:
items: The cut involves Washington rescinding a 25% punitive duty on Indian goods.
At the time of the announcement, the White House had issued the Federal Register notice needed to make the new rates binding.
New Delhi explicitly confirmed a timeline for ending its purchases of Russian oil.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only statement 1 is correct. The White House had not yet issued the presidential proclamation or Federal Register notice needed to make the deal binding. New Delhi had not explicitly confirmed the Russian exit timeline, and Indian refiners warned that winding down existing contracts would take months.
source: In exchange, Washington is rescinding a 25% punitive duty and lowering its “reciprocal” tariff from 25% to 18%.

prompt: In February 2026, reports said India was in talks with Ant International to link UPI with Alipay+ for overseas use. Consider the following statements about the context of these talks:
items: UPI has already been taken abroad through bilateral corridors with countries including Singapore and the United Arab Emirates.
Under the corridor model, the National Payments Corporation of India ties up with local payment networks and regulators market by market.
Alibaba's consumer apps, including Alipay, have been banned in India since 2023.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because Alibaba's consumer apps, including Alipay, have been banned in India since 2020, not 2023. Linking UPI to Alipay+ would shift its expansion from slow bilateral corridors to a single platform integration spanning multiple countries.
source: UPI has already been taken abroad through bilateral corridors with countries like Singapore and the United Arab Emirates.

prompt: In February 2026, the Centre told which court that it would finalise the remaining rules to operationalise parts of the Industrial Relations Code by end-February 2026?
explain: The Centre gave the undertaking to the Delhi High Court. Petitioners there argued the Code was in force but lacked rules on how labour courts or industrial tribunals operate and how members are appointed.
source: On Monday, the Centre told the Delhi High Court it will finalise the remaining rules to operationalise parts of the Industrial Relations Code by end-February, after petitioners warned the system was running without an instruction book.

prompt: In February 2026, the US Trade Representative described the India–US trade deal terms. Which of the following was among the US products on which India will eliminate duties?
explain: India will eliminate duties on US tree nuts, fruits, vegetables, wine and spirits. The USTR said nothing about rice, beef, soybeans, sugar and dairy, which were also excluded from India's deal with the EU.
source: India will eliminate duties on US tree nuts, fruits, vegetables, wine, and spirits.

prompt: In February 2026, Adani Defence & Aerospace signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Italy's Leonardo to establish an integrated helicopter manufacturing ecosystem in India. Consider the following statements:
items: The partnership centres on Leonardo's AW169M and AW109 TrekkerM platforms.
The initial focus of the partnership is civil aviation, with military demand to be addressed later.
Adani Defence's CEO said the Indian Armed Forces project a need for more than 1,000 helicopters over the next 10 years.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the initial focus is military demand, with possible spillover into civil aviation later. The plan goes beyond assembly to include phased indigenisation, local manufacturing, MRO and pilot training, and India has fewer than 250 helicopters for 1.4 billion people.
source: The partnership centres on Leonardo’s AW169M and AW109 TrekkerM platforms.

prompt: In February 2026, who was sworn in as Chief Minister of Manipur, ending a year of President's Rule in the state?
explain: Yumnam Khemchand Singh, a Meitei veteran pitched as a bridge-builder, took office on 4 February 2026. N. Biren Singh is the former Chief Minister who resigned, while Nemcha Kipgen and Losii Dikho became Deputy Chief Ministers.
source: Yesterday, Yumnam Khemchand Singh was sworn in as Chief Minister, ending direct administration from New Delhi.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Manipur government sworn in in February 2026:
items: It has two Deputy Chief Ministers, one from the Kuki-Zo community and one from the Naga community.
Nemcha Kipgen is the first Kuki woman to serve as Deputy Chief Minister.
The Chief Minister's 100-day roadmap includes reviving CM da Haisi, a citizen grievance platform.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct: Nemcha Kipgen (Kuki-Zo) and Losii Dikho (Naga) are the two Deputy Chief Ministers, and CM da Haisi means "Let's tell the CM". The roadmap also covers resettlement of displaced persons and power-sharing after ethnic violence that began in May 2023.
source: His 100-day roadmap includes the resettlement of displaced persons, active power-sharing, and reviving the citizen grievance platform, CM da Haisi (“Let’s tell the CM”).

prompt: In early 2026, the Election Commission of India drew criticism for postponing its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls in one poll-bound state while going ahead in others. In which state was the exercise postponed?
explain: The ECI postponed the SIR in BJP-ruled Assam but went ahead in opposition-held West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, plus Puducherry. The SIR was initially slated for the states heading to the polls in 2026.
source: However, eyebrows were raised when the ECI postponed the exercise in BJP-ruled Assam while going forward in opposition-held West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala (plus Puducherry where the BJP is in an alliance with the government).

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls, as of February 2026:
items: Unlike annual reviews, an intensive revision requires every voter to be re-verified.
West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee challenged the SIR by personally arguing before the Supreme Court.
Phase 2 of the SIR includes Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. An intensive revision re-verifies every voter, Mamata Banerjee personally argued in the Supreme Court on 4 February 2026 to halt the SIR, and Phase 2 now covers BJP strongholds such as UP and Gujarat. Banerjee alleged the ECI was rushing to do in two months what takes two years, using trivial errors to disenfranchise legitimate voters.
source: West Bengal Chief Minister (CM) Mamata Banerjee personally argued in the Supreme Court on Wednesday to halt the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls, claiming the SIR targets her state ahead of the 2026 elections.

prompt: In February 2026, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the first tranche of the India-US trade deal was almost ready. Consider the following statements about implementing the deal:
items: The US can cut its tariffs through an executive order without waiting for the formal signing.
India must wait for the formal signing of the deal before it can lower its Most-Favoured Nation (MFN) rates.
MFN rates are the standard rates India applies to countries with which it has no preferential trade agreement.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the US can cut tariffs immediately by executive order, while India must wait for the formal signing to lower its MFN rates, which are the standard rates for countries without a preferential trade agreement with India. Goyal expected the deal to be signed by mid-March 2026, and India also needs Cabinet approval and possibly legislative changes to apply preferential rates.
source: India, however, must wait for the formal signing to lower its Most-Favoured Nation (MFN) rates, which are standard rates applied to countries that India doesn’t have a preferential trade agreement with.

prompt: In February 2026, the Competition Commission of India (CCI) ordered a formal investigation into IndiGo after the airline's flight cancellations in December 2025. Consider the following statements:
items: The CCI suspects IndiGo used its 60% market share to withhold capacity, creating artificial scarcity and fare spikes.
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) had earlier fined IndiGo USD 2.45 million for roster failures.
The CCI rejected IndiGo's argument that the DGCA's ongoing action barred a competition investigation, holding that sector-specific rules do not grant immunity from competition law.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the CCI suspects IndiGo of withholding capacity using its 60% share, the DGCA had already fined it USD 2.45 million, and the CCI dismissed IndiGo's plea that DGCA action shielded it from competition law. IndiGo had cancelled over 4,500 flights in early December 2025, stranding tens of thousands of passengers.
source: The CCI dismissed this, asserting that sector-specific rules do not grant immunity from competition law.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Bharat Taxi, launched in February 2026:
items: It was launched by the Union Minister of Cooperation.
It is a surge-free platform on which drivers receive the full fare.
Before launch, it ran a pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. Amit Shah, Union Home and Cooperation Minister, launched Bharat Taxi on 5 February 2026 after a two-month pilot in Delhi-NCR and Gujarat, as a zero-commission, surge-free platform where drivers receive the full fare. Any surplus is routed back to members, and drivers also get health insurance, accident cover and retirement savings.
source: A zero-commission, surge-free platform where drivers receive the full fare and any surplus is routed back to members.

prompt: The Bharat Taxi ride-hailing platform, launched in India in February 2026, is structured as which of the following?
explain: Bharat Taxi makes drivers members rather than users. Fees fund operations and welfare, and the surplus flows back to drivers. This sets it apart from investor-owned aggregators like Uber and Ola and from SaaS marketplaces like Rapido, where drivers pay for access but do not share in profits.
source: Cooperative models like Bharat Taxi make drivers members, not users.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the US-India joint statement on a framework for an Interim Trade Agreement, released in February 2026:
items: The United States applies a reciprocal 18% tariff on Indian goods, with its removal conditional on the interim pact being concluded.
India takes on a binding obligation to purchase USD 500 billion of US goods over five years.
India commits to eliminating or reducing tariffs on all US industrial goods.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The USD 500 billion purchase over five years, covering energy, aircraft, GPUs and coking coal, is a signal of intent, not an obligation. The framework is a bridge to the broader Bilateral Trade Agreement talks launched in February 2025.
source: India signals intent, not obligation, to purchase USD 500 billion of US goods over five years

prompt: Under the US-India framework for an Interim Trade Agreement announced in February 2026, US tariff relief for Indian pharmaceuticals was deferred until the conclusion of which of the following?
options: A Section 301 unfair trade practices investigation
A World Trade Organization dispute panel ruling
explain: The United States deferred pharmaceutical relief until a Section 232 national security investigation concludes. It did agree to lift steel, aluminium and copper tariffs on Indian aircraft and parts and to grant India a preferential tariff-rate quota for auto parts.
source: defer pharmaceutical relief until a Section 232 national security investigation concludes.

prompt: Prime Minister Modi visited Malaysia in February 2026. In August 2025, India and Malaysia had upgraded their bilateral ties to which level?
explain: The February 2026 trip was Modi's first visit to Malaysia since ties were upgraded to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership the previous August. The visit's joint statement covered local-currency trade, semiconductors and digital payments.
source: Prime Minister Modi wrapped his two-day visit to Malaysia on Sunday, his first trip there since upgrading bilateral ties to a "Comprehensive Strategic Partnership" last August.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Malaysia relations as reflected in the joint statement issued during Prime Minister Modi's visit in February 2026:
items: Bilateral trade between India and Malaysia reached USD 18.6 billion in 2025.
Both countries are pushing INR-MYR local-currency settlement, partly to cut hedging costs for small and medium enterprises.
The newly launched Malaysia-India Digital Council is tasked with cooperation across areas including cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence and fintech.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are stated in the story: trade hit USD 18.6 billion in 2025, INR-MYR settlement aims to bypass the dollar and cut SME hedging costs, and the Digital Council covers semiconductors, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, AI and fintech. The two sides also plan to link India's UPI with Malaysia's PayNet.
source: The joint statement confirmed the launch of the Malaysia-India Digital Council, a body tasked with accelerating cooperation across semiconductors, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, and fintech.

prompt: Under the semiconductor cooperation outlined in the India–Malaysia joint statement of February 2026, India's strengths in chip design are to be combined with Malaysia's experience in which segment?
explain: The joint statement pairs India's chip-design strengths with Malaysia's extensive experience in assembly, testing and packaging. TBB's analysis notes that drawing on Malaysia's know-how offers India a shortcut to a resilient domestic chip ecosystem.
source: with both sides looking to deepen trade and cooperation as they combine India’s strengths in chip design with Malaysia’s extensive experience in assembly, testing, and packaging.

prompt: In February 2026, construction began on the Amaravati Quantum Valley, described as India's first integrated campus for quantum research and manufacturing. In which state is it located?
explain: Union Minister Jitendra Singh began construction of the 50-acre campus in Andhra Pradesh on 8 February 2026. The site is backed by the National Quantum Mission and aims to cover the whole value chain, from skill development to hardware.
source: On Sunday, Union Minister Jitendra Singh kicked off construction on the 50-acre Amaravati Quantum Valley in Andhra Pradesh, the nation’s first integrated campus for quantum research and manufacturing.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's National Quantum Mission, as reported in February 2026:
items: It aims to build 1,000 physical qubits within eight years.
It targets a quantum communication network of 2,000 km.
It spans 43 institutions divided into four thematic hubs.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct: the USD 662 million mission targets 1,000 physical qubits in eight years and a 2,000-km quantum communication network, and spans 43 institutions across 19 regions in four thematic hubs. Since quantum computing could in theory break modern cryptography, India's investment is largely defensive research for secure communications.
source: The goal is ambitious: 1,000 physical qubits within eight years and a 2,000-km quantum communication network.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–US interim trade deal, as described by Indian officials in February 2026:
items: It excludes imports of staples such as rice, wheat and corn into India.
It offers Indian exporters of basmati rice, spices, coffee and tea duty-free access to the US market.
It opens the Indian market to imports of US dairy products.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Officials say dairy is excluded from the deal along with rice, wheat and corn, so the third statement is wrong. Farm unions argue that lower tariffs on items such as crude soybean oil, apples and animal feed products could still hurt domestic producers.
source: Officials say the current deal excludes imports of staples such as rice, wheat, corn and dairy, while offering duty-free access to the US market for Indian exporters of basmati rice, fruits, spices, coffee and tea.

prompt: In February 2026, Indian farm unions opposing the India–US interim trade deal singled out imports of distillers dried grains as a threat to the prices of which crops?
explain: Unions warned that distillers dried grain imports, an animal feed product, could depress maize and oilseed prices. Farm leaders argue Indian growers cannot compete with larger, heavily subsidised US producers.
source: with distillers dried grain imports in particular seen as a threat to maize and oilseed prices

prompt: Under the Supreme Court's February 2026 order on West Bengal's Special Intensive Revision, who holds the final decision on deleting voters from the rolls?
explain: The Court ruled that micro-observers may assist but cannot adjudicate, so final decisions on deletions stay with Electoral Registration Officers. This addressed Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's fear of shadow decision-making by outside observers.
source: Final decisions on voter deletions stay with Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), addressing Banerjee’s fear of shadow decision-making by outside observers.

prompt: In February 2026, India's Ministry of External Affairs announced a three-day visit by French President Emmanuel Macron. Consider the following statements:
items: The India–France strategic partnership dates back to 1998.
Macron was scheduled to arrive in Mumbai to launch the India-France Year of Innovation.
The AI Impact Summit was scheduled to be held in New Delhi on 19 February 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the partnership dates back to 1998, and Macron was to arrive in Mumbai to launch the India-France Year of Innovation before heading to New Delhi for the AI Impact Summit on 19 February. France stayed a consistent partner even when India faced international sanctions, and the relationship rests on strategic autonomy.
source: Macron will arrive in Mumbai to launch the India-France Year of Innovation before heading to New Delhi for the AI Impact Summit on February 19

prompt: "Horizon 2047", a 25-year roadmap covering defence co-production, AI governance and maritime security in the Indo-Pacific, guides India's partnership with which country?
explain: Horizon 2047 is designed to align Paris and New Delhi on defence co-production, AI governance and Indo-Pacific maritime security. Macron's February 2026 visit to India was built on it, as ties shift from buyer–seller defence deals towards jointly shaping rules, standards and R&D.
source: The visit leans on "Horizon 2047", a 25-year roadmap designed to align Paris and New Delhi on defence co-production, AI governance, and maritime security in the Indo-Pacific.

prompt: In February 2026, India and Greece set in motion a plan for defence industrial cooperation. What is the duration of this plan?
explain: The defence ministers' meeting in New Delhi put a five-year plan for industrial cooperation in play. TBB reads the deepening ties with Greece, Turkey's main rival, as a counter-alignment as Turkey eyes a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.
source: A five-year plan for industrial cooperation is now in play, alongside a 2026 Military Cooperation Plan for joint exercises.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's policy push on critical minerals and rare-earths, as reported in February 2026:
items: The USD 800mn incentive scheme approved in November 2025 targets 6,000 tonnes of permanent magnets annually within three years.
In 2023, India classified more than 20 minerals as critical to its aim of self-reliance.
The Union Budget 2026-27 announced Dedicated Rare-Earth Corridors to cluster mining, processing, R&D and manufacturing.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: the scheme targets 6,000 tonnes of permanent magnets annually within seven years, not three. The rare-earth corridors aim to shorten timelines, ease approvals and give investors predictable infrastructure.
source: In November 2025, it approved an USD 800mn incentive scheme targeting 6,000 tonnes of permanent magnets annually within seven years.

prompt: As reported in February 2026, roughly what share of India's magnets is supplied by China?
explain: China dominates rare-earth processing and supplies nearly 90% of India's magnets. Magnets are central to EVs, renewables, grid storage and defence electronics, which is why India is seeking alternative partners.
source: Today, that supply chain runs largely through China, which dominates rare-earth processing and supplies nearly 90% of India’s magnets.

prompt: In February 2026, India was reported to be in talks to jointly explore, extract, process and recycle lithium and rare-earths with which group of countries?
explain: New Delhi is talking to Brazil, Canada, France and the Netherlands. Brazil and Canada bring mining depth, while France and the Netherlands add processing technology, advanced manufacturing and long-term capital.
source: New Delhi is in talks with Brazil, Canada, France, and Netherlands to jointly explore, extract, process, and recycle lithium and rare-earths.

prompt: In February 2026, India's IT Ministry amended internet regulation to require social media platforms to remove flagged deepfakes within what time?
explain: The IT Ministry mandated removal of flagged deepfakes within three hours. The 2021 IT Rules had given platforms 36 hours to comply with takedown orders, and from 20 February 2026 that window shrinks by 90%.
source: mandating that social media platforms remove flagged deepfakes within just three hours.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the deepfake rules notified by India's IT Ministry in February 2026:
items: The law formally defines "synthetically generated information" for the first time.
The definition of synthetically generated information covers good-faith edits such as colour correction and accessibility tweaks.
Large platforms must require users to declare AI-generated content at the time of upload.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the definition carves out good-faith edits like colour correction or accessibility tweaks, covering only AI-altered audio or video that looks real. Large platforms must also verify user declarations with automated tools and embed permanent, unremovable metadata to trace origin.
source: For the first time, the law formally defines “synthetically generated information.”

prompt: In February 2026, the White House revised its factsheet on the interim US–India trade agreement within 24 hours of its release. Consider the following statements:
items: Certain pulses, namely lentils and chickpeas, were deleted from the tariff-cut list in the revised factsheet.
The revised factsheet describes India's USD 500 billion purchase figure as a firm commitment to be met within five years.
The official joint statement explicitly links US tariff relief to India halting purchases of Russian oil.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first is correct. The USD 500 billion figure was softened from a commitment to an intention, and the White House version has no timeline. It was the factsheet, not the joint statement, that linked tariff relief to Russian oil, since the joint statement is silent on it. Both sides call the deal an interim agreement, and it remains a framework until legal text is signed.
source: (lentils and chickpeas) were deleted from the tariff-cut list

prompt: According to reporting on the interim US–India trade agreement in February 2026, what was the position of India's goods trade with the United States?
options: A goods surplus of USD 41 billion
A goods deficit of USD 41 billion
A goods surplus of USD 100 billion
A goods deficit of USD 100 billion
explain: India runs a USD 41 billion goods surplus with the US. Importing USD 100 billion a year in American energy and technology under the stated purchase intention would flip India's trade balance, and the Indian private sector would have to bankroll it.
source: Currently, India runs a USD 41 billion goods surplus with the US.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the interim India-US trade deal that drew farmer protests in February 2026:
items: India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on US dried distillers’ grains (DDGs) and red sorghum for animal feed.
US soybean oil has been kept outside the deal's tariff concessions.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal claimed that 90-95% of domestic produce is shielded.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because soybean oil is listed among the US products on which India will eliminate or reduce tariffs, alongside tree nuts, fruit, and wine and spirits. Farmers argue that US imports could depress local prices, a backlash that echoes the 2020-21 protests which forced the repeal of three farm laws.
source: Under the interim deal, India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on a wide range of US food and agricultural products, including dried distillers’ grains (DDGs), red sorghum for animal feed, tree nuts, fresh and processed fruit, soybean oil, and wine and spirits.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bangladesh general election held in February 2026:
items: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) defeated a 9-party Islamist alliance in the first elections held since the 2024 uprising.
BNP leader Tarique Rahman is the son of the late former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia.
Dhaka is seeking Sheikh Hasina's extradition from India for crimes against humanity.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the BNP crushed an 11-party Islamist alliance, not a 9-party one, in the first elections since the 2024 uprising. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, and Hasina's extradition remains a sore point because New Delhi is still sheltering her.
source: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) secured a landslide victory Friday in the first elections since the 2024 uprising, crushing an 11-party Islamist alliance.

prompt: In February 2026, the new BNP government's interest in a China-backed river project near India's Siliguri Corridor was seen as a source of friction with New Delhi. Which river is this project on?
explain: The BNP has shown interest in the China-backed Teesta River project near the sensitive Siliguri Corridor. TBB's analysis notes that New Delhi is trying to keep Dhaka from pivoting fully into China's orbit.
source: Add to this the BNP’s interest in the China-backed Teesta River project near the sensitive Siliguri Corridor, and the reset looks increasingly uphill.

prompt: In February 2026, a guilty plea in New York drew attention to India's external intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW). RAW is housed in which of the following?
explain: US prosecutors described Vikash Yadav as employed by India's Cabinet Secretariat, which houses RAW. They allege he recruited Nikhil Gupta in May 2023 for the plot against Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, which Delhi says was against government policy.
source: Prosecutors say Indian intelligence official Vikash Yadav, employed by India's Cabinet Secretariat, which houses the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), recruited Gupta in May 2023.

prompt: In February 2026, Nikhil Gupta pleaded guilty to orchestrating a failed plot to assassinate Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York City. Consider the following statements:
items: India designated Pannun a terrorist in 2020.
Pannun is a dual US-British citizen.
In September 2023, the then Canadian Prime Minister accused India in parliament of involvement in the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Pannun, a lawyer at Sikhs for Justice, is a dual US-Canadian citizen. After the Nijjar accusation, India and Canada expelled each other's diplomats, while Washington chose to run a sting and build a federal case instead.
source: The target: Pannun, a dual US-Canadian citizen and lawyer at Sikhs for Justice, has campaigned globally for Khalistan, a proposed sovereign Sikh state carved from India's Punjab.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–South Korea Foreign Policy and Security Dialogue (FPSD):
items: The 6th round of the dialogue was held in Seoul in February 2026.
The 2014 round of the dialogue focused on defence.
The 2023 round of the dialogue focused on post-COVID resilience.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The 6th FPSD concluded in Seoul in February 2026, and the story notes that the 2014 round was about defence while the 2023 round was about post-COVID resilience. In 2026 the focus shifted to economic security, with most weight on shipbuilding, critical minerals and AI.
source: In 2014, it was about defence; by 2023, it was post-COVID resilience.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the AI Impact Summit that opened in New Delhi in February 2026:
items: It was the first time the global AI summit was held in the developing world.
It was scheduled to run until 20 February 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct. The summit opened on Monday 16 February 2026 and was expected to draw roughly 250,000 attendees through February 20. The government used it to position India as a voice for the Global South on AI policy.
source: This is the first time the global AI summit has been held in the developing world.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's artificial intelligence policy as outlined around the India AI Impact Summit in February 2026:
items: India is pushing a "Global AI Commons", a shared repository of AI use-cases.
