Data centres are being designated as "Strategic National Infrastructure".
Companies setting up data centres are offered tax holidays until 2047.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are stated in the story. The Global AI Commons aims to shape global AI norms around affordability rather than raw model power, and the data-centre incentives support a full-stack domestic AI cycle.
source: By designating data centres as “Strategic National Infrastructure” and offering tax holidays until 2047, New Delhi is building an AI ecosystem with a focus on frugal, sector-specific applications rather than resource-heavy chatbots.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's AI strategy as of February 2026:
items: At the India AI Impact Summit, the IT Minister projected USD 200 billion in AI and data infrastructure investment over the next two years.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 backs a race to build frontier AI models for global prestige.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the Economic Survey 2025-26 explicitly rejects the prestige race of frontier models and favours frugal, sector-specific applications. Of the projected USD 200 billion, USD 70 billion was already committed.
source: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw projected USD 200 billion in AI and data infrastructure investment over the next two years (USD 70B already committed) on Tuesday at the India AI Impact Summit.

prompt: In February 2026, India and France upgraded their bilateral relationship to which of the following?
explain: Prime Minister Modi and President Macron upgraded ties to a Special Global Strategic Partnership on 17 February 2026. The label puts France on par with India's top-tier relationships with Japan and the US.
source: Prime Minister Modi and President Macron upgraded bilateral ties to a "Special Global Strategic Partnership" on Tuesday, moving beyond just trade to co-manufacturing everything from Everest-bound helicopters to AI health tech.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the outcomes of the India–France summit held in February 2026:
items: An Airbus H125 helicopter assembly line was inaugurated in Karnataka.
A BEL-Safran joint venture was approved to manufacture HAMMER precision-guided missiles in India.
The India-France Year of Innovation 2026 was launched with a focus on AI in health and digital science.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. The H125 is an Everest-capable helicopter that both sides are targeting for export, and a Swami Vivekananda Cultural Centre will also open in France.
source: The duo inaugurated an Airbus H125 helicopter – the Everest-capable helicopter that both sides are targeting for export – assembly line in Karnataka and greenlit a BEL-Safran joint venture to manufacture HAMMER precision-guided missiles in India.

prompt: The Great Nicobar mega-project, cleared by the National Green Tribunal in February 2026, includes a transhipment hub located near which strait?
explain: The hub sits near the Malacca Strait and aims to reduce India's dependence on foreign transhipment ports such as Colombo and Singapore. It is also meant to firm up India's presence in the eastern Indian Ocean against China's network of facilities.
source: Located near the Malacca Strait, the hub aims to break India's dependence on foreign transhipment ports (like Colombo or Singapore)

prompt: In February 2026, India pitched an 'AI Commons' at the first AI summit held on Global South soil. Consider the following statements about the proposal:
items: It envisages a shared pool of multilingual models, open datasets and compute resources.
It proposes a funding facility to which nations would contribute data, compute or use-case development instead of building everything independently.
It builds on the Economic Survey's case that India should prioritise building frontier mega-models.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. The Economic Survey argued India should skip the mega-models and build small open-weight systems for real use cases. The AI Commons aims at affordable, locally relevant AI for public services, education and rural economies across the Global South.
source: The pitch: An AI Commons, a shared pool of multilingual models, open datasets, and compute resources designed for economies that can't afford Big Tech's price tag.

prompt: The Economic Survey released in early 2026 proposed layering an 'AI-OS' onto which existing Indian digital infrastructure?
explain: The Survey suggested layering an AI-OS onto India Stack so that startups would not have to spend billions on compute. India cites Aadhaar, UPI and India Stack as proof that open, interoperable digital infrastructure can scale to billions.
source: layer an "AI-OS" onto India Stack so startups aren't burning billions on compute

prompt: In February 2026, India began easing restrictions on Chinese suppliers in public procurement. Consider the following statements:
items: The restrictions, imposed after a 2020 border clash, required Chinese bidders on public contracts to register with a government committee and secure political and security clearances.
Under the easing, state-run firms can import critical power-transmission components from China without the standard government clearance.
The easing responds to a projected 40% shortfall in transformers and reactors over the next three years.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. The 2020 curbs had effectively locked Chinese firms out of a government contract market estimated at over USD 700 billion, and the government has framed the change as a targeted waiver.
source: State-run firms can now import critical power-transmission components from China without the standard government “Mother May I.”

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's push to manufacture rare earth permanent magnets, as of February 2026:
items: In November 2025, the government approved a USD 800 million programme to build an end-to-end rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing ecosystem.
Up to five private sector partners are to be selected through global competitive bidding.
India's consumption of these magnets is expected to double by 2040.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because India's consumption is expected to double by 2030, not 2040. The private partners will be supported by capital subsidies and production-linked incentives, and the Budget 2026-27 added dedicated rare earth corridors.
source: In November 2025, New Delhi approved an USD 800 million programme to build an end-to-end rare earth permanent magnet manufacturing ecosystem.

prompt: NdFeB permanent magnets, used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and modern weapons systems, are made of which elements?
explain: NdFeB stands for neodymium-iron-boron. China controls 90% of global processing of these materials, which left India's defence and green energy supply chains exposed when China restricted shipments in 2025.
source: Neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets are inside every electric vehicle, wind turbine, and modern weapons system.

prompt: In February 2026, India and Israel signed a defence Memorandum of Understanding meant to institutionalise cooperation between their private companies in weapons development. In which city was it signed?
explain: The MoU was signed in Tel Aviv on 19 February 2026, alongside a seminar involving 30 Indian and 26 Israeli firms. It signals a shift from buying and selling towards joint ventures and co-development under India's Make in India policy.
source: India and Israel signed a defence Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Tel Aviv on Thursday, a move designed to institutionalise cooperation between their private companies in weapons development.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Israel relations:
items: India and Israel established full ties in 2002.
India originally turned to Israel for arms to diversify away from its heavy dependence on French arms.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Neither statement is correct: the story says full ties were established in 1992, not 2002, and India first looked to Israel to reduce its heavy dependence on Russian arms, not French arms. Since then, defence has been the bedrock of the relationship, and Israel found a large, reliable customer for its high-tech sensors and drones.
source: Since establishing full ties in 1992, defence has been the bedrock of the relationship.

prompt: In February 2026, the US Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that which US law does not authorise the president to impose tariffs?
explain: The court held that IEEPA, a 1977 emergency law, does not authorise tariffs, noting that the word tariff does not appear in the statute. The ruling knocked out the legal basis of the Liberation Day tariffs on which the India-US interim deal was built.
source: In a 6-3 ruling on February 20, the court held that the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 emergency law, does not authorise the president to impose tariffs.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Pax Silica, which India joined in February 2026:
items: It was launched in December 2025 with India as one of its founding members.
The European Union and Taiwan participate in it as non-signatories.
Japan and the UAE are among its signatories.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: India was not part of the founding group when Pax Silica launched in December 2025, an absence linked to trade tensions with Washington. Signatories include Japan, South Korea, Singapore and the UAE, while the EU and Taiwan participate as non-signatories.
source: Notably, India was not part of the founding group when Pax Silica launched in December 2025.

prompt: In February 2026, India signed a landmark mining and minerals pact focused on iron ore and critical minerals during a state visit by the President of which country?
explain: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva received a full state welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan, and the minerals pact was central to the visit. It secures India's supply chain for its steel and manufacturing push while giving Brazil long-term, reliable demand.
source: Central to this visit was a landmark mining and minerals pact focused on iron ore and critical minerals.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Brazil trade, as discussed during the Brazilian President's visit to India in February 2026:
items: Bilateral trade between India and Brazil stood at USD 20 billion in 2025.
Prime Minister Modi set a USD 20 billion bilateral trade target to be met within ten years.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because bilateral trade stood at USD 15.2 billion in 2025, and USD 20 billion is the target. Statement 2 is wrong because that target is to be met within five years, not ten. Raw commodities such as iron ore and critical minerals will anchor the relationship for now.
source: Bilateral trade stood at USD 15.2 billion in 2025.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the New Delhi Declaration adopted at the close of the AI Impact Summit in February 2026:
items: Its centrepiece is a Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI that is binding on all signatory countries.
It proposes a Global AI Impact Commons, a repository to help countries replicate successful AI use cases across borders.
It champions open-source AI as an engine of economic and social development.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI is voluntary, not binding, so statement 1 is wrong. The voluntary Global AI Impact Commons and the push for open-source AI are both part of the Declaration, which aims to make AI adoption benefit the Global South.
source: The centerpiece is a voluntary Charter for the Democratic Diffusion of AI.

prompt: The New Delhi Declaration, adopted at the AI Impact Summit in February 2026, invoked which philosophy meaning "the world is one family"?
explain: The Declaration invoked Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the "world is one family" philosophy. In that spirit, it framed meaningful and affordable connectivity as a necessity for deploying AI rather than a luxury.
source: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: Invoking the “world is one family” philosophy, the Declaration frames

prompt: In February 2026, the Government of India unveiled PRAHAAR. Which of the following best describes it?
options: India's first comprehensive national counter-terrorism policy
India's first comprehensive national cybersecurity strategy
India's first comprehensive national drone regulation policy
India's first comprehensive national maritime security doctrine
explain: PRAHAAR stands for Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism and is India's first comprehensive national counter-terrorism policy. It brings intelligence agencies, police and prosecutors under one coordinated system.
source: India has unveiled PRAHAAR (Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism), its first comprehensive national counter-terrorism policy.

prompt: Consider the following statements about PRAHAAR, the national counter-terrorism policy unveiled by India in February 2026:
items: Its threat focus on CBRNED risks covers digital threats alongside chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive ones.
Prosecutors are brought into terror cases only after the investigation has been completed.
Real-time intelligence sharing between federal agencies and state police has been made formal policy.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the policy involves prosecutors from the start, so that terror cases survive court scrutiny. PRAHAAR replaces decades of agency-by-agency responses with a single national playbook.
source: Real-time intelligence sharing between federal agencies and state police is now formal policy, not a system that relies on interpersonal ties.

prompt: In February 2026, President Droupadi Murmu unveiled a bust at Rashtrapati Bhavan, replacing that of Edwin Lutyens. It depicts the only Indian to have served as Governor-General. Who was he?
explain: Rajagopalachari, known as Rajaji, was the only Indian Governor-General. He occupied the building from 1948 until 1950, when India became a republic and the post was abolished.
source: Rajagopalachari, better known as Rajaji, was the only Indian to serve as Governor-General.

prompt: Consider the following statements about steps taken in 2022 to remove colonial symbols:
items: Rajpath, the ceremonial boulevard outside Rashtrapati Bhavan, was renamed Kartavya Path.
The Indian Navy replaced the St George's Cross on its ensign with the seal of Maratha emperor Shivaji.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both changes took place in 2022. Rajpath (King's Way) was designed by Lutyens, and Shivaji built one of India's first indigenous naval forces to resist European colonial powers in the 17th century.
source: In 2022, the ceremonial boulevard outside Rashtrapati Bhavan, Rajpath (King's Way), also designed by Lutyens, was renamed to Kartavya Path (Path of Duty).

prompt: In February 2026, Canada launched legal proceedings to revoke the citizenship of Tahawwur Hussain Rana, accused by India of helping orchestrate the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks. Consider the following statements:
items: Canada's proceedings are based on terror charges linked to the 2008 Mumbai attacks.
Rana was extradited to India from the United States in 2025.
Rana obtained Canadian citizenship in 2001.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. Canada is not acting on terror charges, and immigration authorities (IRCC) allege Rana committed serious and deliberate deception by lying about his residency details on his citizenship application. The move came days before Prime Minister Mark Carney's scheduled visit to India.
source: Following his 2025 extradition from the US, he is currently in Indian custody awaiting trial.

prompt: In February 2026, the Union Cabinet approved renaming Kerala as 'Keralam'. Which Schedule of the Constitution lists all states by name and must be amended for such a change?
explain: The First Schedule lists all states by name, and it never reflected the Malayalam name 'Keralam'. India's states were drawn on linguistic lines in 1956.
source: The Constitution's First Schedule, which lists all states by name, never reflected that.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the proposal to rename Kerala as 'Keralam', approved by the Union Cabinet in February 2026:
items: After the Cabinet approval, the President refers the bill to the Kerala legislature for its views before Parliament votes on it.
The rename is sought on linguistic grounds, so that the Constitution reflects the state's Malayalam name.
The resolution demanding the rename was passed in 2024 by Kerala's CPI(M) government.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the CPI(M) government passed the resolution in 2024 on linguistic grounds, and the Cabinet approval now leads to the President referring the bill to Kerala's legislature before Parliament votes. The BJP-led Centre approved it nearly two years later, and with both state and Centre aligned the rename is expected to go through.
source: The CPI(M) government passed the original resolution in 2024 on linguistic grounds, arguing the Constitution should reflect the state's Malayalam name.

prompt: In February 2026, during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's two-day visit to Israel, India–Israel ties were upgraded to which of the following?
explain: The visit upgraded bilateral ties to a Special Strategic Partnership. Israel usually reserves this status for allies such as the US and Germany.
source: By upgrading ties to a Special Strategic Partnership, India now holds an elite status Israel usually reserves for its allies, such as the US and Germany.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Israel cooperation announced during Prime Minister Modi's visit to Israel in February 2026:
items: Israeli systems such as the Iron Dome and the Arrow interceptor are being folded into Sudarshan Chakra, India's planned indigenous missile shield.
Talks are underway for the co-production of the Iron Beam, a 100kW laser-based defence system.
The "Hexagon of Alliances" unveiled by Benjamin Netanyahu links India, Israel, Greece and Cyprus with moderate Arab and African states.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. Sudarshan Chakra is India's planned indigenous missile shield, the Iron Beam is Israel's 100kW laser system, and the Hexagon was pitched as a counterweight to the "radical Shia axis" and an "emerging radical Sunni axis".
source: India is folding Israeli tech, including the Iron Dome and Arrow interceptor, into Sudarshan Chakra, its planned indigenous missile shield.

prompt: The "Hexagon of Alliances", unveiled by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during Narendra Modi's February 2026 visit to Israel, was described as giving a boost to which connectivity project?
explain: The story says the Hexagon also boosts the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC). The grouping links India, Israel, Greece and Cyprus with moderate Arab and African states.
source: It also gives a boost to the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC).

prompt: Consider the following statements about the revised national accounts series that the Ministry of Statistics (MoSPI) launched in February 2026:
items: It adopts double deflation, which separately adjusts input and output prices to capture real value added.
The price basket used for deflation expands from 180 items to 600.
The deflators are drawn only from the wholesale price index (WPI) series.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because the expanded basket draws on both the CPI and WPI series. Critics had argued that the earlier WPI-only approach inflated growth when global commodity prices fell but domestic consumer prices held.
source: The price basket expands from 180 items to 600, drawing from both the consumer price index (CPI) and wholesale price index (WPI) series.

prompt: In February 2026, MoSPI launched a revised national accounts series. What is the new base year of this series?
explain: The base year moves to 2022-23 from 2011-12. The revision also replaces single deflation with double deflation.
source: The base year moves from 2011-12 to 2022-23.

prompt: In February 2026, India and Israel signed 27 agreements during Prime Minister Modi's visit to Israel. Consider the following statements about the outcomes:
items: India will send 50,000 workers to Israel over five years.
An India-Israel Centre of Excellence in Cybersecurity will be established in Israel.
The Centres of Excellence network for transferring Israeli agri-technologies will expand to 100 hubs.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The India-Israel Centre of Excellence in Cybersecurity will be set up in India, not Israel. The labour deal addresses shortages in Israel's construction and nursing sectors, and a Villages of Excellence initiative will take agri-technologies to the grassroots.
source: An India-Israel Centre of Excellence in Cybersecurity will be established in India to facilitate cooperation on cybersecurity, an area where Israel has established itself as a global leader.

prompt: In February 2026, which Indian payment system, described as the world's largest real-time payment system, was announced to launch in Israel?
explain: UPI is launching in Israel, allowing Indian tourists and businesses to pay via QR code. This lets them bypass Western credit card networks.
source: India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI), the world's largest real-time payment system, is launching in Israel.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the India–Canada uranium deal signed in March 2026 and India's nuclear programme:
items: Value of the Cameco uranium supply deal — USD 1.9bn
Period of uranium supply under the deal — through 2040
India's nuclear capacity target for 2047 — 100 GW
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The second pair is wrong: Cameco will supply 22 million pounds of uranium through 2035, not 2040. The fuel feeds India's 24 operating reactors as it works towards 100 GW of nuclear capacity by 2047.
source: Canada's Cameco signed a USD 1.9bn deal to supply 22 million pounds of uranium through 2035.

prompt: Around the time of Canadian PM Mark Carney's visit to India in March 2026, Canada moved to revoke the citizenship of Tahawwur Rana. He is accused of helping plan which of the following?
explain: Rana, a Pakistan-born businessman, is accused of helping plan the 2008 Mumbai attacks. Ottawa's move was seen as a high-value security concession that cleared the path for the economic reset.
source: Ottawa cleared the path by moving to revoke the citizenship of Tahawwur Rana, a Pakistan-born businessman accused of helping plan the 2008 Mumbai attacks.

prompt: In March 2026, with the Strait of Hormuz disrupted, Indian refiners asked Saudi Aramco to reroute crude supplies through the port of Yanbu. On which body of water does Yanbu lie?
explain: Yanbu is a Red Sea port, so shipments from it avoid Hormuz. They would still pass through the Bab el-Mandeb strait, within range of Iran-backed Houthi forces.
source: Indian refiners are asking Saudi Aramco to reroute supplies via the Red Sea port of Yanbu.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's energy situation during the Middle East conflict in March 2026:
items: India's oil reserves covered only about 25 days of demand.
Qatar, India's top LNG supplier, halted production.
Domestic oil fields met more than a quarter of India's crude needs.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: domestic fields cover less than 15% of India's crude needs. With the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, 40% of India's oil imports were stranded, and Russia offered to divert 9.5 million barrels of crude to India.
source: India's reserves cover only 25 days of demand.

prompt: After the US Supreme Court's ruling of February 2026 curbed the President's main tariff tool, the Trump administration's fallback was a blanket 15% levy expiring in July 2026. Under which provision was this levy imposed?
explain: The blanket 15% levy was imposed under Section 122 and expires in July. This weakened Washington's leverage over India, which had agreed in an interim trade framework to curb Russian oil purchases in exchange for lower tariffs.
source: His fallback, a blanket 15% levy under Section 122, expires in July.

prompt: In March 2026, the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena was torpedoed and sunk by a US Navy submarine about 40 nautical miles off which Sri Lankan location?
explain: The Dena was sunk on 4 March 2026 off Galle, in international waters. Washington confirmed the strike as part of Operation Epic Fury, the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.
source: A US Navy submarine torpedoed and sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena on March 4, 40 nautical miles off Galle, Sri Lanka.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Nepal's general election held in March 2026:
items: It was Nepal's first election since the Gen Z-led protests that ousted Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal.
The Gen Z protests of September 2025 began as a demonstration against fuel and medicine shortages.
Balendra 'Balen' Shah, whose RSP was on track for an outright majority, had earlier been mayor of Pokhara.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are wrong: the protests ousted PM KP Sharma Oli, they began as a digital rights protest that grew into an uprising against corruption, nepotism and youth unemployment, and Shah was mayor of Kathmandu, not Pokhara. Shah's RSP is barely three years old, so New Delhi's old playbook of working through Nepal's traditional parties will need to change.
source: The protests culminated in the ousting of PM KP Sharma Oli and his administration.

prompt: In which year did Nepal sign onto China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)?
explain: Nepal joined the BRI in 2017. Chinese-built projects such as the Pokhara International Airport and the proposed Kathmandu-Tibet railway are already on the ground.
source: Nepal signed onto China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) in 2017.

prompt: In 2015, India objected that Nepal's new constitution failed to accommodate which community, which has ties on both sides of the India–Nepal border?
explain: India said Nepal's fast-tracked 2015 constitution did not accommodate the Madhesi community. An unofficial blockade followed that choked off fuel and medicine and pushed Kathmandu towards Beijing. Balendra Shah is himself Madhesi.
source: In 2015, Nepal fast-tracked a new constitution over India's objections that it failed to accommodate the Madhesi community, an ethnic group with ties on both sides of the border.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's crude oil supply as reported in March 2026:
items: The US Treasury granted India a 30-day waiver to buy Russian crude already loaded on tankers.
Around 40% of India's crude imports pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
India's strategic reserves cover about 60 days of crude supply.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: India's strategic reserves cover only 20-25 days of crude supply, not 60 days, so statement 3 is wrong. The US Treasury granted the 30-day waiver on 6 March 2026, as the Middle East conflict disrupted shipping through Hormuz, even though India had earlier reduced Russian oil purchases under US pressure.
source: Around 40% of India’s crude imports pass through Hormuz, while strategic reserves cover only 20-25 days of crude supply

prompt: In March 2026, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted by conflict in the Middle East. Roughly what share of the world's oil trade does the strait normally carry?
explain: Hormuz normally carries about one-fifth of the world's oil trade, so even partial disruption pushes prices higher. In March 2026, insurers pulled war-risk coverage and shipping companies suspended Gulf transits.
source: Hormuz normally carries about 1/5 of the world’s oil trade, so even partial disruption sends prices higher.

prompt: In March 2026, India allowed the Iranian naval vessel IRIS Lavan, which had reported engine failure, to dock at which Indian port?
explain: The IRIS Lavan docked in Kochi on 4 March 2026 and remained there under Indian supervision. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar framed the decision as a humanitarian necessity rather than a political statement.
source: allow the Iranian naval vessel IRIS Lavan to dock in Kochi, framing the move as a humanitarian necessity rather than a political statement

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena, sunk in March 2026:
items: It was sunk by a US submarine about 40 miles off the Indian coast.
Sri Lankan authorities are holding about 200 of its surviving sailors in Colombo.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the story says the US submarine sank the IRIS Dena 40 miles off the Sri Lankan coast, not the Indian coast. Statement 2 is wrong because Sri Lanka recovered 87 bodies from the Dena strike, while the 200 sailors held in Colombo came from another vessel, the IRIS Bushehr. The Dena had just left India after taking part in the MILAN 2026 exercises.
source: a US submarine sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena 40 miles off the Sri Lankan coast

prompt: In March 2026, which country's defence ministry confirmed an agreement to procure the maritime variant of India's BrahMos supersonic cruise missile?
explain: Indonesia's defence ministry confirmed the agreement, which covers the maritime variant and is valued at roughly USD 200-450 million. Vietnam, Malaysia and Egypt are among the countries still in various stages of discussion. Jakarta's maritime dispute with China over the South China Sea and the Natuna Islands makes the purchase pointed.
source: Indonesia's defence ministry confirmed on Monday that Jakarta has entered an agreement to procure the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the BrahMos cruise missile:
items: It travels at Mach 3 and is described as the world's fastest operational cruise missile.
Russia holds a 49.5% share in the venture, so every export requires Moscow's approval.
Its first major export was a USD 375 million deal with the Philippines in 2022.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. BrahMos is a joint India-Russia venture that can be launched from land, sea and air. The Indonesia deal of March 2026 became India's second major arms export, after the Manila deal.
source: BrahMos is 49.5% Russian, meaning every export requires Moscow's approval.

prompt: As reported in March 2026, what is India's defence export target for 2029?
explain: India's 2029 defence export target is USD 5.9 billion. Exports reached a record USD 2.76 billion in the previous year, and BrahMos carries most of the hope of closing the gap. TBB notes that India still remains the world's second-largest arms importer.
source: India's defence exports hit a record USD 2.76 billion last year, and BrahMos is carrying most of the ambition to push that further toward its 2029 target of USD 5.9 billion.

prompt: Under India's Environmental Impact Assessment framework, as described in March 2026, which bodies handle most regional projects?
options: Benches of the National Green Tribunal
Regional offices of the Central Pollution Control Board
explain: Large national projects are reviewed by the central government, while most regional projects go to the State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities. The proposed SAEIA is meant to act as a backup when these state authorities stop functioning.
source: Large national projects are reviewed by the central government under the EIA framework, while most regional projects are handled by the State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities locally.

prompt: In March 2026, following supply disruptions caused by the West Asia conflict, India took steps to manage its gas supply. Consider the following statements:
items: The government invoked force majeure and fully protected gas supplies to households and vehicles.
The minimum interval between LPG cylinder bookings was extended from 21 to 25 days to curb hoarding.
Imports meet about one-third of India's annual LPG consumption.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because imports fill two-thirds of India's annual LPG consumption, not one-third. Under the force majeure priority order, fertiliser plants, factories and commercial users receive only a fraction of their usual supply.
source: To stop hoarding, the government also extended the minimum time between LPG cylinder bookings from 21 to 25 days, after some households that previously booked every 55 days started booking every 15.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's energy and industrial position in March 2026:
items: Share of India's steel output using gas-based production — about 6%
Typical capacity utilisation of gas-fired power plants — about 30%
Bids received for a 12,000 MWh gas-based power tender — zero
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Gas-fired power plants typically run at 6-10% capacity. Roughly 30% was the level they had been expected to reach in summer 2026. With no private bidders willing to commit while LNG was unavailable or too expensive, the workaround was to bring coal plants back online.
source: This year, a tender for 12,000 MWh received zero bids as no private player is willing to commit with LNG either unavailable or too expensive.

prompt: In March 2026, the United States granted India a waiver relating to Russian oil. Consider the following statements:
items: The waiver allowed India to buy Russian oil already stranded at sea for a period of 90 days.
The oil covered by the waiver was estimated to meet about a month of India's oil demand.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told G7 ministers that these cargoes would not benefit the Kremlin because the oil had not yet been loaded.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the story says the waiver lasts 30 days, not 90; Nomura estimated the 20-30 million barrels would cover just four days of Indian demand, not a month; and Bessent said the cargoes would not help the Kremlin because the oil was already loaded. Bessent also said India would eventually buy more American crude instead.
source: The US granted India a 30-day waiver to purchase stranded Russian oil last Friday at sea, which we covered here.

prompt: In March 2026, India changed its rules on foreign direct investment from land-bordering countries. Consider the following statements about the change:
items: The relaxation applies only to investments from China and not to other land-bordering neighbours.
Investments where Chinese beneficial ownership stays below 10% now enter through the automatic route.
Proposals in electronics, batteries, rare-earth magnets, capital goods and solar cells will receive a government decision within 60 days, provided Indian residents retain majority control.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the change is part of a broader policy covering all land-bordering neighbours, though it is squarely aimed at rebuilding commercial ties with Beijing. Under the previous policy, any firm with a Chinese beneficial owner needed government approval regardless of stake, which caught global PE and VC funds with Chinese limited partners.
source: part of a broader policy covering all such neighbours but squarely aimed at rebuilding commercial ties with Beijing after six years of friction.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the thaw in India–China commercial ties:
items: Galwan clash that froze ties — 2020
Narendra Modi's first visit to Beijing in seven years — August 2025
Clearance of business visas for Chinese technicians — February 2026
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Business visas for Chinese technicians were cleared in December 2025; February 2026 was when state-run power and coal companies were allowed to resume equipment imports. The visa freeze had stalled projects such as Bengaluru's Yellow Line metro for years.
source: business visas for Chinese technicians were cleared in December

prompt: In March 2026, US President Donald Trump announced that Reliance Industries would fund a new oil refinery in Brownsville, Texas. Consider the following statements about this announcement:
items: The facility is designed to exclusively process American shale oil.
The USD 300 billion figure attached to the project reflects its construction costs.
Reliance Industries confirmed its role as an equity investor soon after the announcement.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The USD 300 billion figure reflects 20 years of projected output, not construction costs, and Reliance stayed silent, disclosing neither the investment size nor whether its role is an equity stake, offtake agreement or partnership. It would be the first new US oil refinery in 50 years.
source: though the USD 300 billion figure reflects 20 years of projected output, not construction costs.

prompt: Reliance Industries' Jamnagar refining complex, described in March 2026 as the world's largest, is located in which Indian state?
explain: The Jamnagar complex is in Gujarat and can process 1.4 million barrels of crude daily. As of March 2026, Reliance held no overseas refining assets.
source: Reliance operates the world’s largest refining complex in Jamnagar, Gujarat, capable of processing 1.4 million barrels of crude daily.

prompt: In March 2026, the Lok Sabha took up a no-confidence motion against Speaker Om Birla. Consider the following statements:
items: It was only the fourth such motion against a Speaker in India's parliamentary history.
The motion was defeated in a recorded division of members.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The motion was rejected by voice vote, not in a recorded division. The opposition INDIA alliance, led by the Congress, filed it, citing repeated denial of floor time to its members.
source: rejected a no-confidence motion against Speaker Om Birla by voice vote on Tuesday, only the fourth such motion in the country's parliamentary history

prompt: In March 2026, former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Farooq Abdullah survived an assassination attempt in Jammu. Consider the following statements about the region's political background:
items: The Jammu and Kashmir National Conference was founded in 1932 by Sheikh Abdullah.
Article 370, revoked by Parliament in 2019, had granted the region its own constitution and special autonomy.
After the 2019 revocation, Jammu and Kashmir was split into two union territories under a lieutenant governor appointed by New Delhi.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: Sheikh Abdullah founded the National Conference in 1932, and the 2019 revocation of Article 370 split the region into two union territories under direct central administration. Farooq Abdullah's son, Omar Abdullah, is the union territory's current chief minister.
source: In 2019, the Indian parliament revoked Article 370, which had granted the region its own constitution and special autonomy.

prompt: In March 2026, India held talks with Iran on the safe passage of Indian vessels through the Strait of Hormuz. Consider the following statements about India's energy dependence as reported at the time:
items: The Middle East supplies about 80% of India's crude oil.
India relies on the Middle East for nearly all of its LPG.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The Middle East accounts for 40% of India's crude, not 80%, but nearly all of its LPG. With limited strategic reserves, any bottleneck in the Persian Gulf is an immediate economic threat to India.
source: It relies on the Middle East for 40% of its crude and nearly all its LPG.

prompt: In March 2026, India warned drugmakers against directly or indirectly advertising prescription weight-loss drugs. Consider the following statements:
items: The warning was issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).
The regulator said that 'awareness campaigns' about such drugs fall outside the scope of its restrictions.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the warning came from the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), not the FSSAI. Statement 2 is wrong because the CDSCO said even 'awareness campaigns', influencer promotions or exaggerated claims of effectiveness could trigger action. Prescription medicines cannot be marketed to the public under Indian law, and cheaper generic versions of semaglutide were expected once Novo Nordisk's Indian patent expired later in March 2026.
source: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) said even “awareness campaigns,” influencer promotions or claims exaggerating drug effectiveness could trigger action.

prompt: Consider the following statements about US tariff measures affecting India in early 2026:
items: After the US Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs in February 2026, Washington imposed a flat 10% duty on all imports under Section 122, valid through 24 July.
Unlike Section 122 duties, which are capped at 15%, tariffs imposed under Section 301 carry no ceiling and no expiry.
The Section 301 investigations launched in March 2026 covered 16 economies, including India.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the Section 122 duty is a flat 10% valid through 24 July, Section 301 tariffs have no ceiling or expiry unlike Section 122's 15% cap, and the March 2026 probes covered 16 economies including India. The Section 301 probes target excess manufacturing capacity in sectors such as steel, solar and petrochemicals, and Indian officials see them as a pressure tactic.
source: Unlike Section 122's 15% cap, Section 301 tariffs carry no ceiling and no expiry.

prompt: In March 2026, the US issued temporary waivers allowing India to receive Russian crude oil already at sea. Licences for such purchases were issued by which US office?
options: Office of the US Trade Representative
Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States
explain: The US issued Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) licences allowing purchases of Russian crude. This came six weeks after the interim trade framework had required India to halt Russian crude imports, which India had only slowed.
source: the US is issuing Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) licenses to purchase more of it.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the 'Economic Stabilisation Fund' proposed by the Union Finance Minister in March 2026:
items: It was proposed with a size of USD 6.20 billion.
The government raised its FY26 fiscal deficit target to accommodate the fund.
It creates a pre-authorised pool of cash that can be deployed quickly when supply chains snap or energy prices spike.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the government is sticking to its FY26 fiscal deficit target of INR 15.58 trillion despite the new spend. The fund is meant as a war chest to insulate the economy from global volatility.
source: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman proposed a USD 6.20 billion ‘Economic Stabilisation Fund’ last Friday, a war chest designed to insulate New Delhi from global volatility.

prompt: While proposing an Economic Stabilisation Fund in March 2026, the Union government retained its FY26 fiscal deficit target at roughly what share of GDP under the revamped accounting system?
explain: The FY26 fiscal deficit target of INR 15.58 trillion (USD 168 billion) works out to roughly 4.5% of GDP under the revamped accounting system. The government kept this target unchanged despite the new USD 6.20 billion fund.
source: the government is sticking to its FY26 fiscal deficit target of INR 15.58 trillion (USD 168 billion), roughly 4.5% of GDP under the revamped accounting system.

prompt: In March 2026, Iran allowed two Indian-flagged vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz during its blockade. Consider the following statements:
items: The two vessels were LPG carriers chartered by Indian Oil Corp.
The vessels were escorted by the Indian Navy during the transit.
India draws nearly all its crude oil from the Middle East.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because India draws 40% of its crude from the Middle East. It is nearly all of its LPG that comes from the region. The carriers Shivalik and Nanda Devi were due at western Indian ports on 16 and 17 March, while 22 more vessels remained trapped west of the Strait.
source: Escorted by the Indian Navy, the vessels Shivalik and Nanda Devi – chartered by Indian Oil Corp – are passed the bottleneck and will reach western Indian ports by March 16 and 17.

prompt: In March 2026, the Election Commission of India announced assembly elections in five states and Union Territories. Which of the following was scheduled to vote in two phases?
explain: West Bengal was the only one of the five to vote in two phases, on April 23 and 29. Assam, Kerala and Puducherry voted on April 9 and Tamil Nadu on April 23. Counting for all five was set for May 4, and the Model Code of Conduct took effect on announcement.
source: Assam, Kerala, and Puducherry vote on April 9; Tamil Nadu on April 23; West Bengal in two phases on April 23 and 29.

prompt: In February 2026, India intercepted three tankers, the Asphalt Star, Al Jafzia and Stellar Ruby, which later figured in India–Iran talks. Consider the following statements about them:
items: They were intercepted by the Indian Coast Guard about 100 nautical miles off Mumbai.
All three vessels fly the Iranian flag.
They were alleged to have falsified their identities and conducted illegal ship-to-ship fuel transfers.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only Stellar Ruby flies an Iranian flag; the other two are registered in Nicaragua and Mali. In March 2026, Iran's ambassador met Indian foreign ministry officials to seek their release as India negotiated safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.
source: India's Coast Guard intercepted the Asphalt Star, Al Jafzia and Stellar Ruby about 100 nautical miles off Mumbai in early February, alleging they had falsified their identities and conducted illegal ship-to-ship fuel transfers.

prompt: During the Strait of Hormuz disruption of March 2026, almost all of India's LPG imports came from which two countries?
explain: Almost all of India's LPG imports come from Qatar and the UAE, and there is no bypass route for them. That made cooking gas the bottleneck, while crude imports were largely rerouted via Russian supplies and alternative Gulf ports.
source: Almost all of India's LPG imports come from Qatar and the UAE, and there is no bypass for it.

prompt: In March 2026, Shivalik and Nanda Devi were in the news. What were they?
options: Indian LPG carriers allowed through the Strait of Hormuz
Tankers seized by the Coast Guard off Mumbai
Indian Navy frigates sent to force open the strait
Crude tankers rerouted to carry Russian oil
explain: Tehran let the two Indian LPG carriers through the strait, and Jaishankar cited them as proof that talking had yielded results. Six more LPG-laden vessels remained stuck in the Gulf, and India avoided Trump's call to send warships.
source: Tehran recently let two Indian LPG carriers, Shivalik and Nanda Devi, through the strait.

prompt: In September 2025, which body released draft rules requiring wind and solar developers to match their promised supply to the grid more closely, with penalties for deviations?
explain: The Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) issued the draft grid-discipline rules in September 2025. In March 2026, the government asked the CERC to re-examine the penalties after developers warned that they would kill investment.
source: Draft rules released by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) in September 2025 aimed to force renewable players to match their promised supply to the grid.

prompt: Consider the following statements about deviation tolerance bands for renewable energy projects, as reported in March 2026:
items: Under the existing rules, wind developers have a tolerance band of +/-15% around their promised supply.
The CERC draft proposed shrinking the solar tolerance band to +/-5% by 2026.
The CERC draft proposed bringing renewable tolerance bands to parity with conventional generators by 2028.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. The draft proposed a gradual reduction that would reach the tolerance bands of conventional generators by 2031, not 2028. Developers estimated that the tighter bands could cause revenue losses of up to 48% because of the intermittent nature of renewables.
source: Under the new proposal, tolerance bands would shrink to +/-10% for wind and +/-5% for solar by 2026 then gradually reduce until finally having the same tolerance bands as conventional generators by 2031.

prompt: In March 2026, Pakistan carried out airstrikes in Kabul that hit the Omid Addiction Treatment Hospital. Consider the following statements about the international response:
items: India based its condemnation on sovereignty and civilian harm, without addressing whether the Taliban harbours militants.
India was the only country to condemn Pakistan's actions outright.
India sent a special envoy to shuttle between Kabul and Islamabad.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. China, not India, had a special envoy shuttling between the two sides for a week, while India issued statements rather than brokering a solution. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal accused Pakistan of trying to dress up a massacre as a military operation.
source: Meanwhile, China has had a special envoy shuttling between the two sides for a week.

prompt: In March 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA). Consider the following statements about it:
items: It allocates USD 3.6 billion to develop 100 plug-and-play industrial parks.
Parks ranging from 100 to 1,000 acres can receive financial assistance of up to USD 100,000 per acre.
Funding will be shared equally among all states, without any competitive selection.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because states must compete with reform-oriented, investment-ready proposals to win funding. The parks are meant to be fully serviced sites with roads, utilities, drainage, common treatment facilities and ICT networks, built through partnerships between the Centre, states and private developers.
source: On Wednesday, the Cabinet approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna (BHAVYA), allocating USD 3.6 billion to develop 100 plug-and-play industrial parks nationwide.

prompt: The BHAVYA industrial parks scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2026, builds on which existing programme?
explain: BHAVYA builds on the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme, which already has 20 projects across 13 states. The scheme is part of New Delhi's strategy of large infrastructure spending to draw in private investment and lift industrial growth.
source: The scheme builds on the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme, which already has 20 projects across 13 states

prompt: In March 2026, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy extended the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) framework to which part of the solar supply chain, with domestic sourcing mandatory from 1 June 2028?
explain: MNRE announced on 18 March 2026 that all clean energy projects must use domestically manufactured ingots and wafers from 1 June 2028. Locally assembled modules are already required in state-backed projects, and domestic cells become mandatory from June 2026.
source: India will require all clean energy projects to use domestically manufactured solar ingots and wafers from 1 June 2028.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's solar manufacturing localisation push, as of March 2026:
items: Domestically made solar cells become mandatory across all projects from June 2026.
India's domestic ingot and wafer manufacturing capacity is roughly 15 GW.
The ALMM list for ingots and wafers will not be issued until at least three independent manufacturers with a combined 15 GW capacity are operational.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: domestic ingot and wafer capacity sits at roughly 2 GW, all built under the PLI scheme; 15 GW is the combined capacity threshold required before the ALMM list is issued. India still relies almost entirely on Chinese imports for cells, ingots, wafers and polysilicon.
source: Domestic ingot and wafer capacity sits at roughly 2 GW, all of it built under PLI.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Union government's privatisation programme as of March 2026:
items: The strategic sale of IDBI Bank collapsed after bids failed to meet the government's minimum price.
The privatisation of Shipping Corporation of India and HLL Lifecare was completed in 2020-21.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The SCI and HLL Lifecare sales were not completed and have been stuck in limbo since 2020-21. Beyond the sale of Air India to Tata, the drive announced in 2021 has been held back by red tape, high reserve prices and unresolved liabilities such as pension dues.
source: The IDBI deal collapsed last week after bids failed to meet the government’s minimum price, while SCI and HLL have been trapped in limbo since 2020-21.

prompt: In March 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan about the situation in West Asia. Safe and free navigation through which strait did the two leaders stress?
explain: Both leaders stressed safe and free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and agreed to keep working together to restore peace in the region. On the same call, Modi reiterated India's strong condemnation of attacks on the UAE that had caused loss of innocent lives and damage to civilian infrastructure.
source: Both leaders stressed the importance of ensuring safe and free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and agreed to continue working together for the early restoration of peace, security and stability in the region.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's fertiliser supply position in March 2026:
items: West Asia accounts for roughly half of India's diammonium phosphate (DAP) and urea imports.
The government prioritised gas supplies to fertiliser plants, ensuring at least 70% of average consumption.
DAP inventories were lower than a year earlier.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. DAP inventories were up 105% and urea inventories up 10.7% from a year earlier, giving India a healthy buffer. Most shipments need to arrive between March and May ahead of the June–July kharif planting surge.
source: Urea and DAP inventories are up 10.7% and 105% respectively from a year ago.

prompt: In March 2026, threats around which strait disrupted LNG shipments from Qatar to India, prompting the government to prioritise gas supplies to fertiliser plants?
explain: Qatar's LNG shipments were disrupted by threats around the Strait of Hormuz amid the West Asia war. In response, the government ensured fertiliser plants receive at least 70% of their average gas consumption.
source: after LNG shipments from Qatar were disrupted by Strait of Hormuz threats, which we covered here.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's power supply outlook for summer 2026, as reported in March 2026:
items: Peak power demand is projected to reach a record 291 GW.
India has 15 imported coal-based power plants with a combined capacity of 12 GW.
Limited gas supplies have been reprioritised towards the power sector to handle sudden summer demand surges.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: peak demand is projected at a record 271 GW, the 15 imported coal-based plants have 17 GW capacity (12 GW is the estimated peak shortfall), and gas has been reprioritised towards households and fertiliser production rather than the power sector. The Centre is considering invoking Section 11 of the Electricity Act to make these imported coal plants run at full throttle.
source: The government is reportedly targeting some of the 15 imported coal-based power plants that have 17 GW capacity in total to bridge an estimated 12 GW peak summer power demand shortfall.

prompt: In March 2026, it was reported that the Indian government was asking smartphone makers to pre-install the Aadhaar app on new phones. Consider the following statements:
items: Aadhaar is a 12-digit identity number linked to an individual's fingerprints and iris scans.
The updated Aadhaar app released in January 2026 lets users manage family profiles and secure their biometric data against unauthorised use.
The push to preload the Aadhaar app on smartphones came from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the request came from the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), which wants wider reach without an App Store download. Industry body MAIT is pushing back, citing higher production costs and the need for India-specific assembly lines.
source: The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) wants the Aadhaar app preloaded into smartphones to enhance reach and skip the App Store download.

prompt: In March 2026, India recommended anti-dumping duties on imports of DASDA from China. Consider the following statements about this recommendation:
items: The recommendation was made by the Directorate General of Trade Remedies, which functions under the Commerce Ministry.
The Finance Ministry has three months to decide whether to impose the duty.
The proposed duty is a fixed percentage of import value, levied on every shipment regardless of its price.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the DGTR proposed a reference-price duty: importers pay the difference between the arrival price and USD 3,453 per ton only if shipments fall below that threshold. The complaint was filed by Deepak Nitrite, which controls roughly 60% of India's DASDA production.
source: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR), under the Commerce Ministry, proposed a reference-price duty: importers pay the difference between arrival price and USD 3,453 per ton if shipments fall below that threshold.

prompt: DASDA (4,4-Diamino Stilbene-2,2-Disulphonic Acid), on whose Chinese imports India recommended anti-dumping duties in March 2026, is mainly used in which of the following?
explain: DASDA is an organic chemical used in textile dyes and optical brighteners. It feeds into optical brightening agents used across India's textile and paper industries, so downstream manufacturers will absorb the higher input cost first.
source: an organic chemical used in textile dyes and optical brighteners, after finding evidence of dumped pricing.

prompt: As of March 2026, almost all of India's LPG imports and the bulk of its crude imports pass through which maritime chokepoint?
explain: The Strait of Hormuz carries the bulk of India's crude and almost all of its LPG imports. India's big three public sector refiners are configured for Gulf crude, and reconfiguring a refinery for different feedstock is a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar project.
source: The bulk of India's crude and almost all of its LPG imports transit the Strait of Hormuz.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's petroleum sector as reported in March 2026:
items: India's crude oil import dependency is near 89%.
Fuel prices were deregulated between 2010 and 2014.
Retail pump prices rose by roughly 25% after the start of the West Asia conflict.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Retail prices stayed steady after the West Asia conflict began; the roughly 25% rise was in industrial diesel. Although prices are formally deregulated, the government has directed oil marketing companies to hold the line, leaving them with negative margins at USD 100–105 per barrel.
source: Crude import dependency sits near 89%, and domestic LPG cylinder prices have already climbed roughly 7%.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's response to supply disruptions in March 2026:
items: Prime Minister Modi chaired a Cabinet Committee on Security meeting to review energy, fertiliser and supply chain resilience.
India turned to Russia, Belarus and Morocco for fertiliser supplies.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The CCS meeting on 22 March 2026 reviewed energy, fertiliser and supply chain resilience, and India has already sourced fertiliser from Russia, Belarus and Morocco. The Prime Minister also ordered a dedicated group of ministers and secretaries to coordinate across sectors and told states to act against hoarding.
source: Prime Minister Modi chaired a high-level Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) meeting on Sunday to review India's energy, fertiliser, and supply chain resilience, amid sustained disruptions in sourcing.

prompt: In March 2026, the US issued a temporary sanctions waiver on Iranian oil amid the US-Israeli-Iranian conflict. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It covers Iranian oil already at sea that was loaded on or before 20 March 2026 and discharged by 19 April 2026.
It was the first time the US temporarily waived oil sanctions during the conflict.
Earlier temporary waivers during the conflict covered Russian oil already at sea.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The story calls this the third temporary US waiver of oil sanctions during the war, after earlier waivers for Russian oil already at sea. Analysts estimate the 30-day waiver covers roughly 170 million barrels on water. That volume is enough to ease shortages but not to bring prices down sharply.
source: This marks the third time the US has temporarily waived oil sanctions during this war, having previously issued temporary waivers for Russian oil already at sea.

prompt: In March 2026, India scrapped temporary caps on domestic airfares. Consider the following statements:
items: The caps had been imposed during Air India's operational disruption in December 2025.
Domestic airfares in India are formally regulated by the government at all times, not only during crises.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the caps date from IndiGo's operational meltdown in December 2025, not Air India's. Statement 2 is wrong because airfares are technically deregulated, with New Delhi intervening only during crises. Lifting the caps lets airlines pass on higher jet fuel costs from the West Asia conflict.
source: India will scrap temporary domestic airfare caps starting today (March 23), ending a period of state-mandated pricing that began during IndiGo’s operational meltdown last December.

prompt: In March 2026, the Indian rupee fell to a record low against the US dollar amid the West Asia conflict. Consider the following statements:
items: The Reserve Bank of India cut rates by a cumulative 125 basis points during 2025.
Forward dollar sales of nearly USD 100 billion by the Reserve Bank of India helped cushion the rupee's fall.
Since US-Israeli strikes on Iran began, the rupee depreciated less sharply than the Thai baht and the South Korean won.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the RBI cut rates by 125 basis points in 2025, its forward dollar sales of nearly USD 100 billion cushioned the fall, and the rupee's roughly 3% decline was smaller than the Thai baht's 4.9% and the South Korean won's 3.9%. The rupee nonetheless hit a fresh all-time low of 93.94 against the US dollar, with foreign investors pulling USD 9.6 billion from Indian equities in March 2026.
source: The rupee has actually fared better than peers – the Thai baht is down 4.9%, and the South Korean won 3.9% over the same period.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in March 2026:
items: It was introduced in the Lok Sabha, and the Finance Minister proposed referring it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
It would allow eligible firms to conduct up to three share buybacks a year.
Fast-track mergers would be simplified where shareholders holding at least 75% in both firms approve.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the bill allows two buybacks a year, up from one, with a six-month cooling-off gap. The bill also plans to decriminalise select compliance lapses, replacing jail risk with civil penalties.
source: Eligible firms may conduct two share buybacks annually, up from one, with a six-month cooling-off gap.

prompt: Under the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in March 2026, which body would gain broader powers, including a wider definition of professional misconduct for auditors?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
explain: The bill widens the National Financial Reporting Authority's powers so that auditor misconduct covers lapses tied to company law violations. This stronger audit enforcement balances the faster buybacks and mergers the bill permits.
source: The National Financial Reporting Authority would gain broader powers, including a wider definition of “professional misconduct” for auditors tied to company law violations.

prompt: In March 2026, the Ministry of Commerce restored full benefits under the Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products (RoDTEP) scheme. Consider the following statements:
items: The RoDTEP scheme was launched in 2021.
In February 2026, the government had capped RoDTEP benefits at 50%.
The restored full rates were applied only prospectively, from the date of the March 2026 decision.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. The restoration was backdated to 23 February and runs only through 31 March, so it unwinds the February cut retrospectively. The government reversed the cap to offset surging maritime costs from the West Asia conflict.
source: The reversal was backdated to February 23 to offset surging maritime costs stemming from the West Asia conflict.

prompt: The Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products (RoDTEP) scheme, whose full rates were restored in March 2026, is primarily designed to:
options: Refund domestic taxes embedded in the cost of export goods
Provide interest subvention on pre-shipment export credit
Insure exporters against default by overseas buyers
Subsidise ocean freight charges paid by exporters
explain: RoDTEP is a WTO-compliant tool that neutralises domestic taxes, such as electricity duty and VAT on fuel, incurred in making and distributing export goods. Industry groups said the February 2026 cap of 50% had added 1-2% to export prices.
source: Launched in 2021, RoDTEP is a WTO-compliant tool that neutralises domestic taxes – like electricity duty and VAT on fuel – incurred in the manufacturing and distribution of export goods.

prompt: In March 2026, the Supreme Court held that, under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, Scheduled Caste status is restricted to persons professing which religions?
explain: The bench held that SC status under the 1950 Order is limited to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists, so converting to Christianity or Islam ends it. The court reasoned that the caste system is alien to Christianity and Islam.
source: Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Manmohan held that SC status is restricted to Hindus, Sikhs, and Buddhists under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court ruling of March 2026 on conversion and Scheduled Caste status:
items: The court held that SC status under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 is available to Hindus, Sikhs and Christians.
The case involved a Tamil Nadu pastor who had been practising Christianity for over a decade.
The court held that protections under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act continue to apply to a convert.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong. The court held that SC status is restricted to Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists, the case involved an Andhra Pradesh pastor, and Atrocities Act protections cease to apply once a person converts and practises another faith. The bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Manmohan held that the caste system is alien to Christianity and Islam.
source: Once a person converts and practices another faith – as in the case of an Andhra Pradesh pastor who had been practising Christianity for over a decade – protections under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act cease to apply.

prompt: Consider the following statements about commissions on extending Scheduled Caste status to Dalit Christians and Muslims, as of March 2026:
items: A commission in 2007 recommended delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion.
A commission appointed in 2022 to revisit the question submitted its report in October 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The 2022 commission's report was due in October 2025 but had not been submitted. The Modi government opposes extending SC status to Dalit Christians and Muslims and has dismissed the 2007 recommendation as flawed.
source: A new commission was appointed in 2022 to revisit the question; its report, due October 2025, has not been submitted.

prompt: In March 2026, Prime Minister Modi and President Trump held a phone call focused on the Middle East crisis. Which maritime chokepoint did the call specifically seek to keep functional?
explain: The call addressed the urgent need to keep the Strait of Hormuz functional after its near-closure throttled shipping and gas supplies. Modi said keeping the Strait open, secure and accessible is essential for the whole world.
source: PM Modi and President Trump spoke on Tuesday to address the Middle East crisis, specifically the urgent need to keep the Strait of Hormuz functional.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Middle East crisis as reported in March 2026:
items: The Modi–Trump call in March 2026 was the first between the two leaders since the US and Israel launched coordinated strikes against Iran on 28 February 2026.
The Strait of Hormuz handles 40% of India's crude oil imports.
Iran's parliamentary speaker Ghalibaf denied that any negotiations with the US had taken place, calling reports of talks an attempt to manipulate oil markets.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the call was the leaders' first since the 28 February strikes, the Strait carries 40% of India's crude imports, and Ghalibaf denied any talks had occurred. Trump had postponed planned strikes on Iran's power plants, citing 'productive' talks with Tehran.
source: Iran's parliamentary speaker Ghalibaf denied any negotiations had taken place, calling reports of talks an attempt to manipulate oil markets.

prompt: In March 2026, the Supreme Court permitted the withdrawal of life support for Harish Rana, who had been in a vegetative state for 13 years. Consider the following statements about the case:
items: It was the first case to operationalise the Supreme Court's 2018 recognition of the right to die with dignity.
The Delhi High Court had initially denied the family's plea in 2024, and the Supreme Court overturned that decision.
The Supreme Court ruled that clinically assisted nutrition constitutes medical treatment that can be withdrawn.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the case operationalised the 2018 right to die with dignity, and the Supreme Court overturned the Delhi High Court's 2024 refusal. The court held that clinically assisted nutrition can be withdrawn when it no longer serves the patient's interest, and it permitted withdrawal of life support on 11 March 2026.
source: The Delhi High Court had initially denied his family's plea in 2024; the Supreme Court overturned that, ruling that clinically assisted nutrition constitutes medical treatment that can be withdrawn when it no longer serves the patient's interest.

prompt: In March 2026, India delayed by a year its plan to make coal-fired power plants ramp down when solar generation peaks. The plan requires retrofits so that these plants can cut their minimum operating level to which of the following?
explain: The retrofits would cut coal plants' minimum use rate to 40% from the current 55%. The plan stalled because the federal regulator has yet to approve a framework on who pays for the retrofits.
source: Coal plants need expensive retrofits to cut their minimum use rate to 40% from 55%, but no one has agreed on who pays.

prompt: In March 2026, India postponed its plan for flexible operation of coal-fired power plants. Consider the following statements:
items: The Central Electricity Authority estimates that battery storage is at least ten times cheaper per kilowatt-hour than retrofitting coal plants for flexible operation.
When coal plants cannot ramp down, grid operators curtail solar output, and the compensation paid to solar generators is funded from the federal budget rather than through electricity tariffs.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Neither is correct. Statement 1 reverses the comparison: the CEA says flexible coal is at least ten times cheaper, at INR 0.28 to INR 0.60 per kilowatt-hour against INR 5.76 to INR 6.04 for battery storage. Statement 2 is wrong because Ember says the USD 76 million bill was funded through higher electricity tariffs.
source: Retrofitting would add just INR 0.28 to INR 0.60 per kilowatt-hour to tariffs, versus INR 5.76 to INR 6.04 for battery storage, making flexible coal at least ten times cheaper, according to the Central Electricity Authority.

prompt: In March 2026, the Union Cabinet approved India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). What reduction in emissions intensity by 2035, against 2005 levels, does it target?
explain: The updated NDC targets a 47% cut in emissions intensity by 2035 from 2005 levels. Critics call this a marginal shift from the earlier goal of 45% by 2030.
source: On Wednesday, the Union Cabinet approved India’s updated climate pledges, targeting a 47% reduction in emissions intensity by 2035 against 2005 levels.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to climate targets discussed when India approved its updated NDC in March 2026:
items: India's non-fossil fuel share of power capacity by 2035 — 60%
India's carbon sink by 2035 — up to 4 billion tonnes
EU's binding absolute emissions reduction target for 2040 from 1990 levels — 90%
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correct: India commits to 60% non-fossil power capacity and a carbon sink of up to 4 billion tonnes by 2035, while the EU has a binding 90% absolute cut for 2040 from 1990 levels. Critics use the EU target to argue India's pledges are conservative.
source: Beyond emissions intensity, India will commit to 60% non-fossil fuel power capacity and create a carbon sink of up to 4 billion tonnes by 2035 in its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC).

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's updated NDC approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2026:
items: It explicitly prioritises mangrove restoration, glacier monitoring in the Himalayas and a single national-level Heat Action Plan in place of state-level plans.
Compared with earlier NDC updates, it places less emphasis on adaptation and climate-resilient infrastructure.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the NDC prioritises state-level Heat Action Plans, not a single national-level plan. Statement 2 is wrong because, unlike previous updates, this NDC leans heavily into climate-resilient infrastructure. The aim of these adaptation measures is to buffer the economy against extreme weather.
source: It explicitly prioritizes mangrove restoration, glacier monitoring in the Himalayas, and state-level Heat Action Plans to buffer the economy against extreme weather.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the 2023 audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of the first three phases of the UDAN scheme:
items: It found that 52% of the awarded routes never started operations.
It found that a majority of the routes that did fly survived beyond the three-year subsidy window.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because only 7% of the routes that flew survived beyond the three-year subsidy window. The audit covered 774 awarded routes and also found that fifteen airports went inactive during the period.
source: A 2023 audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of the first three phases found that 52% of 774 awarded routes never started operations.

prompt: The regional connectivity scheme UDAN (Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik), whose modified version the Cabinet approved in March 2026, was originally launched in which year?
explain: The original UDAN scheme was launched in 2016. Over nine years it operationalised 663 routes across 95 airports and carried 16.2 million passengers.
source: Since its launch in 2016, the original UDAN (Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik, or ‘let the common citizen fly’) scheme has a patchy record.

prompt: In March 2026, which body issued an advisory barring hotels and restaurants from adding default 'LPG charges' or 'gas surcharges' to customers' bills?
options: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board
