explain: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) held that fuel and energy costs are operational expenses that must be built into menu prices. It warned that listing them as separate line items amounts to an unfair trade practice under the Consumer Protection Act.
source: The CCPA ruled that fuel and energy costs are operational expenses that must be baked into menu prices, and warned that separate line items amount to unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act.

prompt: In March 2026, the Iran war that broke out on 28 February put pressure on India's economy. Consider the following statements:
items: The Centre cut excise duties on petrol and diesel by INR 10 per litre to help oil companies.
India imports about 60% of its oil requirement.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The excise cut is correct, but India imports 85% of its oil, not about 60%. That dependence makes every escalation in West Asia a macro event for India, and the petroleum minister warned the cut would mean a huge hit to tax revenues.
source: New Delhi cut excise duties on petrol and diesel by INR 10 per litre to help out oil companies.

prompt: In March 2026, the RBI moved to curb an arbitrage trade that was pressuring the rupee. In this trade, banks offset large onshore dollar purchases with opposite positions in which offshore market?
explain: Banks netted onshore dollar buys against offsetting positions in the offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) market. This let them run arbitrage books estimated at USD 10-18 billion while staying within limits. The onshore dollar buying pushed the domestic price of the USD up and the INR down.
source: Banks would offset large onshore dollar buys with opposite positions in the offshore, non-deliverable forward (NDF) market.

prompt: In March 2026, India eased restrictions on public sector procurement from China. Consider the following statements:
items: Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) was allowed to source 21 types of critical equipment from Chinese suppliers.
Chinese bidders in state contracts must still register for political and security clearance.
State firms other than BHEL and SAIL were permitted to procure coal-gasification equipment from China.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Chinese bidders in state contracts no longer need political and security clearance registration. The order also gave Steel Authority of India (SAIL) clearance for certain components, moving from broad policy to named firms with specific procurement lists.
source: Chinese bidders in state contracts no longer need political and security clearance registration.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the easing of India–China commercial ties:
items: February 2026 — Easing of power equipment import curbs
March 2026 — Relaxation of FDI rules for Chinese-linked investments
August 2025 — Prime Minister Modi's first visit to China in seven years
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three are correctly matched: power equipment import curbs were eased in February 2026, FDI rules for Chinese-linked investments were relaxed in March 2026, and Modi visited China in August 2025. Since that visit, direct flights have resumed and visa rules for Chinese professionals have loosened.
source: New Delhi began easing power equipment import curbs in February, then relaxed FDI rules for Chinese-linked investments earlier this month.

prompt: In March 2026, India approved USD 25 billion in military purchases. Consider the following pairs of items and the service they were approved for:
items: S-400 missile systems — Indian Air Force
Dhanush guns — Indian Air Force
Su-30 engine overhauls — Indian Army
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Only the S-400 pair is correct. Dhanush guns went to the Army, and Su-30 engine overhauls went to the Air Force. The package was India's second major defence approval in as many months.
source: The Air Force gets S-400s, medium transport aircraft, unmanned attack drones, and Su-30 engine overhauls.

prompt: In March 2026, alongside a USD 25 billion package of defence approvals, India signed a separate USD 47 million contract with Russia. Which system did this contract cover?
explain: The separate USD 47 million contract with Moscow covers Tunguska air defence systems. It was signed alongside approvals that also included Russian S-400 missile systems for the Air Force.
source: A separate USD 47 million contract was also signed with Moscow, covering Tunguska air defence systems.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's defence procurement in the fiscal year 2025-26, as reported in March 2026:
items: India approved 55 proposals worth 6.73 trillion rupees (USD 71 billion), a historic high.
India signed contracts for 503 proposals amounting to 6.73 trillion rupees.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The contracts signed for 503 proposals amounted to 2.28 trillion rupees, while 6.73 trillion rupees was the value of the 55 approved proposals. The spending follows the four-day clash with Pakistan in 2025, which exposed gaps in drone saturation, battlefield communications and rapid deployment.
source: In all, India has approved 55 proposals worth 6.73 trillion rupees (USD 71 billion) and signed contracts for another 503 proposals amounting to 2.28 trillion rupees in this fiscal year, marking a historic high.

prompt: In March 2026, the Ministry of Power directed Tata Power's Mundra plant to start operating to prevent summer blackouts. Under which provision was this direction issued?
options: Section 3 of the Energy Conservation Act
Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act
explain: The government invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to force the 4,000 MW Mundra plant into action by 1 April 2026. The move was part of an emergency playbook to offset gas shortages caused by the West Asia conflict.
source: The government invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to force Tata Power’s 4,000 MW Mundra plant into action by April 1

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Ministry of Power's plan, announced in March 2026, to meet summer electricity demand:
items: Gas accounts for about 10% of India's electricity generation.
The Ministry is accelerating clearances to commission wind and battery energy storage systems.
Maintenance on thermal plants is being deferred to keep 10,000 MW on the grid.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first statement is wrong: gas provides only 2% of India's power, though it supplies 10 GW during peak demand or heatwaves. The Ministry is also pushing up coal inventory and tweaking rules to encourage industries to use captive power.
source: Gas provides only 2% of India’s power, but it provides 10 GW during peak-demand periods or heatwaves.

prompt: In March 2026, India proposed amendments to its IT rules concerning internet platforms. Consider the following statements:
items: Safe harbour is the legal shield that protects platforms from liability for user-posted content.
Under the rules in force before the proposal, IT ministry advisories on deepfake labelling functioned as guidance without legal teeth.
The proposed amendment would treat non-compliance with ministry advisories as a failure to meet safe harbour conditions.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. Under the current rules, the IT ministry's advisories are guidance without legal teeth, and the proposal would make them binding by linking compliance to safe harbour, the shield protecting platforms from liability for user content. The draft rules were published for public feedback, with comments open until 14 April 2026.
source: Under the current rules, the IT ministry's advisories on issues like deepfake labelling and content takedowns function as guidance without legal teeth.

prompt: In February 2026, the AI Impact Summit, attended by the heads of Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, was held in which city?
explain: Sundar Pichai, Sam Altman and Dario Amodei all attended the summit in New Delhi. Global AI companies are competing for Indian users, with free offers and bundling deals with telecom operators Airtel and Jio.
source: At the AI Impact Summit in February, Sundar Pichai, Sam Altman, and Dario Amodei all showed up in New Delhi.

prompt: In March 2026, India approved 29 proposals for domestic manufacture of components such as PCBs, capacitors and rare-earth magnets. Under which scheme were these proposals approved?
options: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for IT Hardware
explain: The package was approved under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and covers PCBs, rare-earth magnets, capacitors, relays and EV inductors. To qualify for incentives, companies must also develop design and engineering capabilities in India.
source: The INR 7,104 crore (USD 751 million) package under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme covers PCBs, rare-earth magnets, capacitors, relays, and EV inductors.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of components and the share of domestic demand they are projected to meet under the electronics component proposals approved in March 2026:
items: Capacitors — 61% of demand
Relays — 100% with export surplus
Rare-earth magnets — 35% of domestic demand
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Rare-earth magnets are projected to reach 25% of domestic demand, up from near zero. The 35% figure is the current domestic capacitor supply, which is set to rise to 61%. Every component on the list is one where China currently holds leverage.
source: Rare-earth magnets will rise to 25% of domestic demand, up from near zero.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the electronics component manufacturing proposals approved by India in March 2026:
items: The approved package was worth INR 7,104 crore (USD 751 million).
Before this round, India's electronics manufacturing was concentrated in the assembly of finished products.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements are correct. The INR 7,104 crore package targets inputs such as PCBs and relays rather than finished-product assembly. Earlier schemes rewarded production volume, while this one ties subsidies to design and engineering capability built in India.
source: Until now, India's electronics manufacturing has been concentrated in assembly of finished products.

prompt: In March 2026, the West Asia conflict disrupted India's fertiliser imports ahead of the kharif season. Consider the following statements:
items: India imports about 60% of its di-ammonium phosphate (DAP).
Oman is India's biggest source of imported urea.
China's suspension of phosphate exports was in place until at least August 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: India imports 60% of its DAP, Oman is the biggest urea source, and China's phosphate export suspension runs until at least August. Both Oman and Saudi Arabia, the top DAP supplier, ship through the Strait of Hormuz, so the government held talks with Russia, Belarus and Morocco to fill the gap.
source: Saudi Arabia is the top DAP supplier; Oman is the biggest urea source.

prompt: In March 2026, the West Asia conflict disrupted roughly half of India's DAP and urea imports. India's leading Gulf suppliers of both fertilisers ship through which waterway?
explain: Both Saudi Arabia, the top DAP supplier, and Oman, the biggest urea source, ship through the Strait of Hormuz. Alternative cargoes from Russia and Belarus take weeks longer than Gulf routes.
source: Both ship through the Strait of Hormuz.

prompt: As of March 2026, before the West Asia conflict began, what had India's fertiliser subsidy bill for 2026-27 been set at?
explain: The 2026-27 subsidy bill was set at INR 1.71 lakh crore (USD 20 billion) before the war. Urea prices have since surged about 50%, and rising import costs are expected to push the bill higher because the government shields farmers from global price spikes.
source: But the subsidy bill for 2026-27 was already set at INR 1.71 lakh crore (USD 20 billion) before the war; rising import costs will push it higher.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the assembly elections held in five states and Union Territories in April 2026:
items: Kerala, Assam and Puducherry voted on the same day.
West Bengal voted in a single phase.
Results for all five assemblies were scheduled to be declared on the same day.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: West Bengal voted in two phases, on April 23 and 29, so statement 2 is wrong. Kerala, Assam and Puducherry voted on April 9, Tamil Nadu on April 23, and results for all five were due on May 4, with roughly 174 million voters covered.
source: West Bengal votes in two phases on April 23 and 29.

prompt: In 2022, the Supreme Court flagged the problem of electoral freebies and asked which body to act on it?
explain: The Supreme Court flagged the freebie problem in 2022 and asked the Election Commission to act. By the 2026 state election cycle, TBB noted that the practice had spread from Tamil Nadu to parties across states, including the BJP.
source: The Supreme Court flagged the freebie problem in 2022 and asked the Election Commission to act.

prompt: In January 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that Tiger Global's units used for its Flipkart stake sale to Walmart were mere "conduits", stripping them of treaty protections. In which country were these units based?
explain: The Supreme Court held that Tiger Global's Mauritius units were conduits and denied treaty protection on the USD 1.6 billion stake sale. The ruling sparked fears that tax officers would reopen legacy deals routed through tax havens.
source: In January, the Supreme Court ruled Tiger Global’s Mauritius units were mere "conduits," stripping treaty protections from their USD 1.6 billion Flipkart stake sale to Walmart.

prompt: In April 2026, a clarification was issued on the applicability of General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR) to foreign investments. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It was issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes.
Investments made before 1 April 2017 are exempt from GAAR.
The protection depends on the exit structure of a transaction rather than the date of investment.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong: the protection covers the investment date, not the exit structure, and GAAR can still apply to a post-2017 transaction lacking commercial substance. The CBDT's clarification took effect immediately.
source: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) clarified that investments made before April 1, 2017 are exempt from General Anti-Avoidance Rules (GAAR).

prompt: In March 2026, which body opened a one-year window for Special Economic Zone (SEZ) manufacturers to sell goods into the domestic market at concessional customs duty rates?
options: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
explain: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) opened the window, citing global trade disruptions. It lets SEZ units clear goods into the Domestic Tariff Area at reduced duty rates.
source: the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) opened a one-year window for Special Economic Zone (SEZ) manufacturers to sell goods into the domestic market at concessional customs duty rates

prompt: Consider the following statements about the concessional window for SEZ units to sell into the Domestic Tariff Area, opened in March 2026:
items: Domestic sales are capped at 30% of a unit's best export year over the previous three financial years.
Goods must have at least 20% value addition over inputs.
The window runs for two years, until 31 March 2028.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the window is for one year, from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027. Only units operational by 31 March 2025 qualify, and sensitive sectors are excluded entirely.
source: Domestic sales are capped at 30% of a unit's best export year over the previous three financial years.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the measures taken by the Reserve Bank of India between 30 March and 1 April 2026 to curb speculation against the rupee:
items: The RBI capped banks' net open rupee positions at USD 100 million.
The RBI banned rupee non-deliverable forwards.
The RBI barred companies from rebooking cancelled forward contracts.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the RBI first capped banks' net open rupee positions at USD 100 million, then banned rupee non-deliverable forwards and barred companies from rebooking cancelled forward contracts after banks offloaded positions to corporates and hedge funds. The rupee then surged 1.8% to 93.10 per dollar on 2 April 2026, its best session since 2013.
source: the central bank followed up on Wednesday by banning rupee non-deliverable forwards and barring companies from rebooking cancelled forward contracts.

prompt: In an order reported in April 2026, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) deferred stricter penalties for wind and solar generators until April 2027. Under which framework are generators fined when actual power supply misses scheduled targets?
explain: Under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism, generators pay penalties when actual supply misses scheduled targets. Industry groups warned that the intermittent nature of renewables could cause 48% revenue losses under stricter rules.
source: Under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM), generators are fined when actual power supply misses scheduled targets.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the CERC order on the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) reported in April 2026:
items: The DSM Regulations were introduced in 2024 and commenced on 31 March 2026.
The order keeps the penalty buffer known as the "X" value at 100% in FY2026-27 and reduces it to 0% by 2031.
The order places the largest annual reduction in the "X" value in FY2027-28.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the order slows the annual phase-down and leaves the largest reduction for FY2030-31. Once the buffer reaches 0%, renewable projects face the same penalties as fossil-fuel generators, and back-loading the cuts gives operators time to improve forecasting and for storage to mature.
source: this new order slows the annual phase-down of this buffer and leaves the largest reduction for FY2030-2031.

prompt: In April 2026, India reported an all-time high in its defence exports for FY 2025-26. What was the value of these exports?
explain: Defence exports reached INR 38,424 crore (USD 4.6 billion) in FY26, a 62.66% year-on-year jump. The story credits global volatility, in Ukraine and the Caucasus, and the Atmanirbhar Bharat push for the rise.
source: India’s defence exports hit an all-time high of INR 38,424 crore (USD 4.6 billion) in FY26, marking a 62.66% year-on-year jump.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's defence exports in FY 2025-26:
items: Exports by government-owned firms grew by about 151%, giving them more than half of the total.
Exports by private firms grew at a faster rate than those of government-owned firms.
The number of active defence exporters grew to 145.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Private firms grew 14%, far below the 151% leap by government-owned firms, which took a 54.84% share. India now ships defence hardware to more than 80 nations.
source: Government-owned firms led the way, with exports leaping 151% to claim a 54.84% market share.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's sugar sector, as reported in April 2026:
items: India is the world's second-largest producer of sugar.
India's expected sugar output for the season under way exceeds its annual domestic consumption.
The government had approved exports of 2 million tons of sugar, expecting a surplus.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. India expects only 28 million tons this season against annual consumption of 29 million tons, so output falls short of demand for the second year running. The 2 million tons of exports were approved on a surplus that never arrived, and the national stockpile is now shrinking.
source: The government recently greenlit 2 million tons in exports, betting on a surplus that never arrived.

prompt: In April 2026, almost all sugar mills had shut down for the season weeks ahead of schedule because of poor crops in which pair of sugar-rich states?
explain: Poor cane crops forced mills in Maharashtra and Karnataka to close early. As a result, India expects 28 million tons of sugar against a forecast of 31 million tons.
source: In the sugar-rich states of Maharashtra and Karnataka, almost all mills have already shut down for the season weeks ahead of schedule.

prompt: In April 2026, a Russian parliamentary delegation met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh. Consider the following statements:
items: The Russian delegation was led by the First Deputy Chairperson of Russia's State Duma.
The two sides discussed restarting the India-Russia Inter-Parliamentary Commission, which last met in 2021.
Russia will host the BRICS Parliamentary Forum in 2026 as the bloc's chair.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the delegation was led by Vladimir Yakushev of Russia's Federation Council, not the State Duma; the Inter-Parliamentary Commission last met in 2018, not 2021; and India, not Russia, will host the BRICS Parliamentary Forum this year as the bloc's chair. The two sides also flagged artificial intelligence, space research and clean energy as new areas for cooperation.
source: The two sides discussed restarting the Inter-Parliamentary Commission, which last met in 2018, and flagged artificial intelligence, space research and clean energy as new areas for cooperation.

prompt: As of April 2026, roughly 40-50% of India's energy needs transited which waterway, whose closure after a conflict that began in February 2026 squeezed Indian energy security?
explain: The story says 40-50% of India's energy needs transit the Strait of Hormuz, and India imports 85% of its crude. Brent crude hit USD 109.77 while Iran kept the strait blocked, roughly 50% higher than when the conflict started on 28 February.
source: India imports 85% of its crude, with 40-50% of its energy needs transiting Hormuz.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's economic position during the Strait of Hormuz closure between late February and early April 2026:
items: India imports about 85% of its crude oil.
India's foreign exchange reserves rose by over USD 30 billion as capital flowed in.
The RBI banned non-deliverable forwards to curb speculative trades in the rupee.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Forex reserves fell by USD 30.5 billion as the RBI intervened to defend the rupee, and foreign portfolio investors pulled out a record Rs 1.22 lakh crore in March. The RBI also capped banks' rupee positions.
source: Forex reserves have fallen USD 30.5 billion since late February as the RBI intervened to defend the rupee.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) readings for March 2026:
items: The Composite PMI rose to its highest reading in nearly three and a half years.
The HSBC India Services PMI fell from its February level but stayed above the 50-mark that separates expansion from contraction.
International orders for services firms reached their second-highest level since the index began tracking them in 2014.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: the Composite PMI dropped to 57.0 from 58.9, its weakest reading in nearly three and a half years. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Services PMI slipped to 57.5 from 58.1 as the West Asia conflict weighed on domestic demand, even as foreign orders surged.
source: The broader Composite PMI dropped to 57.0 from 58.9, its weakest reading in nearly three and a half years.

prompt: In April 2026, the Indian-flagged LPG tankers Green Sanvi and Green Asha made news for safely crossing which maritime chokepoint during a conflict that began in February 2026?
explain: The two tankers cleared the Strait of Hormuz, bringing to eight the Indian gas carriers that had crossed it since the conflict began on 28 February 2026. Green Sanvi carried about 46,650 tonnes of LPG to Mumbai and Green Asha about 20,000 tonnes to Dahej in Gujarat.
source: Two more Indian-flagged LPG tankers, Green Sanvi and Green Asha, have cleared the Strait of Hormuz, bringing the total number of Indian gas carriers to navigate the chokepoint to eight since the conflict began on February 28.

prompt: In March 2026, amid strained LPG supplies, the Government of India directed refineries to maximise cooking gas output by invoking which law?
explain: The government invoked the Essential Commodities Act in early March 2026 to direct refineries to maximise cooking gas output. It also capped commercial LPG supply at 20% of normal, while India coordinated passage of its vessels through Iranian-monitored waters.
source: directed refineries to maximise cooking gas output after invoking the Essential Commodities Act in early March.

prompt: In April 2026, as the Middle East conflict pushed up energy costs, the Union government reviewed its fiscal position. Consider the following statements:
items: The government's fiscal deficit target for FY27 is 4.3%.
The government said budget projections would change only if global pressures lasted beyond three months.
The government passed higher crude prices on to consumers by raising retail fuel rates.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. With four state assembly elections in April 2026, the government absorbed high crude prices through subsidies rather than raising retail rates, which adds an INR 1.83 trillion burden to the federal budget. To hold the 4.3% target, it planned to trim budgets of ministries with low spending capacity and protect capital expenditure on roads, railways and airports.
source: With four state assembly elections this month, the government is absorbing high crude prices via subsidies rather than raising retail rates.

prompt: In April 2026, amid a cooking gas shortage, the Union Food Secretary set out the government's position on sugar and edible oils. Consider the following statements:
items: India's annual sugar consumption is about 29 million tonnes, and output was expected to fall below it for a second straight year.
The government ruled out diverting sugar toward ethanol production to offset crude oil disruption.
The government said it had no plans to cut import duties on edible oils.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra said India has no plans to curb sugar exports or cut edible oil import duties, and ruled out diverting sugar to ethanol, while output is expected to fall below 29 million tonnes of consumption for a second straight year. Falling demand from shuttered eateries is easing pressure, with edible oil imports down nearly 9% in March to 1.2 million tonnes.
source: Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra said India has no plans to curb sugar exports or cut import duties on edible oils, despite output falling short of forecasts for a second consecutive year (we covered it here).

prompt: In April 2026, the Union government approved the 1,200 MW Kalai-II hydroelectric project in Arunachal Pradesh. It is the first hydropower project on which river?
explain: Kalai-II is the first hydropower project on the Lohit river, opening an entirely new basin. It sits in Anjaw, a border district, and is part of India's push to establish prior use across the Brahmaputra system.
source: Kalai-II is the first hydropower project on the Lohit river, opening an entirely new basin.

prompt: In April 2026, the Union government approved the Kamala and Kalai-II hydroelectric projects in Arunachal Pradesh. Consider the following statements about the benefits to the state:
items: Arunachal Pradesh holds a 26% equity stake in the Kamala project.
Arunachal Pradesh receives 12% free power from both plants.
An additional 1% of power is earmarked for a Local Area Development Fund.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct as stated in the approval terms. New Delhi is also funding over 225 km of roads and bridges across the two project sites.
source: Arunachal Pradesh holds a 26% equity stake in the Kamala project and receives 12% free power from both plants, plus an additional 1% earmarked for a Local Area Development Fund.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the hydroelectric projects in Arunachal Pradesh approved in April 2026:
items: Kamala project — 1,200 MW
Kalai-II project — 1,720 MW
Flood moderation component of the Kamala project — INR 40,175 crore
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are wrong. The story gives Kamala as 1,720 MW and Kalai-II as 1,200 MW, and puts the flood moderation component at INR 4,744 crore, with INR 40,175 crore being the total approved for both projects. The plants are meant to manage peak demand and steady a grid increasingly reliant on solar and wind.
source: two hydroelectric projects in Arunachal Pradesh: the 1,720 MW Kamala and 1,200 MW Kalai-II plants.

prompt: In April 2026, India was set to receive its first Iranian oil shipment since 2019. Consider the following statements about this shipment:
items: It followed a 30-day US waiver allowing countries to buy Iranian oil already at sea.
The cargo was bought by a privately owned Indian refiner.
The tanker carrying the cargo was heading to India's west coast.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The state-run Indian Oil Corp bought the cargo aboard the VLCC Jaya, which was originally headed for China and is now heading to India's east coast. The waiver covered roughly 170 million barrels loaded by March 20 and discharged by April 19.
source: State-run Indian Oil Corp (IOC) snagged the cargo aboard the VLCC Jaya, which was originally headed for China and is currently heading to India’s east coast.

prompt: In April 2026, which country brokered a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran in the West Asia conflict?
explain: Pakistan brokered the two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran in the conflict that began on 28 February 2026. The Congress party argued that India's lack of any mediating role, while Pakistan stepped in, undercut years of efforts to isolate Islamabad internationally.
source: The Congress party attacked PM Modi's foreign policy after Pakistan brokered a two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran in the ongoing West Asia conflict.

prompt: As of April 2026, Iran had no embassy in Washington. Which country had represented some Iranian diplomatic interests there?
explain: Pakistan has represented some Iranian diplomatic interests in Washington, where Tehran has no embassy. This, along with its long border with Iran, placed Pakistan better than India to broker a ceasefire between Iran and the US in April 2026.
source: Pakistan has also represented some Iranian diplomatic interests in Washington, where Tehran has no embassy.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of legislatures that voted on 9 April 2026 in the opening phase of the assembly elections, and the number of seats contested:
items: Assam — 126 seats
Kerala — 140 seats
Puducherry — 30 seats
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three are correct: Assam has 126 seats, Kerala 140 and Puducherry 30, for a total of 296 in the first phase. Tamil Nadu and West Bengal voted later in April, and counting for all five assemblies was set for 4 May 2026.
source: A total of 296 seats are in play: 126 in Assam, 140 in Kerala, and 30 in Puducherry.

prompt: In April 2026, India's Civil Aviation Ministry cut landing and parking charges at all domestic airports by 25% for three months. Which body will adjust any resulting airport revenue shortfalls in the next five-year tariff cycle?
explain: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority will offset any revenue shortfall from the cut in the next five-year tariff cycle. The cut is expected to save airlines roughly INR 400 crore and is part of measures to shield carriers from the West Asia crisis, during which New Delhi capped the pass-through of fuel price rises to domestic airlines at 25%.
source: The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority will adjust any airport revenue shortfalls in the next five-year tariff cycle.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the measures India set out at an inter-ministerial briefing in April 2026 on the Strait of Hormuz disruption:
items: Excise duty on petrol and diesel was cut.
Export levies were imposed on diesel and aviation fuel.
Customs duty was zeroed on 40 petrochemical products to protect fertiliser inputs.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because customs duty on the 40 petrochemical products was zeroed to protect pharmaceutical inputs, not fertiliser inputs. The excise cut and the export levies on diesel and aviation fuel were meant to keep domestic supply intact while retail prices stayed unchanged.
source: Customs duty has been zeroed on 40 petrochemical products to protect pharmaceutical inputs.

prompt: In April 2026, India briefed that its missions were moving Indian nationals stranded in Iran out of the region through which two countries named at the briefing?
explain: The briefing named Armenia and Azerbaijan as transit routes for Indians stranded in Iran. With airspace closed in Kuwait and Israel, evacuations were functioning through third countries.
source: Indian missions have been facilitating the movement of nationals out of the region, including through Armenia and Azerbaijan for those stranded in Iran.

prompt: In March 2026, which energy company declared force majeure on long-term gas contracts after Iranian strikes knocked out roughly 17% of its country's export capacity?
explain: QatarEnergy declared force majeure on its long-term gas contracts after the Iranian strikes on Qatar. In April 2026, Petroleum Minister Puri visited Qatar to press for priority LNG deliveries to India.
source: Petroleum Minister Puri is in Qatar today to press for priority Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) delivery after QatarEnergy declared force majeure on long-term gas contracts last month, following Iranian strikes that knocked out roughly 17% of Qatar's export capacity.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the World Bank's April 2026 growth forecast for India:
items: It raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.6% from its October estimate of 6.3%.
It cited recently signed free trade agreements with the EU and UK among the reasons for the upgrade.
The Reserve Bank of India's FY27 growth projection is lower than the World Bank's.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The RBI is more bullish than the World Bank, at 6.9%, while Moody's is more cautious at 6.0%. Even after the upgrade, 6.6% marks a slowdown from FY26's 7.6%, with the West Asia conflict the primary drag.
source: The World Bank raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 6.6%, up from its October estimate of 6.3%, citing robust domestic demand and recently signed free trade agreements with the EU and UK.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the windfall taxes on fuel exports revised by the Ministry of Finance in April 2026:
items: The windfall tax on diesel exports was raised from 21.5 to 55.5 rupees per litre.
Alongside the export taxes, the government raised excise duties on fuel to curb domestic consumption.
The windfall levy on these exports was first introduced in March 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because New Delhi cut excise duties and capped monthly ATF price hikes to shield the domestic economy. The initial levy came on 26 March 2026 to curb an export surge, and the 11 April revision raised the tax on ATF exports from 29.5 to 42 rupees.
source: Effective immediately, the tax on diesel jumped from 21.5 to 55.5 rupees per litre, while ATF rose from 29.5 to 42 rupees.

prompt: In March 2026, Indian refiners raised diesel exports by 20%, which prompted higher windfall taxes in April 2026. Which region were these exports mainly headed to?
explain: Refiners chased higher overseas margins, sending diesel exports mainly to Southeast Asia. With the West Asia crisis throttling global oil flows, the government responded with export taxes to keep domestic stocks secure.
source: Indian refiners boosted diesel exports by 20% in March, primarily to Southeast Asia.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's rice export policy as of April 2026:
items: India renewed a six-month waiver on mandatory inspection certificates for rice exports to non-EU European countries.
The waiver was first introduced in October 2025.
India's rice exports reached USD 12.95 billion in 2024-25, up 62% since 2014.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. In April 2026 India renewed the six-month waiver, extending a policy first introduced in October 2025, and rice exports hit USD 12.95 billion in 2024-25, up 62% since 2014. The Export Inspection Council certificate remains compulsory for EU member states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.
source: Last Friday, New Delhi renewed a six-month waiver on mandatory inspection certificates for rice exports to non-EU European countries, extending a policy first introduced in October 2025.

prompt: Under India's rice export policy renewed in April 2026, the Export Inspection Council (EIC) certificate remains compulsory for rice exports to which of the following countries?
explain: The EIC certificate remains compulsory for EU member states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, while all other European countries are exempt. TBB notes the exemption targets markets in Eurasia and the Balkans that do not demand Brussels-level paperwork.
source: The Export Inspection Council (EIC) certificate remains compulsory for EU member states, the UK, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland.

prompt: In April 2026, the government brought amendments to the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam before a special session of Parliament. Consider the following pairs relating to the proposed Lok Sabha seat structure:
items: Total Lok Sabha seats — 543
Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes — 136
Seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes — 47
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Pairs 1 and 3 are wrong: 543 is the current Lok Sabha strength, which would expand to 816, and 47 is the current number of Scheduled Tribe seats, which would rise to 70. Only pair 2 is correct, as Scheduled Caste seats would rise from 84 to 136, with one-third of SC and ST seats and 273 seats in all going to women.
source: Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (India's constitutionally recognised disadvantaged communities) also increase, from 84 to 136 and 47 to 70 respectively, with one-third of each reserved for women.

prompt: The amendments to the Women's Reservation Act taken up by Parliament in April 2026 aim to bring women's reservation into force in time for which general election?
explain: Using 2011 Census data lets reservation apply in the 2029 general election. The 2023 law had tied implementation to a future census and delimitation, pushing enforcement to roughly 2034.
source: using 2011 Census data instead to get women's reservation in place for the 2029 general election.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's renewable energy transmission constraints, as reported in April 2026:
items: About 60 GW of clean energy projects in Rajasthan were stuck because the grid could not keep pace with construction.
The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has identified 450 GW of renewable potential nationwide.
Transmission plans cover about 300 GW of the nationwide renewable potential.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because transmission plans cover only 240 GW of the 450 GW potential identified by the ministry. The gap shows that transmission planning has not kept pace with booming generation, which leaves projects at risk of becoming stranded assets.
source: CTUIL warns that while the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has identified 450 GW of renewable potential nationwide, transmission plans only cover 240 GW.

prompt: In April 2026, which body admitted in a filing that it lacked infrastructure for nearly half of the 130 GW of grid connectivity applications in Rajasthan?
explain: The Central Transmission Utility (CTUIL) made the admission in an April 10 filing. The crunch was severe enough that regulators told one developer, Saurya Urja, it could withdraw its application and claw back its bank guarantees.
source: In an April 10 filing, the Central Transmission Utility (CTUIL) admitted it lacks the infrastructure for nearly half of the 130 GW of connectivity applications in the state.

prompt: In April 2026, factory workers in Noida protested over rising living costs amid fuel shortages linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Consider the following statements:
items: India is the world's second-largest importer of LPG.
In early April 2026, Haryana ordered a 35% hike in minimum wages after unrest in the auto hub of Manesar.
The government cut household cooking gas allocations to protect gas supplies to industry.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. The government cut industrial gas allocations to protect household cooking supplies, which squeezed businesses and workers. Haryana's hike raised its wage floor to INR 19,000 a month, against about INR 13,000 earned by Noida factory workers.
source: The government has cut industrial gas allocations to protect household cooking supplies, squeezing businesses and workers simultaneously.

prompt: In April 2026, two very large crude carriers loaded with Iranian oil reached Indian ports. Consider the following statements:
items: India had stopped buying Iranian crude in May 2019 under US pressure.
Indian refiners resumed purchases under a permanent US sanctions waiver.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the US sanctions waiver was temporary and was due to expire on 19 April 2026. The cargoes were the first Iranian oil to reach Indian ports in seven years, arriving as the US began enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
source: India stopped buying Iranian crude in May 2019 under US pressure.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the change of government in Bihar in April 2026:
items: In the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, the BJP emerged as the single largest party with 89 of 243 seats.
Outgoing Chief Minister Nitish Kumar moved to the Lok Sabha before resigning.
The transition gave the BJP direct control of Bihar for the first time.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Nitish Kumar was elected to the Rajya Sabha, the upper house, on 16 March 2026 and took his oath on 10 April before resigning as chief minister. The BJP had kept him as chief minister after the 2025 NDA landslide for alliance continuity.
source: the BJP emerged as the single largest party with 89 of 243 seats but kept Nitish as CM for alliance continuity.

prompt: Who was elected leader of the BJP legislature party and sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar in April 2026?
explain: Deputy Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary was unanimously elected BJP legislature party leader and took oath on 15 April 2026, a day after Nitish Kumar resigned. Positioned as the BJP's OBC face, he began in the RJD in 1999 and joined the BJP in 2017.
source: Deputy CM Samrat Choudhary was unanimously elected BJP legislature party leader and takes oath as Bihar's chief minister today.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway inaugurated in April 2026:
items: It is a 210-km corridor designed to cut travel time between Delhi and Uttarakhand from 6 hours to 2.5 hours.
It features a 12-kilometre elevated wildlife corridor to protect the Shivalik forest ecosystem.
It includes a 340-metre tunnel near Delhi.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The 340-metre tunnel is near Dehradun, not Delhi, and is meant to improve connectivity to the Himalayan foothills. The 12-km elevated wildlife corridor is described as Asia's largest.
source: The 210-km corridor, built at a cost of approximately ₹13,000 crore ($14mn), features Asia’s largest 12-kilometre elevated wildlife corridor to protect the Shivalik forest ecosystem.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's trade data released in April 2026:
items: India's trade deficit for March 2026 narrowed to a nine-month low of USD 20.67 billion.
India's trade deficit for FY 2025-26 was at a three-year high of USD 119 billion.
In FY 2025-26, India's export growth outpaced its import growth.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because annual imports grew 6.5% while exports grew only 4.22%, which widened the FY26 deficit to USD 119 billion. The March narrowing came mainly from a sharp fall in imports, especially energy.
source: Despite this monthly dip, the financial year 2025-2026 (FY26) deficit sits at a three-year high of USD 119 billion, as annual imports (+6.5%) continue to outpace export growth (+4.22%).

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's exports to the United States in March 2026:
items: Shipments to the US rose 17.4% to USD 8.02 billion.
The rise followed a US Supreme Court ruling that cut punitive tariffs from 50% to 10%.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements are correct. The increase was led by textiles and engineering goods after the US Supreme Court ruling reduced the 50% tariffs to 10%, even as exports to the Middle East fell by 57.95%.
source: This surge in textiles and engineering goods follows a US Supreme Court ruling that slashed punitive 50% tariffs down to 10%, which we covered here.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's gem and jewellery exports in the financial year 2025-26, as reported in April 2026:
items: Exports declined during the year, marking the sector's worst performance since 2011.
The United States remained India's largest jewellery export market.
Under the India–US trade framework, diamonds and coloured gemstones attract zero duty.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the UAE overtook the US as India's top jewellery export market. Exports fell 3.32% to USD 27.72 billion, mainly because of US tariff pressure. The trade framework restores gems and jewellery tariffs to 18%, with zero duty on diamonds and coloured gemstones.
source: The UAE has overtaken the US as India's top jewellery export market.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to growth in India's gem and jewellery exports in FY 2025-26:
items: Exports to the UAE — 22%
Exports to Australia — 38%
Silver jewellery exports — 6.27%
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Silver jewellery exports surged 52%. The 6.27% figure belongs to studded gold jewellery. The growth in exports to the UAE and Australia was propped up by free trade agreements.
source: Silver jewellery took the trend, surging 52% on rising affordability and global demand.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Wholesale Price Index (WPI) based inflation for March 2026:
items: It was the highest reading since January 2024.
More than half of the 22 industrial groups in the manufacturing sub-index posted price increases.
The manufacturing sub-index accounts for over 64% of the WPI.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the March 2026 reading was the highest since January 2023, not January 2024. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, as 16 of the 22 manufacturing groups posted hikes and the sub-index makes up over 64% of the WPI. WPI inflation rose to 3.88% in March 2026 from 2.13% in February, driven largely by an 8.77% spike in mineral oils.
source: The manufacturing sub-index, comprising over 64% of the WPI, saw 16 of 22 industrial groups post hikes.

prompt: Which of the following was the main driver of the rise in India's WPI inflation in March 2026?
explain: Mineral oils rose 8.77% and pushed the fuel and power index up 4.13%. Electricity prices fell 5.07%, and food and non-food articles eased month-on-month.
source: The fuel and power index climbed 4.13%, supercharged by an 8.77% spike in mineral oils.

prompt: In April 2026, India refused to commit further capital to a cobalt and copper exploration block until the host country guarantees long-term mining rights. Which country allocated this block to India?
explain: India paused investment in the Zambian block, which Zambia allocated in 2025, until Lusaka guarantees long-term tenure. Geologists have finished initial fieldwork, but New Delhi will not move to private-sector extraction without secure rights.
source: India has hit pause on Zambian critical mineral investment, refusing to commit further capital until Lusaka guarantees long-term mining rights.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's critical mineral position, as reported in April 2026:
items: The block Zambia allocated to India for cobalt and copper exploration covers about 9,000 square kilometres.
The 2018 closure of Vedanta's Sterlite Copper smelter turned India from a copper exporter into an importer.
India's copper imports fell 4% in the fiscal year ending March 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: copper imports rose 4% to 1.2 million tonnes in the fiscal year ending March 2025. India is also pursuing government-to-government deals across Africa and Latin America, including an initial agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo.
source: India's copper imports rose 4% to 1.2 million tonnes in the fiscal year ending March 2025.

prompt: In April 2026, a Japan-led 'AZEC Plus' virtual summit launched the 'Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience' (POWERR Asia). What is this framework primarily meant for?
explain: POWERR Asia is a roughly USD 10 billion framework for crude oil procurement and stockpiling across India, Australia and ASEAN. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi convened the summit on 15 April 2026 to coordinate Asian responses to energy supply disruptions from West Asia, and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar attended.
source: a roughly USD 10 billion framework for crude oil procurement and stockpiling across India, Australia and ASEAN.

prompt: In 1976, during the Emergency, the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among states was frozen on the basis of which Census?
explain: The 1976 freeze used 1971 Census figures so that states that controlled population growth, mainly in the South, would not lose seats to states with higher birth rates. The freeze was later extended until 2026.
source: In 1976, during the Emergency, the government froze the seat allocation based on the 1971 Census to ensure that states which successfully implemented population control (primarily in the South) were not punished by losing seats to states with higher birth rates (primarily in the North).

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to Lok Sabha seats and delimitation, as discussed in April 2026:
items: Article 81 of the Constitution — delimitation and readjustment of seats after every census
Seats currently reserved for Scheduled Castes — 84
Seats currently reserved for Scheduled Tribes — 70
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong. Seats reserved for Scheduled Tribes currently number 47, and 70 was the figure proposed under the expanded House, while Scheduled Caste seats would have risen from 84 to 136. Critics said the failed bill would have removed the Article 81 obligation and left Parliament to decide when delimitation happens and which census it uses.
source: Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (India's constitutionally recognised disadvantaged communities) also increase, from 84 to 136 and 47 to 70 respectively, with one-third of each reserved for women.

prompt: In April 2026, after Iranian forces fired on two Indian-flagged vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, India approved support for a maritime insurance pool. Consider the following statements about it:
items: India approved a government-backed guarantee of INR 129.8 billion for the pool.
The pool covers hull, cargo and war risk for a period of ten years.
GIC Re, India's government-owned reinsurer, was among the reinsurers that had pulled cover or raised premiums.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The guarantee (USD 1.4 billion) backs a pool covering hull, cargo and war risk for ten years, and GIC Re was one of the reinsurers that pulled cover or hiked premiums. Member insurers will issue policies with combined underwriting capacity of about INR 9.5 billion.
source: Hours after the attack, India approved an INR 129.8 billion (USD 1.4 billion) government-backed guarantee for a maritime insurance pool covering hull, cargo, and war risk for ten years.

prompt: In March 2026, the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena was sunk off Sri Lanka shortly after taking part in India's MILAN 2026 naval exercise. Where was MILAN 2026 held?
explain: The Dena had just left MILAN 2026 in Visakhapatnam as New Delhi's guest when a US submarine torpedoed it in international waters on 4 March, killing at least 87 sailors. India never publicly criticised the US for the sinking.
source: The Dena had just left India's MILAN 2026 naval exercise in Visakhapatnam

prompt: In April 2026, India shelved its plan to pre-install the Aadhaar app on all smartphones sold in the country. Consider the following statements:
items: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology reviewed the proposal and decided against it.
The ministry cited the security risks flagged by Apple and Samsung as its official reason for dropping the plan.
A December 2025 mandate to pre-install the Sanchar Saathi telecom app was rolled back within days.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because MeitY decided against the plan with no official reason given, even though Apple and Samsung had flagged security and compatibility concerns. This was the sixth attempt in two years to mandate pre-installed state apps, and the industry opposed all six.
source: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) reviewed the proposal and decided against it, with no official reason given.

prompt: In April 2026, the Competition Commission of India set a final hearing date in its antitrust case against Apple. Apple had challenged India's antitrust penalty law because that law allows the CCI to calculate fines on the basis of which of the following?
explain: Apple challenged the penalty law in the Delhi High Court because it lets the CCI compute fines on global turnover. Apple said this could expose it to penalties of up to USD 38 billion.
source: Instead, it challenged India's antitrust penalty law in the Delhi High Court, which allows the CCI to calculate fines based on global turnover.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Competition Commission of India's antitrust case against Apple, for which a final hearing was set for May 2026:
items: CCI investigators found in 2024 that Apple abused its dominant position by forcing app developers to use its proprietary in-app payment system.
Apple challenged India's antitrust penalty law in the Supreme Court.
The CCI refused Apple's request to pause proceedings pending its court challenge.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Apple filed its challenge in the Delhi High Court, not the Supreme Court. The CCI turned down Apple's request to pause and set a final hearing for May 21, 2026, while Apple denies wrongdoing.
source: Competition Commission of India (CCI) investigators found in 2024 that Apple abused its dominant position in the app market by forcing developers to use its proprietary in-app payment system.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) currency market measures in March–April 2026:
items: In April 2026, the RBI lifted its ban on rupee non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts and restored the ability to rebook cancelled forward contracts.
The USD 100 million cap on banks' net open positions, imposed in March 2026, was withdrawn along with the NDF ban.
The rupee hit an all-time low of INR 95.22 to the dollar in late March 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the USD 100 million position cap imposed on March 27 remains in force even after the NDF ban was lifted on 20 April 2026. The RBI had acted after the Iran conflict pushed Brent crude above USD 110 and banks built up an estimated USD 30 to USD 40 billion in onshore-offshore arbitrage positions.
source: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Monday lifted its April 1 ban on rupee non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts and restored the ability to rebook cancelled forward contracts.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–South Korea summit held in April 2026:
items: The two sides pledged to double bilateral trade to USD 54 billion by 2030.
They agreed to fast-track talks to upgrade the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, a trade pact dating from 2010.
They established a ministerial-level economic cooperation committee for the first time.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are stated in the story. Prime Minister Modi and President Lee Jae Myung announced the trade target alongside a 250+ person business delegation, and India hopes the CEPA upgrade will narrow its trade deficit while Seoul seeks deeper market access.
source: On Monday, Indian Prime Minister Modi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung pledged to double bilateral trade to USD 54 billion by 2030, anchored by a 250+ person business delegation and an upgrade of their 2010 trade pact.

prompt: In April 2026, South Korea's POSCO and India's JSW finalised a USD 1.09 billion joint venture for a steel plant in which Indian state?
explain: The POSCO–JSW joint venture is for a steel plant in Odisha. It was finalised during the India–South Korea summit, where 20 other MOUs covering shipbuilding, semiconductors and green energy were also signed.
source: South Korea’s POSCO and India’s JSW finalised a USD 1.09 billion joint venture for a steel plant in Odisha.

prompt: The HPCL Rajasthan Refinery (HRRL) at Balotra, scheduled for inauguration by the Prime Minister in April 2026, is designed to process crude oil from which domestic source?
explain: HRRL is designed to process local Mangala crude and produce high-value petrochemicals, helping India cut its import dependency. A fire broke out at the facility on 20 April 2026, a day before the scheduled inauguration, but it was brought under control with no casualties.
source: HRRL aims to help the country slash import dependency by processing local Mangala crude and producing high-value petrochemicals.

prompt: In April 2026, a group of citizens complained about the Prime Minister's national address of 18 April. Consider the following statements:
items: The complaint was lodged with the Supreme Court, alleging that the address violated the Model Code of Conduct in force ahead of elections in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.
The address was delivered a day after the women's reservation bill was defeated in the Rajya Sabha.
The complainants sought equal airtime for opposition parties on private broadcasters if the speech was pre-approved.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the complaint was filed with the Election Commission, not the Supreme Court; the bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha; and the complainants sought equal airtime on public broadcasters, not private ones. The complainants alleged that publicly funded platforms were used for partisan electioneering days before polling on 23 April.
source: The complainants want the Election Commission (EC) to investigate and, if Modi's speech was pre-approved, grant opposition parties equal airtime on public broadcasters.

prompt: In April 2026, over 700 citizens alleged that the Prime Minister's national address violated the Model Code of Conduct. With which body was this complaint filed?
explain: The complaint, filed on 20 April 2026, asked the Election Commission to investigate the address. The Communist Party of India and CPI(M) lodged separate complaints.
source: Over 700 citizens filed a complaint to the Election Commission alleging that Prime Minister Modi's April 18 national address violated the Model Code of Conduct (MCC)

prompt: In April 2026, India and Germany signed defence agreements in Berlin. Consider the following statements:
items: One agreement is a roadmap for co-developing and co-producing defence equipment in niche technologies.
A separate arrangement covers cooperation in UN Peacekeeping Training.
The India-EU Security and Defence Partnership was signed at the same Berlin meeting.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Rajnath Singh and Boris Pistorius signed the Defence Industrial Cooperation Roadmap and a UN Peacekeeping Training arrangement. The India-EU Security and Defence Partnership was signed earlier, in January 2026, and Singh cited it as the wider frame. TBB reads the roadmap as turning Germany from a vendor into a manufacturing partner.
source: a roadmap for co-developing and co-producing defence equipment in niche technologies, and a separate arrangement for cooperation in UN Peacekeeping Training.

prompt: In April 2026, India invited the German Air Force to take part in Tarang Shakti in September 2026. What is Tarang Shakti?
options: A multilateral air exercise hosted by India
A bilateral naval exercise of India and Germany
A multilateral army exercise hosted by Germany
A trilateral coast guard exercise of India and the EU
explain: Tarang Shakti is India's multilateral air exercise. Its 2024 edition drew air forces from 11 countries, including France, the UK, the US, Australia, Japan and the UAE, with 18 others as observers.
source: Singh invited the German Air Force to join Tarang Shakti, India's multilateral air exercise, this September.

prompt: In April 2026, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy extended local sourcing rules for solar projects from modules to cells by amending which framework?
explain: MNRE amended its Approved Models and Manufacturers framework, in place since 2019, to cover cells as well as modules. India has 80 GW of module-making capacity but only 7 GW of cell capacity, with the rest imported mostly from China.
source: India's renewable energy ministry (MNRE) amended its Approved Models and Manufacturers framework, which has been in place since 2019, to extend local sourcing rules from modules to cells.

prompt: As stated in April 2026, what is India's target for non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030?
explain: India aims for 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, up from 156 GW at the time of the April 2026 solar cell mandate. TBB argues that requiring domestic cells before supply catches up is meant to force capital into Indian cell manufacturing.
source: India's target is 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, up from 156 GW today.

prompt: Consider the following statements about US trade action on solar imports in April 2026:
items: The US Commerce Department imposed a preliminary antidumping duty of 123.04% on Indian solar imports.
Laos faced a higher preliminary antidumping rate than Indonesia.
Combined with countervailing duties imposed in February 2026, the total tax burden on Indian solar exports exceeds 200%.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: Indonesia faces 35.17% and Laos just 22.46%, both far below India's 123.04%. The blow is heavy because the US accounts for over 95% of India's solar cell and module exports.
source: India’s rate dwarfs its peers, with Indonesia facing 35.17% and Laos just 22.46%.

prompt: In the US antidumping case on solar imports that led to duties on India in April 2026, which body ruled that these imports had 'materially injured' the US domestic industry?
options: Office of the United States Trade Representative
United States Department of the Treasury
explain: The injury finding came from the United States International Trade Commission, while the Commerce Department set the preliminary duty rates. The probe began on a petition from US manufacturers in July 2025.
source: The United States International Trade Commission (ITC) had ruled in August that these imports "materially injured" the US domestic industry.

prompt: US manufacturers who petitioned in July 2025 for the antidumping probe that led to duties on Indian solar imports in April 2026 claimed that firms had moved to India and Indonesia to dodge tariffs previously imposed on which countries?
explain: The petitioners alleged that firms relocated to India and Indonesia to escape earlier tariffs on Cambodia and Vietnam. The duties landed while an Indian delegation was in Washington trying to finalise an interim trade deal.
source: A group of US manufacturers petitioned for the probe in July 2025, claiming firms relocated to India and Indonesia to dodge tariffs previously slapped on Cambodia and Vietnam.

prompt: In April 2026, seven of the Aam Aadmi Party's ten Rajya Sabha members joined the BJP. Under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, what is the minimum share of a legislature party's members needed for a recognised merger?
explain: Seven of ten seats is exactly two-thirds, the minimum for a recognised merger under the Tenth Schedule, India's anti-defection law. Raghav Chadha had introduced a bill in 2022 to raise the threshold to three-fourths, which would have required eight defectors.
source: Seven is exactly two-thirds of AAP's ten Rajya Sabha seats, the minimum for a recognised party merger under the Tenth Schedule, India's constitutional anti-defection law.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the defection of Aam Aadmi Party Rajya Sabha members to the BJP in April 2026:
items: The defections reduced AAP's strength in the Rajya Sabha from ten seats to three.
After the defections, the NDA held 146 seats in the 245-member Rajya Sabha, still short of a two-thirds majority.
Six of the seven defectors hold Rajya Sabha seats from Punjab.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: AAP fell from ten seats to three, the NDA now holds 146 seats, 17 short of two-thirds, and six of the seven defectors hold Punjab seats. Seven is exactly two-thirds of AAP's ten Rajya Sabha seats, the minimum for a recognised merger under the Tenth Schedule.
source: The coalition now holds 146 seats, 17 short of the two-thirds majority needed for constitutional amendments

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's power situation in April 2026:
items: India's peak power demand hit a record 256.1 GW during a heatwave.
The Ministry of Power's emergency playbook deferred maintenance on 10,000 MW of hydropower plants until July.
NTPC procured gas through the Indian Gas Exchange to meet demand.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the deferred maintenance covered 10,000 MW of thermal plants, not hydropower plants. To meet the record demand, coal-fired generation ramped up to 187 GW, supported by 9.6 GW of gas-fired capacity.
source: deferring maintenance on 10,000 MW of thermal plants until July

prompt: In September 2025, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate on small cars and two-wheelers was revised. Which of the following correctly describes the change?
explain: The September 2025 GST cuts lowered the tax on small cars and two-wheelers from 28% to 18%. By April 2026 this had lifted industry-wide wholesale volumes 13.2% year-on-year in Q4 FY26, up from 2.4% in the previous quarter.
source: driven by the September 2025 GST cuts that slashed tax on small cars and two-wheelers from 28% to 18%.

prompt: In April 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addressed the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) defence ministers' meeting, citing Operation Sindoor. In which city was the meeting held?
explain: Singh spoke at the SCO defence ministers' meeting in Bishkek, saying Operation Sindoor proved terror epicentres are no longer immune to punishment. On the sidelines he met China's Defence Minister Admiral Dong Jun and Russia's Defence Minister Andrei Belousov.
source: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh told the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) defence ministers' meeting in Bishkek

prompt: Consider the following statements about Pakistan and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), as of April 2026:
items: Pakistan has been a member of the SCO since 2017.
Pakistan chairs the SCO's Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS).
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct: Pakistan joined the SCO in 2017 and chairs its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure. Singh's call for action against states that shelter terrorists was aimed at Pakistan without naming it.
source: Pakistan, an SCO member since 2017, was the unmistakable target.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the declaration adopted at the SCO summit in Tianjin in September 2025:
items: It explicitly condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.
It condemned the attack on Pakistan's Jaffar Express train.
It rejected double standards on terrorism.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The Tianjin declaration condemned Pahalgam as well as attacks on the Jaffar Express and in Khuzdar, Balochistan, and rejected double standards on terrorism, with Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif present.
source: Last September's declaration at the summit in Tianjin explicitly condemned the Pahalgam attack and rejected "double standards" on terrorism, with Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif at the table.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to aviation turbine fuel (ATF) in India as of April 2026:
items: Excise duty on ATF — 11%
Value Added Tax on ATF in Delhi — 29%
Cap on April's domestic ATF base price hike — 100%
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Only the first pair is correct, since the excise duty on ATF is 11%. Pair 2 is wrong because Delhi charges 25% VAT on ATF (29% is Tamil Nadu's rate), and pair 3 is wrong because the government capped April's domestic base price hike at 25%, while over 100% was the rise in international fuel prices. With state assembly elections underway, the Federation of Indian Airlines has sought a temporary suspension of the excise duty and cuts in state VAT rates.
source: With state assembly elections underway, the government capped April's domestic ATF base price hike at 25% while international fuel prices rose by over 100%.

prompt: In April 2026, the Federation of Indian Airlines sought relief on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) costs. Consider the following statements about ATF in India:
items: ATF makes up about 4% of India's refinery output.
Domestic airlines consume most of the ATF produced in India, leaving little for export.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Domestic airlines consume only 30% of the ATF India refines, and the rest is marked for export. ATF now accounts for 55-60% of airline costs, up from 30-40% before April's price hike.
source: Domestic airlines consume only 30% of that, with the rest marked for export.

prompt: In April 2026, the Reserve Bank of India ordered banks to report offshore rupee derivative trades executed by their group entities. Consider the following statements about this mandate:
items: Banks must report over-the-counter FX contracts to the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
Foreign lenders must disclose trades from their offshore units, not just their Indian branches.
Lenders must report 100% of notional value by July 2028.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: banks must report both deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts to the Clearing Corporation of India, not SEBI. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, with implementation phased from 70% of notional value by July 2027 to 100% by July 2028, and trades under USD 1 million exempt.
source: Banks must now report both deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts to the Clearing Corporation of India.

prompt: Under the Reserve Bank of India's April 2026 mandate, banks must report offshore rupee derivative trades by their group entities to which of the following?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India
explain: Banks must report deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts to the Clearing Corporation of India. The move follows other RBI steps to manage the rupee, including a USD 100 million cap on net open positions.
source: Banks must now report both deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts to the Clearing Corporation of India.

prompt: In April 2026, India named Dinesh Trivedi as its next high commissioner to Bangladesh. Consider the following statements:
items: Trivedi is a career diplomat, in keeping with India's usual practice for the post.
Trivedi is a former railways and health minister who joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2021.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Trivedi is a veteran politician, and appointing a non-diplomat to the post is a rare move. The appointment follows the Bangladesh Nationalist Party's election win in February 2026 and an April 2026 visit by Bangladesh's foreign minister seeking fuel, fertiliser and energy cooperation.
source: Trivedi, 75, is a former railways and health minister who joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in 2021.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the draft rules on higher ethanol blends published in April 2026:
items: The draft was published by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
It proposes amending the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to add E85 and E100 fuels to India's regulatory framework.
The draft is open for public comment for 30 days.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. MoRTH proposed amending the Central Motor Vehicles Rules to recognise E85 and E100 and opened the draft to 30 days of public comment. The amendment creates a legal basis for type-approval testing of vehicles built for higher blends, with a phased E85 rollout targeted for late 2026.
source: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) proposed amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules adding E85 (85% ethanol, 15% petrol) and E100 (nearly pure ethanol) to India's regulatory framework.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's ethanol blending programme as of April 2026:
items: Grain-based ethanol accounts for a majority of India's ethanol production.
The mandatory nationwide rollout of E20 on 1 April 2026 came a year later than the original target.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because India achieved the E20 rollout a year ahead of its original target, not behind it. Grain-based ethanol now makes up 60% of production, though sugarcane remains the crop that shapes politics.
source: This follows the mandatory nationwide rollout of E20 (20% ethanol) on 1 April 2026, which India achieved a year ahead of its original target.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to ethanol-blended fuels:
items: E85 — 85% ethanol and 15% petrol
Energy content of ethanol — roughly 27-30% more per litre than petrol
NITI Aayog recommendation of 2021 — higher-blend fuels to be priced above regular petrol
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Only the first pair is correct. Ethanol carries roughly 27-30% less energy per litre than petrol, not more, and in 2021 NITI Aayog recommended pricing higher-blend fuels below regular petrol to compensate for this energy loss. In April 2026 the transport ministry published draft rules to recognise E85 and E100, though E85 will not reach fuel pumps immediately.
source: Ethanol carries roughly 27-30% less energy per litre than petrol.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's fuel duty measures announced in April 2026:
items: The export duty on diesel was cut to INR 23 per litre from INR 55.5 per litre.
Domestic fuel duties were reduced alongside the cut in export duties.
The government capped monthly ATF price increases for domestic carriers at 25%.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because domestic fuel duties remained unchanged; only export duties on diesel and ATF were cut on 30 April 2026. The cut partially unwound the hikes of 12 April, imposed to curb an export surge by refiners chasing better margins in Southeast Asia.
source: Export duty on diesel dropped to INR 23 per litre from INR 55.5, while ATF fell to INR 33 from INR 42.

prompt: In May 2026, Apple went to court against an Indian regulator, accusing it of 'usurping' judicial authority by demanding financial data for a potential USD 38 billion penalty. Which body has been investigating Apple since 2024 for abusing its dominant position in the iPhone app market?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
explain: The Competition Commission of India, India's antitrust watchdog, has been investigating Apple since 2024 over abuse of dominance in the iPhone app market. It asked Apple to submit financial records ahead of a final hearing on May 21.
source: Since 2024, the Competition Commission of India (CCI) has been investigating Apple for abusing its dominant position in the iPhone app market.

prompt: In April 2026, who replaced Suman Bery as vice-chairman of NITI Aayog?
explain: Former Chief Economic Adviser Ashok Lahiri took over as vice-chairman on 24 April 2026. Rajiv Gauba, K V Raju and Abhay Karandikar were named full-time members in the same overhaul.
