source: On April 24, former Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) Ashok Lahiri replaced Suman Bery as vice-chairman.

prompt: Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
items: Like the Planning Commission, it controls plan funds and has allocation leverage over states.
It replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.
It has no statutory authority and no enforcement power.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: plan funds and allocation leverage over states belonged to the Planning Commission, while NITI Aayog is purely recommendatory with no budget. Several opposition-ruled states already boycott its meetings, and ministries routinely sideline its reports.
source: NITI Aayog is purely recommendatory, with no budget, no statutory authority, and no enforcement power.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog overhaul completed in April–May 2026:
items: The new vice-chairman is the first to hold the post with elected political experience.
Former Cabinet Secretary Rajiv Gauba was the only full-time member retained from the earlier team.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Ashok Lahiri is a BJP legislator from Balurghat in West Bengal, and Gauba was the only holdover among the full-time members. Two more members joined on 2 May 2026, taking total membership to seven.
source: Lahiri, a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) legislator from West Bengal's Balurghat, is the first vice-chairman with elected political experience.

prompt: In May 2026, Ecuador's Foreign Minister Gabriela Sommerfeld Rosero concluded a visit to New Delhi. Consider the following statements about the visit and India–Ecuador ties:
items: Ecuador joined both the International Solar Alliance and the International Big Cat Alliance.
India pledged INR 12 crore in development grants to be spread over ten years.
Pharmaceuticals were among India's main imports from Ecuador in 2023–24.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 2 and 3 are wrong: India pledged INR 12 crore (USD 1.4 million) over five years, not ten, and pharmaceuticals are an Indian export to Ecuador, while India imports crude oil, gold and cocoa. Only statement 1 is correct, and bilateral trade stood at USD 1.26 billion in 2023–24.
source: India pledged INR 12 crore (USD 1.4 million) in development grants over five years.

prompt: During the Ecuadorian Foreign Minister's visit to New Delhi that concluded in May 2026, the framework for which type of trade agreement was discussed with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal?
explain: Piyush Goyal and Gabriela Sommerfeld Rosero discussed a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) framework, along with expanded Indian pharmaceutical exports. TBB's analysis calls the PTA the wrapping paper and the minerals the gift.
source: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and Sommerfeld discussed a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) framework, expanded Indian pharmaceutical exports, and supply-chain partnerships in copper and gold.

prompt: In May 2026, India and Ecuador discussed supply-chain partnerships in which two minerals?
explain: The talks covered supply-chain partnerships in copper and gold. Ecuador sits on the southern extension of the Andean metallic belt, where Chinese state-owned companies already operate its largest copper mine.
source: discussed a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA) framework, expanded Indian pharmaceutical exports, and supply-chain partnerships in copper and gold

prompt: Consider the following statements about Mission Drishti, launched by the Bengaluru-based startup GalaxEye in May 2026:
items: It is the world's first satellite to combine optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging on a single platform.
It was launched aboard an ISRO Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle.
GalaxEye has partnered with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) for global distribution of its imagery.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the 190 kg satellite was launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9, not an ISRO rocket. It is also India's largest privately built satellite, and NSIL, ISRO's commercial arm, will handle global distribution of the imagery.
source: The 190 kg satellite is the world's first to combine optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging on a single platform, allowing all-weather, day-and-night Earth observation.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Kerala Legislative Assembly election results declared in May 2026:
items: The majority mark in the 140-seat assembly is 71.
The CPI(M) won 26 seats, down from 62 in 2021.
Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan lost his Dharmadam constituency.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Vijayan held Dharmadam, although at least 12 of his cabinet ministers were trailing or lost their seats. The Congress-led UDF crossed the majority mark with over 90 seats, ending the LDF's decade-long hold on the state.
source: Vijayan himself held his Dharmadam constituency, but at least 12 of his cabinet ministers were trailing or lost their seats.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of states and the year in which CPI(M)-led rule there ended:
items: West Bengal — 2018
Tripura — 2011
Kerala — 2026
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Only the Kerala pair is correct. The story says the CPI(M) held West Bengal until 2011, not 2018, and Tripura until 2018, not 2011. With the LDF's defeat in Kerala in May 2026, no Left party governs any Indian state.
source: The CPI(M) held West Bengal for 34 years until 2011, Tripura until 2018, and Kerala until today.

prompt: In the Kerala assembly election of May 2026, BJP state president Rajeev Chandrasekhar defeated sitting CPI(M) minister V. Sivankutty in which constituency?
explain: Chandrasekhar won Nemom in Thiruvananthapuram, one of the BJP's three seats in the election. Dharmadam is Pinarayi Vijayan's seat, and Paravur is held by V.D. Satheesan, the front-runner for Chief Minister.
source: The BJP won three seats, including Nemom in Thiruvananthapuram, where state president Rajeev Chandrasekhar defeated sitting CPI(M) minister V. Sivankutty.

prompt: In May 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 to cushion businesses against the West Asia conflict. What additional credit flow does the scheme target?
explain: ECLGS 5.0 targets INR 2.55 lakh crore (USD 26.8 billion) in additional credit, including INR 5,000 crore earmarked for airlines. INR 3.61 lakh crore is what versions 1.0 to 4.0 issued in guarantees before the scheme wound down in March 2023.
source: The scheme targets INR 2.55 lakh crore (USD 26.8 billion) in additional credit flow, including INR 5,000 crore (USD 526 million) earmarked for airlines.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 approved in May 2026:
items: The National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited provides 90% guarantee coverage for MSMEs.
Additional credit for an airline is capped at INR 1,500 crore per borrower.
Borrowers pay no guarantee fee under the scheme.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first statement is wrong: NCGTC gives 100% coverage for MSMEs, and 90% applies to non-MSMEs and airlines. Airlines can get up to 100% additional credit, capped at INR 1,500 crore per borrower, and there is no guarantee fee.
source: The government-owned National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC) provides 100% guarantee coverage for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and 90% for non-MSMEs and airlines.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS):
items: First launch of ECLGS — May 2020, under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat package
Winding down of versions 1.0 to 4.0 — March 2023
Validity of ECLGS 5.0 — until 31 March 2027
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs match the story. ECLGS began in May 2020 to keep MSMEs afloat during COVID lockdowns, wound down in March 2023, and version 5.0 runs until 31 March 2027. TBB notes that the COVID problem was lost demand, while the West Asia shock hits supply.
source: ECLGS was first launched in May 2020 under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) package to keep MSMEs afloat during COVID lockdowns.

prompt: In May 2026, Indian traders resumed wheat exports for the first time in four years. Consider the following statements:
items: India had banned overseas sales of wheat in 2022 to protect local supply.
The government cleared a total of 5 million tons of wheat for export in a single tranche.
Indian wheat is cheaper than rival supplies from Australia and the Black Sea.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The 5 million tons were cleared across two tranches, and Indian wheat is about USD 20 more expensive than Australian or Black Sea supplies. The 2022 ban was extended to 2023 and 2024 and lifted after a robust 2025 harvest.
source: The government has cleared a total of 5 million tons for export across two recent tranches.

prompt: In May 2026, ITC loaded India's first wheat export shipment in four years, destined for the UAE, at which port?
explain: ITC was loading 22,000 metric tons of wheat at Kandla for the UAE. Because of the price gap, Indian wheat mainly suits buyers with immediate supply gaps or geographic proximity, such as the Middle East.
source: Conglomerate ITC is currently loading 22,000 metric tons at Kandla port destined for the UAE.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the cotton mission approved by the Union Cabinet in May 2026:
items: It has an outlay of INR 5,659 crore over five years.
It was launched against the backdrop of India's cotton production falling to a 17-year low.
It aims to modernise 5,000 ginning and processing facilities.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The mission targets the modernisation of 2,000 ginning and processing facilities, not 5,000, to cut contaminants in the supply chain. The INR 5,659 crore, five-year mission responds to a 17-year production low that has pushed India into record-high imports.
source: The Union Cabinet approved a INR 5,659 crore (USD 594 million) five-year mission on Tuesday to rescue India’s wilting cotton sector from a 17-year production low.

prompt: Under the cotton mission approved by the Union Cabinet in May 2026, 'Kasturi Cotton Bharat' is being expanded. What is it?
options: A branding initiative to improve traceability of Indian cotton
A climate-resilient Bt cotton seed variety for rainfed areas
A price support scheme for small cotton farmers
An export credit facility for cotton textile mills
explain: The mission expands Kasturi Cotton Bharat branding for better traceability, alongside modernising 2,000 ginning and processing facilities. TBB notes that traceability matters for multinational buyers facing ESG audits in the US and EU.
source: expanding the Kasturi Cotton Bharat branding for better traceability

prompt: In May 2026, while approving a cotton mission, the government cited a pest's growing immunity to Bt cotton as a cause of stagnating yields. Which pest is it?
explain: The Pink Bollworm's growing immunity to Bt cotton, together with outdated seeds and erratic monsoons, has stalled yields. As a result India, traditionally a cotton exporter, has turned to record-high imports to feed its mills.
source: Outdated seeds, erratic monsoons, and the Pink Bollworm’s growing immunity to Bt cotton have forced India – traditionally an exporter – into record-high imports to feed its domestic mills.

prompt: In May 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the final two projects under India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 1.0. Consider the following statements:
items: The two projects are a Gallium Nitride (GaN) display panel facility in Dholera and a chip packaging plant in Surat.
The two projects together bring in investment of about INR 39,360 crore.
Half of the projects approved under ISM 1.0 are located in Gujarat.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the two assembly-tier facilities bring a combined INR 3,936 crore (USD 414 million). With these approvals ISM 1.0 closes at 12 projects worth INR 1.64 lakh crore, six of them in Gujarat.
source: The two assembly-tier facilities bring a combined INR 3,936 crore (USD 414 million) in investment and close out ISM 1.0 at 12 approved projects worth INR 1.64 lakh crore (USD 17.3 billion).

prompt: In May 2026, during the India visit of Vietnamese President To Lam, India–Vietnam bilateral ties were elevated to which level?
explain: The visit concluded on 7 May 2026 with ties raised to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. TBB reads the upgrade as part of a middle-power effort to stay insulated from US-China friction.
source: President To Lam of Vietnam wrapped up his India visit today, elevating bilateral ties to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to insulate both nations from superpower friction.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the economic outcomes of the India–Vietnam summit held in May 2026:
items: The two countries set a bilateral trade target of USD 25 billion by 2030.
India's UPI is to be linked with Vietnam's Fast Payment System.
The two sides pledged to complete the review of the ASEAN India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) by the end of 2028.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the leaders pledged to finish the AITIGA review by year-end, meaning the end of 2026, to fix trade imbalances. A critical minerals pact and the UPI linkage are central to reaching the USD 25 billion goal.
source: They also pledged to finish the ASEAN India Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) review by year-end to fix trade imbalances.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Vietnam maritime and defence commitments made in May 2026:
items: The two countries committed to expanding oil and gas exploration in accordance with international law.
Defence cooperation will include regular joint hydrographic surveys and increased naval port calls.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both commitments were made. The reference to international law on oil and gas exploration is read as a nod to resisting Beijing's maritime claims in the South China Sea, and the two sides also agreed to move beyond buyer-seller roles to co-produce military technology.
source: This includes regular joint hydrographic surveys and increased naval port calls to boost maritime awareness.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the leadership of the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) as of May 2026:
items: Vempati received the Padma Shri, India's third-highest civilian honour, in January 2026.
Shashi Shekhar Vempati was appointed CBFC chairperson for a three-year term.
Prasoon Joshi had led the CBFC since August 2017, succeeding Pahlaj Nihalani.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the story describes the Padma Shri as India's fourth-highest civilian honour, not the third. Vempati, a former CEO of Rajya Sabha TV and Prasar Bharati, replaced Joshi, whose tenure focused on digitising the board's certification process.
source: He previously served as CEO of Rajya Sabha TV and Prasar Bharati, and received a Padma Shri, India’s fourth-highest civilian honour, in January 2026.

prompt: In May 2026, Prasoon Joshi was moved from the Central Board of Film Certification to head Prasar Bharati, India's public broadcaster. Which ministry made this move?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
explain: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry moved Joshi to Prasar Bharati on 2 May 2026, creating the CBFC vacancy that Vempati filled. The two men have effectively traded chairs across the same two institutions.
source: On May 2, the Information and Broadcasting (I&B) Ministry moved him to head Prasar Bharati, creating the vacancy Vempati now fills.

prompt: In May 2026, Vijay of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam submitted letters of support from MLAs to the Governor of Tamil Nadu to stake a claim to form the government. Who was the Governor?
explain: Vijay submitted letters from 112 MLAs to Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, who asked him to return with proof of support from 118 MLAs, the majority mark in the 234-seat Assembly.
source: Vijay submitted support letters from 112 MLAs to Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday, who told him to return with proof of 118.

prompt: Consider the following statements in the context of India's sporting engagement with Pakistan as of May 2026:
items: A memo issued by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports in May 2026 cleared the way for Pakistani teams to compete in multilateral events hosted by India.
Under the May 2026 policy, India will continue to refuse to play one-on-one series against Pakistan or host it for standalone matches.
India is bidding to host the 2036 Olympics and the 2038 Asian Games.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The May 2026 memo opens multilateral events to Pakistani teams, while India still refuses bilateral series or standalone matches, and India is bidding for the 2030 Commonwealth Games, 2036 Olympics and 2038 Asian Games. Bilateral cricket between the two countries has been frozen since 2012.
source: India will still refuse to play one-on-one series against Pakistan or host them for standalone matches.

prompt: During the India-hosted T20 World Cup in 2026, in which country did Pakistan play its matches?
explain: Pakistan played its matches in Sri Lanka to avoid the optics of crossing the border. Bilateral cricket between India and Pakistan has been frozen since 2012, and a military skirmish in May 2025 hardened the freeze further.
source: During this year’s India-hosted T20 World Cup, Pakistan played its matches in Sri Lanka to avoid the optics of crossing the border.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog report on school education released in May 2026:
items: Private schools make up 38.8% of all schools in India.
Government schools make up 68.1% of all schools in India.
Only 5.4% of schools offer continuous education from Grade 1 to 12.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: private schools are 23.1% of institutions, and 38.8% is their share of enrolment. Government schools, though 68.1% of all schools, now enrol only 49.24% of students, down from 71% in 2005.
source: Private schools, at 23.1% of institutions, now account for 38.8% of enrolment.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to school education data in the NITI Aayog report released in May 2026:
items: Gross Enrolment Ratio at primary level — 90.9%
Gross Enrolment Ratio at higher secondary level — 58.4%
Schools with zero student enrolment that still receive funding — nearly 80,000
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The report flagged nearly 8,000 schools, not 80,000, with zero enrolment that still get funding and staff because of outdated records. The fall in GER from 90.9% at primary to 58.4% at higher secondary means nearly four in ten children leave before finishing school.
source: The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) drops from 90.9% at primary level to 58.4% at higher secondary.

prompt: In May 2026, amid the West Asia crisis, Prime Minister Narendra Modi made an appeal to conserve foreign exchange and fuel. Consider the following statements:
items: He asked Indians to stop buying gold for a year and to postpone foreign travel.
He urged farmers to halve chemical fertiliser use and move to solar-powered irrigation.
State-owned Oil Marketing Companies had raised retail petrol and diesel prices to offset their under-recoveries.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because retail petrol and diesel prices remained unchanged. Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum were instead absorbing under-recoveries of INR 1,600–1,700 crore a day as crude rose from USD 70 to over USD 120 per barrel.
source: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday asked Indians to stop buying gold for a year, cut fuel consumption, and postpone foreign travel to conserve foreign exchange amid the West Asia crisis.

prompt: In May 2026, the central government notified the implementing rules for India's four labour codes. Consider the following statements about these codes:
items: The Code on Wages was enacted in 2019, while the other three codes date from 2020.
Together, the four codes consolidate 29 existing labour laws into a single framework.
The four codes came into force only after their implementing rules were notified in May 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the codes came into force on 21 November 2025 but lacked the rules needed to function. Draft rules were published on 30 December 2025 for stakeholder feedback, and the final notification was the last procedural step before enforcement.
source: All four came into force on November 21, 2025, but lacked the rules needed to actually function.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to provisions under the labour code rules notified by India in May 2026:
items: Minimum share of basic pay in total salary — 50%
Cap on weekly working hours — 48 hours
Minimum age for entitlement to free health check-ups — 40 years
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correct: basic pay must be at least 50% of total salary, weekly hours are capped at 48, and workers aged 40 and above get free health check-ups. The rules also make appointment letters mandatory and bring gig and platform workers into the social security net for the first time.
source: Workers aged 40 and above are entitled to free health check-ups, and weekly working hours are capped at 48.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India-European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), as of May 2026:
items: It entered into force in October 2025.
It commits the EFTA bloc to USD 100 billion in FDI in India over 15 years.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements match the story. The EFTA bloc is Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, and the TEPA formed the commercial backdrop to the first Indian prime ministerial visit to Norway in 43 years.
source: which entered into force in October 2025 and commits the EFTA bloc (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein) to USD 100 billion in FDI over 15 years.

prompt: The 3rd India-Nordic Summit was held in Oslo in May 2026. Consider the following pairs of a participating Nordic country and the trade agreement that covers its commerce with India:
items: Finland — India-EU FTA
Iceland — India-EFTA TEPA
Denmark — India-EFTA TEPA
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Denmark is an EU member, so it falls under the India-EU FTA along with Sweden and Finland. Only Norway and Iceland are covered by the India-EFTA TEPA. Earlier India-Nordic summits were held in Stockholm (2018) and Copenhagen (2022).
source: three of the five Nordic participants (Sweden, Denmark, and Finland) fall under the India-EU FTA, while the remaining two (Norway and Iceland) are covered by the India-EFTA TEPA.

prompt: In May 2026, Prime Minister Modi's European tour included a stop in the home country of ASML, the world's sole maker of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines. Which country is it?
explain: ASML is a Dutch firm. It already supplies equipment to the Tata-PSMC mega-fab in Gujarat and is seeking partnerships with Indian companies under India Semiconductor Mission 2.0.
source: Dutch firm ASML, the world's sole maker of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, is already supplying equipment to India's Tata-PSMC mega-fab in Gujarat

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's retail inflation data for April 2026, released in May 2026:
items: Retail inflation came in above the forecast of 3.8%.
The print was held down because the Centre absorbed most of the oil price shock instead of raising prices at the pump.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Retail inflation rose to 3.48%, below the 3.8% forecast, so statement 1 is wrong. The Centre's decision to absorb the oil shock kept fuel prices steady, though food inflation climbed to 4.2%.
source: India's retail inflation rose to 3.48% in April, undershooting the 3.8% forecast, as the Centre absorbed most of the oil price shock rather than raising prices at the pump.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the proposed India–Chile Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), as of May 2026:
items: It would replace a Preferential Trade Agreement signed in 2006 and expanded in 2017.
Its negotiations were formally launched in April 2024 during Chilean President Gabriel Boric's visit to India.
It would cover digital services, MSMEs and critical minerals.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Negotiations were launched during Boric's visit in April 2025, and April 2024 is when the Joint Study Group report was finalised. TBB's analysis notes the CEPA is less a trade deal than a play for access to minerals.
source: Negotiations were formally launched during Chilean President Gabriel Boric's visit to India in April 2025, following a Joint Study Group report finalised in April 2024.

prompt: In May 2026, Chile's Foreign Minister visited New Delhi to advance a trade agreement with India. Chile holds the world's largest reserves of which mineral?
explain: Chile holds the world's largest lithium reserves and is also the leading global copper producer. Both are key inputs for batteries, electric vehicles and clean energy infrastructure.
source: Chile holds the world's largest lithium reserves and is the leading global copper producer.

prompt: In May 2026, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways announced a tripartite MoU with South Korea's HD KSOE for India's first mega greenfield shipyard. Where is the shipyard to be built?
explain: The MoU, signed in April 2026 and announced by the MoPSW on 13 May 2026, is for a facility in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu. South Korean yards bring the high-end technology, and India brings a large workforce.
source: signed a tripartite MoU with South Korea’s HD KSOE earlier in April to build a massive facility in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–South Korea greenfield shipyard agreement announced in May 2026:
items: The shipyard targets an annual capacity of 2.5 million gross tonnage.
It is the first major win for VOYAGES, a maritime framework launched during South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit.
The Indian signatories were National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park and Sagarmala Finance Corporation.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. The yard targets 2.5 million GT a year under a tripartite MoU with HD KSOE, and it is the first major outcome of the VOYAGES framework.
source: The yard targets an annual capacity of 2.5 million gross tonnage (GT).

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's shipbuilding push, as reported in May 2026:
items: Target year for India to be among the world's top five shipbuilders — 2047
Corpus of the Maritime Development Fund — USD 2.9 billion
New vessels India needs by 2042, as projected by the MoPSW — 734
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong because the MoPSW projects that India needs 437 new vessels by 2042, not 734. The government has also overhauled the Merchant Shipping Act and launched a Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Programme to cut contract costs.
source: The MoPSW projects that India needs 437 new vessels by 2042.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's new airports, as of May 2026:
items: Navi Mumbai International Airport began commercial operations in December 2025.
Noida International Airport in the Delhi-NCR began commercial services in March 2026, the month it was inaugurated.
Both airports are designed with an eventual capacity exceeding 70 million passengers each.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Noida International Airport was inaugurated in March 2026, but its commercial services begin in June 2026. The airports are opening just as Indian carriers cut international flights because of the Pakistan and Iran airspace closures and high jet fuel prices.
source: Noida International Airport in the Delhi-National Capital Region (NCR) was inaugurated in March and begins commercial services in June.

prompt: In May 2026, the National Testing Agency scrapped the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) after its questions were leaked. Consider the following statements:
items: The case was filed under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.
When NEET questions were leaked in 2024, the government also cancelled the test.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The case was filed under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, a law passed after the 2024 NEET leak. In 2024 the government did not cancel the test. In May 2026 the Centre handed the investigation to the CBI, which arrested five people across Jaipur, Gurugram and Nashik.
source: The case was filed under the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, a law passed after NEET questions were similarly leaked in 2024.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting that opened on 14 May 2026:
items: It was held in New Delhi and opened by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar.
Iran and the UAE, both BRICS members, were on opposing sides of the ongoing conflict in West Asia.
A deputy-level BRICS meeting in April 2026 ended with a consensus joint statement.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong: the April deputy-level meeting ended without consensus because of the split between Iran and the UAE. At the May meeting Jaishankar called for safe and unimpeded maritime flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea without naming any party.
source: Iran and the UAE, now on opposing sides of the conflict and both BRICS members, have made a joint statement difficult.

prompt: In May 2026, the Indian-flagged dhow Haji Ali sank after a suspected drone or missile strike in the waters of which country?
explain: The dhow was struck in Omani waters, and all 14 crew were rescued by the Omani coast guard. It was the second vessel sunk since the US-Israeli war with Iran began on 28 February 2026.
source: caught fire after a suspected drone or missile strike in Omani waters in the early hours of Wednesday.

prompt: In May 2026, India banned sugar exports. Consider the following statements about this decision:
items: The ban covers raw, white and refined sugar until 30 September 2026, or until further notice.
Earlier in 2026, the government had cleared mills to export 1.59 million tonnes of sugar.
More than 1.2 million tonnes of the approved quota had already been shipped when the ban was announced.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. Only about 800,000 tonnes of the 1.59 million tonne quota were contracted, and just over 600,000 tonnes had been shipped. That leaves roughly 200,000 tonnes of committed orders stranded.
source: India pulled the plug on sugar exports on Wednesday, banning all shipments of raw, white, and refined sugar until September 30, or until further notice.

prompt: In May 2026, India banned sugar exports. Which of the following was the main domestic supply concern behind the ban?
options: Consumption could exceed production for a second straight season
A surplus of sugar stocks was pushing domestic prices down sharply
Mills had shipped far more sugar than their approved export quota
Sugarcane acreage had shifted to rice under a new procurement policy
explain: The story says India risks consuming more sugar than it produces for the second straight season, as cane yields weaken in major growing states. El Niño-linked monsoon disruptions could make the next season worse.
source: India now risks consuming more than it produces for the second straight season, with weakening cane yields in major growing states.

prompt: In May 2026, India raised the import duty on gold and silver from 6% to what rate?
explain: On 13 May 2026, India raised import duties on gold and silver from 6% to 15%. The hike came days after PM Modi urged citizens to pause gold purchases for a year to conserve foreign exchange.
source: On Wednesday, India hiked import duties on gold and silver from 6% to 15%, a drastic move to shore up foreign exchange reserves as geopolitical instability rattles the rupee.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India and gold, in the context of the import duty hike of May 2026:
items: The duty hike was intended to shore up India's foreign exchange reserves.
India is the world's largest consumer of gold.
Indian gold demand is driven largely by investments and jewellery.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: India is the world's second-largest gold consumer, not the largest, so statement 2 is wrong. The hike aimed to protect foreign exchange reserves as geopolitical instability weighed on the rupee.
source: India is the world’s second-largest gold consumer, with demand largely driven by investments and jewellery.

prompt: In May 2026, the Indian National Congress named V.D. Satheesan as Chief Minister of Kerala. Consider the following statements about the April 2026 Kerala Assembly elections and their outcome:
items: The Congress-led United Democratic Front won 102 of the 140 Assembly seats.
The result ended a decade of Left Democratic Front rule under Pinarayi Vijayan.
The Indian Union Muslim League, which backed Satheesan, is a constituent of the Left Democratic Front.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because the story describes the IUML as the UDF's most influential alliance partner, not an LDF constituent. Satheesan, a six-time legislator from Paravur and Leader of the Opposition since 2021, was chosen over K.C. Venugopal and Ramesh Chennithala.
source: ending 11 days of internal jockeying after the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) swept the April assembly elections with 102 of 140 seats

prompt: During the Indian Prime Minister's visit to Abu Dhabi in May 2026, the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) agreed to store up to how much crude oil on Indian soil?
explain: ADNOC will store up to 30 million barrels of crude in India, expanding an existing strategic petroleum reserve arrangement. TBB notes that with the Strait of Hormuz under stress, such supplier-side physical reserves act as a hedge for India.
source: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) will store up to 30 million barrels of crude on Indian soil, expanding an existing strategic petroleum reserve arrangement.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–UAE energy agreements in 2026:
items: Under the package signed in Abu Dhabi in May 2026, the Indian Oil Corporation secured an increased supply of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
The 10-year LNG supply agreement with ADNOC, signed in January 2026, was concluded by the Indian Oil Corporation.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the 10-year LNG supply agreement was signed between HPCL and ADNOC, not the Indian Oil Corporation. It was signed during UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan's visit to New Delhi in January 2026.
source: The Indian Oil Corporation also secured an increased liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) supply under the package.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Netherlands relations as of May 2026:
items: During Prime Minister Modi's visit in May 2026, the bilateral relationship was elevated to a Strategic Partnership with a five-year roadmap for 2026–2030.
The Netherlands is India's fourth-largest source of foreign direct investment.
Over 300 Dutch companies operate in India.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The roadmap adopted by Modi and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten covers semiconductors, defence, green hydrogen, critical minerals, water management and migration. The visit followed the India–EU FTA concluded in January 2026, with the Netherlands acting as a gateway to the EU single market.
source: Modi and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten elevated the bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership, adopting a five-year roadmap (2026–2030) covering semiconductors, defence, green hydrogen, critical minerals, water management, and migration.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India–Netherlands cooperation in May 2026:
items: Afsluitdijk — Dam protecting the Netherlands from the Baltic Sea
Kalpasar project — Maharashtra
Europe's largest port — Antwerp
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are wrong: the Afsluitdijk protects the Netherlands from the North Sea, the Kalpasar project is in Gujarat, and Europe's largest port is Rotterdam in the Netherlands. During Modi's May 2026 visit, both sides signed a Letter of Intent for Dutch technical cooperation on Kalpasar.
source: Modi and Jetten visited the Afsluitdijk, a 32-kilometre dam protecting the Netherlands from the North Sea, drawing parallels with India's Kalpasar project in Gujarat.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting held in May 2026:
items: It was held over two days in Abu Dhabi, with the United Arab Emirates as the host.
The ministers adopted a joint statement condemning the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The United Arab Emirates, a BRICS member, rejected Iran's allegation that it was directly involved in military operations.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 1 and 2 are wrong. The talks were held in Delhi with India as host, and the ministers failed to agree on a joint statement, so India issued a chair's statement acknowledging differing views. Modi was in Abu Dhabi meeting the UAE President while the meeting took place, and the UAE categorically rejected Iran's allegations.
source: BRICS foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement after two days of talks in Delhi on Friday

prompt: Consider the following statements about Rajasthan's power sector as of May 2026:
items: In 2024, Rajasthan became the first Indian state to have solar exceed 50% of its installed power capacity.
Rajasthan has the largest installed renewable energy capacity of any Indian state.
In May 2026, the Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission blocked a proposed 3.2 GW coal-fired project for the second time since November 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Rajasthan's roughly 47 GW of installed renewable capacity is second only to Gujarat's. The regulator told state utilities to carry out rigorous resource planning to show that new coal capacity is needed over cleaner alternatives.
source: Rajasthan became the first Indian state to have solar exceed 50% of its installed power capacity in 2024.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of states or Union Territories and the chief ministers who took office after the assembly elections of May 2026:
items: West Bengal — Suvendu Adhikari
Kerala — V.D. Satheesan
Puducherry — N. Rangaswamy
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three are correctly matched. Adhikari, a former TMC leader who defected to the BJP in 2020, replaced Mamata Banerjee. Satheesan, a five-term MLA and former Leader of Opposition, became Kerala's chief minister, and Rangaswamy returned in Puducherry.
source: Kerala’s new Chief Minister is V.D. Satheesan, a five-term member of the legislative assembly and former Leader of Opposition.

prompt: In May 2026, the rollout of the India–UK free trade agreement was delayed. Which issue did India's Commerce Secretary cite as the hurdle?
options: The UK's new steel import safeguards
The UK's new pharmaceutical import curbs
The UK's new textile import rules
The UK's new IT professional visa limits
explain: The UK's stricter steel safeguards were announced in March 2026, take effect from July 1, and had not been factored into negotiations. They sharply reduce tariff-free quotas and impose steep duties beyond them, which could dilute the market access Indian steelmakers expected.
source: Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the UK's stricter steel safeguards, announced in March and set to take effect from July 1, were not factored into negotiations.

prompt: In May 2026, the Netherlands returned the Anaimangalam Copper Plates of the Chola dynasty to India. Consider the following statements about these plates:
items: They had been held at Leiden University since the mid-19th century.
They record grants by Chola emperor Rajaraja I to a Buddhist monastery at Nagapattinam in Tamil Nadu.
India had pursued their restitution since 2012.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the plates were held at Leiden University since the mid-19th century, record Rajaraja I's grants to a Buddhist monastery at the port town of Nagapattinam, and India had sought their return since 2012. The 11th-century set of 21 large and three small sheets was handed back during Modi's visit.
source: The Anaimangalam Copper Plates, a set of 21 large and three small sheets held at Leiden University since the mid-19th century, record grants by Chola emperor Rajaraja I to a Buddhist monastery at the port town of Nagapattinam in Tamil Nadu.

prompt: In May 2026, the Narcotics Control Bureau made India's first-ever interception of which drug, recovering it across Delhi and Mundra port under Operation RAGEPILL?
explain: The NCB seized 227 kilograms of Captagon, valued at INR 182 crore, in the country's first interception of the drug. It uncovered an international syndicate using India as a transit corridor to the Gulf. Captagon is a psychotropic stimulant that gained notoriety during the Syrian civil war.
source: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) seized 227 kilograms of Captagon in the country's first-ever interception of the drug, uncovering an international syndicate using India as a transit corridor to funnel the stimulant into Gulf nations.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill taken up in April 2026:
items: It proposed expanding the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats.
It proposed reallocating Lok Sabha seats by population using 2011 Census data.
It failed to secure the two-thirds majority required for its passage.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The Bill sought 850 seats allocated by 2011 Census population and fell 54 votes short of the required two-thirds majority. Southern states objected that population-based redistribution would penalise them for successful family planning.
source: Last month, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill proposed expanding the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats and reallocating them by population using 2011 Census data.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of states and their total fertility rate (TFR), as reported in May 2026:
items: Andhra Pradesh — about 2.0
Bihar — 2.4
Madhya Pradesh — 2.7
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: None of the pairs is correct. Andhra Pradesh's TFR is roughly 1.5 (2.0 is the national average), Bihar's is 2.8 (2.4 is Madhya Pradesh's), and Madhya Pradesh's is 2.4 (2.7 is Uttar Pradesh's). All five southern states report TFRs between 1.3 and 1.6, against a replacement level of 2.1.
source: Meanwhile, Bihar (2.8), Uttar Pradesh (2.7), and Madhya Pradesh (2.4) remain well above replacement.

prompt: In May 2026, which state announced the "Children Are Wealth" scheme offering families INR 30,000 for a third child and INR 40,000 for a fourth?
explain: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu announced the scheme at a rally in Srikakulam, revising an earlier proposal of INR 25,000 for a second child. Sikkim offers year-long maternity leave and IVF support instead, while Tamil Nadu's former chief minister only urged newlyweds to have more children.
source: Naidu's scheme, dubbed "Children Are Wealth," will pay families INR 30,000 (USD 312) for a third child and INR 40,000 (USD 415) for a fourth.

prompt: In May 2026, several large Indian non-bank lenders planned to raise funds through three-year floating-rate bonds instead of fixed-rate debt. Consider the following statements about these floating-rate bonds:
items: They pay interest at a spread over the three-month Treasury bill yield.
Their interest rate resets every quarter.
They allow investors to benefit if interest rates rise.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the bonds pay a spread over the three-month Treasury bill yield, reset every quarter, and let investors benefit if interest rates rise. Issuers including ICICI Home Finance and Tata Capital turned to them as markets began pricing in at least 100 basis points of RBI rate hikes.
source: Floating-rate bonds pay interest at a spread over the three-month Treasury bill yield and reset every quarter.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the US sanctions waiver on Russian oil and India's crude imports, as reported in May 2026:
items: The US first issued the waiver in March 2026 to keep global oil prices stable.
In May 2026, the US Treasury Secretary announced a 30-day extension of the waiver for "energy-vulnerable" nations.
India's imports of Russian crude in May 2026 were expected to reach about 1.9 million barrels per day, near record highs.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the waiver was first issued in March 2026 to keep global prices stable, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a 30-day extension for "energy-vulnerable" nations, and Russian crude imports were expected to hit 1.9 million barrels per day in May 2026, near record highs. The extension came hours after a petroleum ministry official said India would keep buying Russian oil regardless of any waiver.
source: Russian imports are expected to hit 1.9 million barrels per day this month – near record highs.

prompt: In May 2026, India and Norway upgraded their bilateral ties on the sidelines of the Nordic summit. What is the new partnership called?
explain: Prime Ministers Narendra Modi and Jonas Gahr Støre upgraded ties to a Green Strategic Partnership on 18 May 2026. At the same meeting they also signed a pact to jointly fund projects in the Global South.
source: On Monday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre upgraded ties to a Green Strategic Partnership and signed a pact to jointly fund projects in the Global South.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the outcomes of the India–Norway talks held in May 2026:
items: Under the triangular development cooperation agreement, Norway will export its digital public infrastructure model while India co-funds the projects.
The Indian Space Research Organisation signed an MoU with the Norwegian Space Agency.
Norway joined India's Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 reverses the roles. Under the triangular agreement, India's digital public infrastructure is rolled out in Global South countries with Norway co-funding the projects while India exports the model. Norway joining the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative is a notable signal from a NATO member with Arctic interests.
source: Both sides signed a triangular development cooperation agreement to jointly roll out India's digital public infrastructure (DPI) in Global South countries, with Norway co-funding projects while India exports the model.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Sweden Strategic Partnership announced in May 2026:
items: Bilateral ties were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during the Indian Prime Minister's visit to Gothenburg.
It comes with a joint action plan for 2026–2030 covering areas including critical minerals and defence.
The two sides set a target of doubling bilateral trade and investment within ten years.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the target is to double bilateral trade and investment within five years, not ten. The two sides also endorsed a joint AI corridor called SITAC, and Sweden awarded Modi the Royal Order of the Polar Star.
source: The two sides endorsed a joint AI corridor (SITAC) and set a target of doubling bilateral trade and investment within five years.

prompt: In May 2026, the 3rd India-Nordic Summit was held in which city?
explain: The 3rd India-Nordic Summit concluded in Oslo on 18 May 2026. Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings there with the leaders of Finland, Denmark, Iceland and Norway. Stockholm hosted the 2018 edition and Copenhagen the 2022 edition.
source: The summit follows previous editions in Stockholm (2018) and Copenhagen (2022).

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's bilateral outcomes at the India-Nordic Summit in May 2026:
items: India and Finland elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalization and Sustainability.
The India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership was launched in 2022.
India and Finland will jointly host the World Circular Economic Forum in Gandhinagar in September 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership was launched in 2020. India and Finland also committed to double bilateral trade by 2030.
source: Modi and Acting Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen reviewed progress under the India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership, launched in 2020.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's engagement with Nordic countries as reported in May 2026:
items: The India-European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement entered into force in October 2025.
The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research's collaboration on floating offshore wind technology is with SINTEF, Norway's largest independent research organisation.
India and Denmark have a joint Smart Laboratory on Clean Rivers in Varanasi.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The SINTEF floating offshore wind collaboration was the centrepiece of five CSIR agreements with Norwegian research bodies. Norway and Iceland fall under the EFTA TEPA, while Sweden, Denmark and Finland fall under the India-EU FTA.
source: The centrepiece is a collaboration on floating offshore wind technology with SINTEF, Norway's largest independent research organisation.

prompt: Consider the following statements about BRICS under India's chairship in 2026:
items: The BRICS Foreign Ministers' Meeting held in New Delhi in May 2026 ended without a joint communiqué because members disagreed on language about the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
India, as chair, issued a summary of the May 2026 Foreign Ministers' Meeting.
The BRICS summit is scheduled to be held in New Delhi on 12-13 September 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the ministerial meeting failed to agree on language on the US-Iran conflict, not Russia-Ukraine, so India issued a chair's summary instead. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin will attend the New Delhi summit, his second trip to India in less than a year.
source: Last week’s ministerial meeting ended without a joint communiqué after members failed to agree on language on the US-Iran conflict.

prompt: In May 2026, Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that India was free from Maoism. Consider the following statements about this announcement:
items: It was made during a visit to Bastar, a former insurgent stronghold.
It included a plan to reintegrate 3,000 surrendered Naxals into mainstream society.
It pledged to bridge the region's infrastructure gap within ten years.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because the pledge is to bridge the infrastructure gap within three to five years, not ten. The plan also turns remote security camps into public service centres so that tribal communities get the same facilities as major cities.
source: He further pledged to bridge the region's historical infrastructure gap within three to five years

prompt: Consider the following statements about India-Italy relations as of May 2026:
items: Italy acts primarily as a supplier of steel and chemicals to India.
In May 2026, the two countries elevated their relations to a Special Strategic Partnership at a meeting in Rome.
They set a bilateral trade target of EUR 20 billion by 2029.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. Italy is primarily a machinery supplier to India, with machinery making up nearly 40% of Italian exports, while steel, electronics and chemicals are Indian exports to Italy. Bilateral trade stood at EUR 14.2 billion in 2024, so the 2029 target needs roughly 40% growth.
source: Bilateral trade stood at EUR 14.2 billion in 2024, with Italy acting primarily as a machinery supplier to India (EUR 2 billion, nearly 40% of Italian exports) while importing Indian steel, electronics, and chemicals.

prompt: In May 2026, India and Italy called for the first ministerial meeting of which connectivity initiative to take concrete steps in 2026?
explain: Modi and Meloni reaffirmed their commitment to IMEC and called for its first Ministerial meeting in 2026. They also pushed for early implementation of the India-EU FTA, whose negotiations concluded in 2026.
source: Both leaders reaffirmed their commitment to the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) and called for the first IMEC Ministerial meeting to take concrete steps in 2026.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to outcomes of the India-Italy summit in Rome in May 2026:
items: Joint Declaration of Intent — Nurse mobility from India to Italy
Defence industrial roadmap — Co-production of helicopters, naval platforms and electronic warfare systems
INNOVIT India — Innovation hub covering sectors from semiconductors to quantum computing
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs match the story. The two sides also signed MoUs on critical minerals and agriculture.
source: a defence industrial roadmap covering co-production of helicopters, naval platforms, and electronic warfare systems, and a Joint Declaration of Intent on nurse mobility from India to Italy

prompt: In May 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh signed three defence Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with South Korea in Seoul. Consider the following statements:
items: One of the MoUs provides for training exchanges between India's National Defence Academy and Korea National Defence University.
L&T and Hanwha signed three commercial agreements on defence technology at a business roundtable chaired by Singh in Seoul.
Rajnath Singh's two-nation tour, which ended in Seoul, began in Japan.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the training MoU links India's National Defence College (not the National Defence Academy) with Korea National Defence University, L&T and Hanwha signed two (not three) commercial agreements, and the tour began in Vietnam, not Japan. Both sides also discussed operationalising KIND-X, a joint platform for co-developing and co-producing defence systems.
source: L&T and Hanwha also signed two commercial agreements on defence technology at a business roundtable Singh chaired in Seoul.

prompt: During Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's visit to Seoul in May 2026, India and South Korea discussed operationalising KIND-X. What is KIND-X?
options: A joint platform for co-developing and co-producing defence systems
A biennial joint naval exercise held in the Indo-Pacific
A reciprocal military logistics support agreement
A joint satellite programme for maritime surveillance
explain: KIND-X, the India-Korea Defence Innovation Accelerator Ecosystem, is a joint platform for co-developing and co-producing defence systems. L&T and Hanwha also signed two commercial defence technology agreements at a business roundtable Singh chaired in Seoul.
source: Beyond the MoUs, both sides discussed operationalising KIND-X (India-Korea Defence Innovation Accelerator Ecosystem), a joint platform for co-developing and co-producing defence systems.

prompt: Consider the following statements about municipal bonds in India, as reported in May 2026:
items: The government is offering incentives of INR 10 billion for large municipal bond issues.
The government is offering 2% interest subsidies to encourage municipal bond issues.
Indian municipal bonds had raised only INR 45 billion over the previous nine years.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the story says the incentive for large issues is INR 1 billion (USD 10 million), not INR 10 billion. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. These incentives aim to revive a stagnant market that raised only INR 45 billion in nine years.
source: the government is offering INR 1 billion (USD 10 million) incentives for large issues and 2% interest subsidies

prompt: In May 2026, which state-backed institution was reported to be stepping in as an anchor investor for debut municipal bond issues by Indian cities?
options: National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
Small Industries Development Bank of India
explain: The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development and commercial banks are acting as anchor investors. Close to a dozen cities, including at least seven in Maharashtra, are preparing debut issues. New rules will also allow refinancing of old loans and higher rates for retail investors.
source: Key players like the state-backed National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development and commercial banks are stepping in as anchor investors.

prompt: Consider the following statements about US tariffs affecting India, as of May 2026:
items: After the US Supreme Court scrapped the "Liberation Day" tariffs, Washington imposed a 10% flat duty under Section 301.
The US Court of International Trade declared the 10% flat duties unlawful.
Following the US Court of International Trade ruling, US Customs continued to collect the 10% duty from everyone except the specific plaintiffs.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the 10% flat duty was imposed under Section 122, while Section 301 was used to launch investigations into Indian trade practices. Statements 2 and 3 are correct, as the Court of International Trade's win against the duties was narrow and benefited only the plaintiffs.
source: Washington pivoted to a 10% flat duty under Section 122 and launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices (we covered it here).

prompt: Consider the following statements about US investment commitments in India announced by Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal in May 2026:
items: US companies had committed over USD 60 billion in investments over the preceding six months.
The commitments were concentrated in textiles, food processing and agriculture.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the commitments were concentrated in data centres, digital infrastructure and advanced manufacturing. Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari separately urged Indian firms to form joint ventures with US companies to absorb know-how in infrastructure, mobility and logistics.
source: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal announced that US companies have committed over USD 60 billion in investments over the last six months, concentrated in data centres, digital infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India-Africa Forum Summit postponed in May 2026:
items: The postponement followed a WHO warning about an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo involving a strain for which a vaccine is available.
It was to be the fourth edition of the summit, held with the African Union in New Delhi.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the WHO said the outbreak involves a rare strain for which no vaccine exists. The fourth summit, scheduled for 28 to 31 May 2026 in New Delhi, was to cover trade, investment, digital technology and global governance, and the MEA said new dates would be finalised in due course.
source: India and the African Union (AU) have postponed the fourth India-Africa Forum Summit, which was scheduled for May 28–31 in New Delhi, citing an "emerging public health situation" in Africa.

prompt: Consider the following statements about US trade measures affecting India, as of May 2026:
items: The US Supreme Court scrapped the "Liberation Day" tariffs, which had been the original basis for the India–US trade deal.
After the ruling, Washington imposed a flat duty of 18% under Section 122.
The US launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the flat duty under Section 122 is 10%, not 18%. India–US trade talks stalled after the Supreme Court ruling, and US negotiators were expected in India in June 2026.
source: Washington pivoted to a 10% flat duty under Section 122 and launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices

prompt: In May 2026, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was due to attend a Quad foreign ministers' meeting. Which group of countries makes up the Quad?
options: India, the US, Australia and Japan
India, the US, Australia and South Korea
India, the US, Japan and the Philippines
India, the US, the UK and Australia
explain: Rubio was to meet his counterparts from India, Australia and Japan at the Quad ministerial meeting. Despite the trade friction, the security imperative in the Indo-Pacific remains what holds the India–US partnership together.
source: Rubio heads into a Quad ministerial meeting on Tuesday with counterparts from India, Australia, and Japan.

prompt: In May 2026, India and Cyprus elevated their relationship to a Strategic Partnership. Consider the following statements about the outcomes of that visit:
items: Cyprus joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI).
Both sides announced a defence cooperation roadmap for 2026–2031.
Cyprus announced plans to open a trade centre in Chennai.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the planned Cypriot trade centre is in Mumbai, not Chennai. The visit also produced six MoUs, a cyber security dialogue and a joint task force on shipping and infrastructure.
source: Separately, both sides announced a defence cooperation roadmap for 2026–2031, a cyber security dialogue, a joint task force on shipping and infrastructure, and Cyprus' entry into the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI).

prompt: The northern corridor of the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), stalled as of May 2026, is designed to run overland to European ports through which countries?
explain: The overland route passes through Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Israel. It is stalled because Haifa port faces Iranian strikes, Jordan is reluctant to be a transit corridor and Saudi-Israeli normalisation has been frozen since 2023.
source: the northern corridor, designed to run overland through Saudi Arabia, Jordan, and Israel to European ports

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) as reported in May 2026:
items: IMEC's eastern segment, connecting India to the Gulf, broke ground in April 2025.
Cyprus formed an IMEC friends group within the EU during its presidency of the Council of the European Union.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements match the story. Cyprus is proposing itself, alongside Greece and Italy, as IMEC's European entry point, and India and Cyprus set up a bilateral connectivity dialogue to take this forward.
source: IMEC's eastern segment, connecting India to the Gulf, broke ground in April 2025.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Ethiopia relations as of May 2026:
items: In May 2026, India signed a bilateral accession protocol in Geneva supporting Ethiopia's membership of the World Trade Organization.
India is Ethiopia's largest trading partner.
Bilateral relations were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during the Indian Prime Minister's visit to Ethiopia in December 2025.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The second statement is wrong because India is Ethiopia's second-largest trading partner, not its largest. The first and third are correct. Ethiopia is still negotiating its WTO entry, and its Working Party held a seventh round in April 2026.
source: India is Ethiopia's second-largest trading partner, and bilateral relations were elevated to a Strategic Partnership during Modi's visit to Ethiopia in December 2025.

prompt: In May 2026, India test-launched the nuclear-capable Agni-1 missile. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It was launched from Chandipur, Odisha, under the Strategic Forces Command.
It is a short-range ballistic missile.
It has a range of 700–1,200 km.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the story describes the Agni-1 as a short-range ballistic missile launched from Chandipur, Odisha under the Strategic Forces Command, with a range of 700–1,200 km. In the same week, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh flagged off Suryastra, India's first 300 km Universal Rocket Launching System.
source: India successfully test-launched the nuclear-capable Agni-1 short-range ballistic missile from Chandipur, Odisha on Thursday, validating all operational parameters under the Strategic Forces Command.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Assam, 2026 Bill tabled in the Assam Legislative Assembly in May 2026:
items: It would replace religion-specific personal laws for all residents except Scheduled Tribes.
It provides for up to seven years' imprisonment for bigamy and polygamy.
It requires all live-in relationships to be registered within one month.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are provisions of the Bill. It also sets the minimum marriage age at 21 for men and 18 for women, and makes registration of all marriages and divorces compulsory.
source: The Bill requires all live-in relationships to be registered within one month.

prompt: A Uniform Civil Code, which Assam sought to enact through a Bill tabled in May 2026, is enshrined as a Directive Principle of State Policy under which Article of the Constitution of India?
explain: The UCC is a directive principle under Article 44. The BJP-led central government has long promised a national UCC but has never tabled one in Parliament.
source: enshrined as a directive principle under Article 44 of the Constitution, but has never tabled one in Parliament.

prompt: In May 2026, Assam tabled a Bill that would make it the third Indian state to enact a Uniform Civil Code. Which two states had enacted one before it?
explain: Uttarakhand enacted a UCC in 2024 and Gujarat in March 2026. Assam would be the first state where a UCC affects a large Muslim population, making it a test of enforceability.
source: If passed, Assam would become the third Indian state to enact a UCC, after Uttarakhand in 2024 and Gujarat in March this year.

prompt: Consider the following statements about US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India in May 2026:
items: His four-day India visit concluded with the Quad foreign ministers' meeting.
He described Pakistan as the "primary interlocutor" with Iran at the Quad foreign ministers' meeting.
He said India's concerns about cross-border terrorism from Pakistan did not arise in the context of Pakistan's mediation in the US-Iran conflict.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: Rubio called Pakistan the "primary interlocutor" at the NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg, three days before landing in India. Washington's language has escalated from praising Islamabad's "constructive role" in July 2025, while Rubio insisted ties with other countries do not come at the expense of the strategic alliance with India.
source: Three days before landing in India, he called Pakistan the "primary interlocutor" at the NATO foreign ministers' meeting in Helsingborg.

prompt: In May 2026, the Union government barred households with piped natural gas (PNG) connections from refilling LPG cylinders. Consider the following statements:
items: India is the world's largest importer of LPG.
The order was issued by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
Affected consumers must surrender their LPG connection or take a transfer voucher within 30 days.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the story describes India as the world's second-largest LPG importer, not the largest. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Almost all of India's LPG imports come from Qatar and the UAE, and the West Asia crisis has choked these supplies.
source: India is the world's second-largest LPG importer, and the US-Israeli war on Iran has choked fuel supplies.

prompt: In May 2026, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman named fuel, fertiliser and foreign exchange as the economy's critical pressure points amid the West Asia crisis. Consider the following statements:
items: Excise duty cuts on petrol and diesel were costing the exchequer INR 1 lakh crore.
She attributed the pressures mainly to weakening domestic fundamentals.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Sitharaman said India's domestic fundamentals remain positive and resilient, and that the challenges are externally driven. Crude has risen from around USD 70 to over USD 115 per barrel since the Strait of Hormuz disruptions began in late February 2026.
source: excise duty cuts on petrol and diesel are already costing the exchequer INR 1 lakh crore (USD 11.7 billion)

prompt: In May 2026, the Quad launched a Critical Minerals Initiative Framework. How much government and private sector support does it intend to mobilise?
explain: The framework aims to mobilise USD 20 billion to strengthen critical mineral supply chains. It was rolled out alongside a separate Indo-Pacific energy security initiative.
source: They also rolled out a Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework with the intent to mobilise USD 20 billion in government and private sector support to strengthen critical mineral supply chains

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Quad foreign ministers' meeting of May 2026:
items: Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration — Quad's first initiative to pool maritime surveillance
Pax Silica — Welcomed as a pillar of shared economic security
Terror attacks condemned in the joint statement — Pahalgam and Bondi Beach
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The IPMSC is the Quad's first initiative to pool maritime surveillance. The joint statement welcomed Pax Silica as a pillar of shared economic security and explicitly condemned the attacks at Pahalgam and Bondi Beach. It also opposed the imposition of tolls on the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.
source: The ministers announced the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration (IPMSC), the Quad’s first initiative to pool maritime surveillance.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) negotiations as of May 2026:
items: Terms of Reference for the talks were signed in March 2026 during Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's visit to Ottawa.
The third round of negotiations was held in New Delhi.
Both sides aim to conclude the agreement by 2030.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are wrong. The Terms of Reference were signed in March 2026 during Mark Carney's visit to India, the third round ran in Ottawa rather than New Delhi, and both sides want to conclude the CEPA by the end of 2026 (2030 is the target year for USD 50 billion in bilateral trade). The third round ran alongside Goyal's visit with a delegation of over 100 companies.
source: A third round is running in parallel with Goyal's visit in Ottawa this week, with negotiators from both sides working through May 29.

prompt: In May 2026, as India and Canada advanced talks on a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, what target was cited for bilateral trade by 2030?
explain: The target is USD 50 billion by 2030, up from bilateral goods trade of around USD 8.5 billion. Ties had frozen in 2023 after then-PM Justin Trudeau alleged Indian involvement in the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar.
source: Bilateral trade in goods currently sits at around USD 8.5 billion. The target is USD 50 billion by 2030.

prompt: In May 2026, the Union government constituted a high-level committee to study demographic changes caused by illegal immigration and other 'unnatural' reasons. Consider the following statements about it:
items: The committee is headed by a retired High Court judge.
It is tasked with recommending a temporary mechanism for the identification, detention and deportation of illegal immigrants.
It has been directed to submit its report within six months.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong. The committee is headed by retired Supreme Court judge Prakash Prabhakar Navlekar, it must recommend a permanent mechanism, and it has one year to report, with six months only as a possible extension. The panel will also propose measures on border management, national security and population stabilisation.
source: Headed by retired Supreme Court Judge Prakash Prabhakar Navlekar, the panel is tasked with analysing population shifts across religious and social communities and recommending a permanent mechanism for the identification, detention, and deportation of illegal immigrants.

prompt: Consider the following statements about SARTHAK-PDS, approved in May 2026:
items: It was approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs.
It has an outlay of INR 25,530 crore and runs through March 2031.
It merges two existing schemes, pairing financial support for state-level grain transport with a technology layer.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The CCEA approved the INR 25,530 crore overhaul of the Public Distribution System on 27 May 2026, and it brings two existing schemes under one umbrella. The government expects food grain travel distances to fall by 15–50%, saving roughly INR 280 crore annually.
source: On Wednesday, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approved SARTHAK-PDS, an INR 25,530 crore (USD 3 billion) overhaul of the Public Distribution System (PDS) running through March 2031.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of AI-powered platforms under SARTHAK-PDS, approved in May 2026, and their functions:
items: NIRMAL — Real-time beneficiary registry with cross-ministry integration
ASHA — Route optimisation and QR-code traceability of food grain
SAKSHAM — Vehicle tracking and demand forecasting in grain transport
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: ASHA is wrongly matched: it handles grievance redressal across calls, WhatsApp, IVRS and multilingual chatbots, while route optimisation and QR-code traceability fall under SAKSHAM. SAKSHAM is meant to cut waste in food grain transport.
source: ASHA handles grievance redressal across calls, WhatsApp, IVRS, and multilingual chatbots.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's visit to Canada in May 2026:
items: In Toronto, he co-chaired an investment roundtable with Canadian pension funds and banks alongside Canada's Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu.
Canada announced a Team Canada Trade Mission to India for November 2026, the first such delegation since the diplomatic reset earlier in 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements match the story. Goyal co-chaired the Toronto roundtable with Maninder Sidhu, who announced the November trade mission to India as the first since the diplomatic reset. Goyal also met Canadian firms across insurance, banking, food processing and critical minerals.
source: Sidhu announced a Team Canada Trade Mission to India in November, the first such delegation since the diplomatic reset earlier this year.

prompt: In May 2026, Siddaramaiah resigned as Chief Minister of Karnataka. Consider the following statements:
items: His resignation takes effect only once the state Governor formally accepts it.
Under the power-sharing deal struck after the 2023 assembly elections, DK Shivakumar was to hold the Chief Minister's post for the first 2.5 years.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: A Chief Minister's resignation becomes effective only on the Governor's formal acceptance. Under the 2.5-year rotational deal, Siddaramaiah took the first innings and Shivakumar stayed on as Deputy Chief Minister, with the handover due in November 2025.
source: He submitted his resignation, though it only takes effect once the state Governor formally accepts it.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Mysuru Urban Development Authority (MUDA) land scam case involving Siddaramaiah, as reported in May 2026:
items: The Governor sanctioned Siddaramaiah's prosecution in August 2024.
The Central Bureau of Investigation attached properties worth INR 300 crore in the case.
The Lokayukta, Karnataka's anti-corruption ombudsman, continues to investigate the case.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: It was the Enforcement Directorate, not the CBI, that attached properties worth INR 300 crore (USD 35 million). The case dogged Siddaramaiah's second term, which ended with his resignation in May 2026.
