prompt: In July 2026, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) issued notices to the quick-commerce platform Swiggy Instamart. Consider the following statements:
items: Failure to respond with the required proof of quality checks within the deadline would attract action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
FSSAI holds e-commerce platforms responsible for compliance only for products they sell directly, not for those listed by third-party sellers.
The 'dark stores' used by quick-commerce apps are small warehouses that customers cannot access.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: FSSAI insists platforms own compliance for everything they list, whether or not a third-party seller is involved. FSSAI served Instamart nine notices over items such as expired whey protein, rotten eggs and unsafe infant formula, after Blinkit faced similar complaints in May 2026.
source: FSSAI is now insisting e-commerce platforms own compliance for everything they list, third-party seller or not, a standard the sector's breakneck expansion had largely outrun.

prompt: Consider the following statements about INS Mahendragiri, commissioned by the Indian Navy in July 2026:
items: It was built by Mazagaon Dock Shipbuilders Limited.
It was commissioned into the Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam.
It carries over 75% indigenous content.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: INS Mahendragiri was built by Mazagaon Dock Shipbuilders Limited, joined the Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam and carries over 75% indigenous content. It is the sixth Project 17A stealth frigate and can be fitted with the BrahMos cruise missile.
source: The Indian Navy commissioned INS Mahendragiri, the sixth Project 17A stealth frigate, into its Eastern Fleet at Visakhapatnam on Saturday, July 11.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's merchandise trade data for June 2026, released by the Commerce Ministry in July 2026:
items: The merchandise trade deficit widened to USD 30.43 billion, a five-month high.
Merchandise exports grew faster than merchandise imports year-on-year.
Merchandise exports were led by gems, jewellery and engineering goods.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Exports rose 15.5% to USD 40.41 billion, while imports grew almost twice as fast, up 31% to USD 70.84 billion. The government attributed the larger import bill to higher global prices for crude and precious metals rather than to rising volumes.
source: Merchandise exports rose 15.5% year-on-year in June to USD 40.41 billion, led by gems, jewellery, and engineering goods.

prompt: In July 2026, India began reviewing its trade agreement with Japan. Consider the following statements about the India-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and related ties:
items: The CEPA was signed and took effect in 2011.
The 7th India–Japan CEPA Joint Committee Meeting was held in New Delhi in March 2026.
Japan is India's fifth-largest source of foreign direct investment.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the 7th Joint Committee Meeting was held in Tokyo, not New Delhi. At that meeting India called for a more balanced bilateral trade relationship.
source: The two sides held the 7th India–Japan CEPA Joint Committee Meeting in Tokyo in March 2026

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India–Japan economic ties, as reported in July 2026:
items: Indian imports from Japan in 2025-26 — USD 21.43 billion
Indian exports to Japan in 2025-26 — USD 6 billion
Japan's investment pledge for the next decade — JPY 10 trillion
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correctly matched. Imports rose from USD 9.8 billion in 2015-16 while exports grew only from USD 4.6 billion, so the deficit nearly tripled to USD 15.4 billion. India is now using the review to seek more Japanese investment instead of relying on goods exports.
source: Indian imports from Japan skyrocketed from USD 9.8 billion in 2015-16 to USD 21.43 billion in 2025-26, while India's exports crawled from USD 4.6 billion to just USD 6 billion.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the interim India-US trade pact of February 2026:
items: Under the pact, Washington offered a 10% tariff track for Indian exports.
The pact was unwound by a Supreme Court ruling in May 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements are wrong: Washington offered an 18% tariff track, not 10%, and the Supreme Court ruling that unwound the pact came in March 2026, not May. The 10% figure is the temporary tariff now in place, which lapses on 24 July 2026.
source: The Supreme Court ruling in March unwound it weeks later, and a temporary 10% tariff now lapses on July 24.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's first hydrogen-powered train, which the Prime Minister was scheduled to flag off from Jind, Haryana, on 17 July 2026:
items: Its commercial operations will run on the 89-kilometre Jind–Sonipat section under Northern Railway.
It is a 10-car, 1,200 KW trainset that runs on hydrogen fuel cells.
It is the first train under the Hydrogen for Heritage programme, which plans 35 such trains for dedicated freight corridors.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the Hydrogen for Heritage programme plans 35 trains for heritage and hill routes, not freight corridors. Each train costs roughly INR 80 crore, plus INR 70 crore in route infrastructure. Indian Railways approved the trainset in May 2026, and it emits only water vapour.
source: The launch is the first under the "Hydrogen for Heritage" programme, which plans 35 such trains for heritage and hill routes at roughly INR 80 crore (USD 8 million) per train, plus INR 70 crore (USD 7 million) in route infrastructure.

prompt: In July 2026, Indian seafarers were killed and injured in missile attacks on two tankers. Consider the following statements about the incident:
items: The Ministry of External Affairs lodged a strong protest with Iran's Deputy Chief of Mission.
The UAE Defence Ministry attributed the strike to two Iranian cruise missiles.
The tankers were in Iranian territorial waters when they were struck.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the UAE said the missiles were fired while the tankers sat in Omani waters, not Iranian waters. India protested to Iran's envoy but condemned the attacks without publicly naming Iran, leaving the attribution to the UAE.
source: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) Defence Ministry attributed the strike to two Iranian cruise missiles fired while the tankers sat in Omani waters.

prompt: In July 2026, India summoned Iran's deputy ambassador after missile attacks on two tankers carrying Indian crew. Through which strait were the tankers passing?
explain: The tankers MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa were struck while crossing the Strait of Hormuz, killing one Indian seafarer and injuring ten. The attacks followed fresh US action against Iran and a renewed threat to blockade the strait.
source: India summoned Iran's deputy ambassador yesterday after an Indian seafarer was killed and ten injured in missile attacks on two tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz.

prompt: In July 2026, India prohibited the import of goods produced wholly or partly through forced labour. Consider the following statements about this prohibition:
items: It defines forced labour using the wording of the International Labour Organization's 1930 Forced Labour Convention.
It took effect immediately on publication in the gazette.
It was brought in by amending the Foreign Trade Policy 2023.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the rule takes effect 30 days after gazette publication. Even then, nothing is blocked until the DGFT investigates and names specific products, with procedures to follow the Handbook of Procedures, 2023.
source: The notification inserts a new clause into the FTP defining forced labour by borrowing the International Labour Organization (ILO)'s 1930 Forced Labour Convention wording, and empowers the Centre to block specific goods once an inquiry finds evidence they were made with forced labour.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the United States Trade Representative's (USTR) Section 301 action on forced-labour imports, as of July 2026:
items: Number of economies under investigation — 60
Tariff proposed against India on 3 June 2026 — 12.5%
Subject of the other separate USTR probe affecting India — currency manipulation
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong because the other USTR probe concerns industrial overcapacity, not currency manipulation. Either probe could push India's current flat 10% US tariff higher.
source: India currently faces a flat 10% US tariff, and this is one of two separate USTR probes, the other into industrial overcapacity, that could push that rate higher.

prompt: In July 2026, which body amended India's Foreign Trade Policy to prohibit imports of goods made with forced labour?
options: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
explain: The DGFT issued the ban on 13 July 2026 by amending the Foreign Trade Policy 2023. It came five weeks after the US proposed fresh tariffs against India over the same issue.
source: India's Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) prohibited the import of goods produced wholly or partly through forced labour on Monday, amending the Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023 five weeks after Washington proposed fresh tariffs against India over the same issue.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Maldives economic ties as of July 2026:
items: The first round of India–Maldives Free Trade Agreement talks covered eight policy areas.
A Bilateral Investment Treaty is being pursued in parallel with the Free Trade Agreement.
India is the Maldives' largest trading partner.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because India is the Maldives' second-largest trading partner, not its largest. Bilateral trade rose 13.54 per cent to USD 771.76 million in 2025-26, and on 8 July 2026 the two commerce ministers agreed to expedite both the FTA and the BIT.
source: India is the Maldives' second-largest trading partner, with bilateral trade reaching USD 771.76 million in 2025-26, up 13.54 per cent from USD 679.70 million the year before.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which took effect in July 2026:
items: The UK removes duties immediately on 96.8% of tariff lines, covering 97.7% of trade value.
India removes duties immediately on 64.1% of tariff lines and phases out tariffs on a further 21%.
Dairy products are among the sectors India opens to UK imports on a phased basis.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because dairy, grains and oilseeds stay off the table entirely, the same defensive basket India has protected in every recent trade agreement. Indian textiles, leather, footwear, marine products, gems and jewellery gain duty-free entry against UK tariffs that ran from 4% to 20%.
source: Dairy, grains, and oilseeds stay off the table entirely, the same defensive basket India has protected in every recent trade agreement.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the India-UK CETA, which came into force in July 2026:
items: Completely built UK vehicles allowed each year at preferential tariffs — 37,000
Services sub-sectors covered by market access — 137
Value of India's procurement market opened to UK suppliers — around USD 120 billion
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong. India's procurement market opens to UK suppliers at around USD 114 billion, while roughly USD 120 billion is the size of the UK's own procurement market. The automobile opening comes through a phased quota of 37,000 vehicles a year.
source: India's procurement market opens to UK suppliers at around USD 114 billion.

prompt: The Double Contribution Convention, linked to the India-UK trade agreement that took effect in July 2026, exempts eligible Indian professionals and employers from which UK levy?
explain: The convention exempts eligible Indian professionals and employers from UK National Insurance contributions for stays of up to five years. It covers roughly 75,000 workers and 900 employers, and it protects India's services trade with the UK, where India ran a surplus of nearly USD 7.9 billion in 2024.
source: The linked Double Contribution Convention exempts eligible Indian professionals and employers from the UK's National Insurance contributions for stays of up to five years, covering roughly 75,000 workers and 900 employers.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's purchases of Russian oil and a bipartisan US Senate sanctions bill, as reported in July 2026:
items: India's imports of Russian oil rose by 34% in June 2026 to a record USD 5.2 billion.
In June 2026, India overtook China to become the world's biggest buyer of Russian oil.
The Senate bill would allow the US President to waive the tariffs in the US national interest.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because India was the second-biggest buyer of Russian oil, behind China. The bill would let the President impose tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian energy, down from a 500% ceiling, and he could waive them in the US national interest.
source: India’s imports of Russian oil surged by 34% in June to a record USD 5.2 billion, making it the world’s second-biggest buyer of Russian oil behind China.

prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0. Consider the following statements:
items: Semicon 2.0 has an outlay of USD 13.3 billion (INR 1.275 trillion) and covers chip design, equipment, materials, fabrication, packaging, research and skills.
The 2021 semiconductor mission approved 12 manufacturing units and 24 design projects.
Three facilities approved under the 2021 semiconductor mission were already producing commercially by July 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: Semicon 2.0 is a USD 13.3 billion programme spanning design to skills, and the 2021 mission approved 12 manufacturing units and 24 design projects, with three facilities already producing commercially. Semicon 2.0 shifts the focus from landing factories to building the ecosystem around them.
source: The 2021 semiconductor mission has approved 12 manufacturing units and 24 design projects; three facilities are already producing commercially.

prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved USD 6.5 billion over five years for mobile-phone manufacturing. What base incentive can firms receive under it, before any extra for local sourcing?
explain: Firms can receive 2.25%–5% of eligible sales, plus up to 1.5% for sourcing key components locally. TBB notes that pairing phone incentives with chip subsidies builds demand alongside supply.
source: Firms can receive 2.25%–5% of eligible sales, plus up to 1.5% for sourcing key components locally.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's electronics sector, as reported in July 2026:
items: India's global rank in mobile-phone manufacturing — Second
Mobile-phone exports in FY2024–25 — USD 20.9 billion
Domestic value addition across electronics — 40%–45%
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong because domestic value addition across electronics remains just 18%–20%. India is the world's second-largest mobile-phone manufacturer, with production of USD 56.9 billion in FY2024–25.
source: Domestic value addition across electronics remains just 18%–20%.

prompt: Consider the following statements about ethanol-blended petrol in India as of July 2026:
items: Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari said that whether pumps should dispense multiple blends was a matter for his own ministry to decide.
India had reached 20% ethanol blending, with E20 sold at every fuel station in the country.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: Gadkari said the question of multiple blends sits with the Petroleum Ministry and declined to comment. Statement 2 is correct, as India has hit 20% blending and E20 is sold at every fuel station. Gadkari also said motorists who do not want ethanol-blended petrol can buy 100% petrol at a higher price.
source: India has hit 20% ethanol blending, with E20 now sold at every fuel station in the country.

prompt: In July 2026, which body issued the directive ordering that Indian seafarers not be deployed on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz?
explain: The Directorate General of Shipping issued the directive on 15 July 2026. It said recent attacks had raised the risks to seafarers and commercial ships significantly.
source: Issued late Wednesday by the Directorate General of Shipping, the directive says recent attacks have raised the risks to seafarers and commercial ships "significantly".

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's July 2026 order on Indian seafarers and the Strait of Hormuz:
items: The order is addressed to shipowners, ship managers and recruitment firms.
The ban on deploying Indian seafarers is for a fixed period of 90 days.
After an Indian seafarer was killed aboard the Al Bahiyah, India publicly named Iran as responsible.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The ban runs until further orders, not for a fixed period. India summoned Iran's deputy ambassador after the Al Bahiyah death but did not publicly name Tehran as responsible.
source: India has ordered shipowners, ship managers, and recruitment firms to stop deploying Indian seafarers on any vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with the ban running until further orders.

prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved the National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 (NIPU-2026). Consider the following statements about it:
items: It replaces a 2012 framework that had expired in 2019.
It offers investors a guaranteed return on equity of 12% to 16%.
It converts fixed costs to rupees from the first year of a plant's operation.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: fixed costs are converted to rupees only after four years, which shields investors from currency volatility. The policy targets new gas-based plants to cut India's reliance on costly urea imports.
source: To lure private capital, the government is offering a guaranteed 12% to 16% return on equity and shielding investors from currency volatility by converting fixed costs to rupees after four years.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's urea sector, as reported when NIPU-2026 was approved in July 2026:
items: Share of annual urea requirement imported — 26%
Existing urea manufacturing units — 33
Estimated saving per plant compared with the old policy — over INR 250 crore
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three are correct. India imports 26% of its urea, and NIPU-2026 aims to add new gas-based plants to the existing 33 units. The government estimates savings of over INR 250 crore per plant compared with the old policy.
source: India imports 26% of its annual urea requirement.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the draft Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) norms for passenger cars circulated in India in July 2026:
items: The draft was circulated by the Ministry of Power.
Carmakers that miss their targets can buy credits from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency at a published price.
Each manufacturer's specific target is scaled to the average engine displacement of the vehicles it sells.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: targets are scaled to the weighted unladen mass of a maker's sales, so a fleet of heavy SUVs gets a looser limit than one of small hatchbacks. The buyout price starts at INR 2,500 per gram per kilometre in 2027-28 and rises to INR 4,500 by 2031-32, and 90 per cent of the proceeds go to state governments.
source: Carmakers running a deficit can purchase credits from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency at INR 2,500 (USD 26) per gram of carbon dioxide per kilometre in 2027-28, rising to INR 4,500 (USD 47) by 2031-32.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to how vehicles are counted in the compliance calculation under India's draft CAFE norms of July 2026:
items: Electric vehicles — 3.0 times actual sales volume
Plug-in hybrids — 2.5 times actual sales volume
Strong hybrids — 1.6 times actual sales volume
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three multipliers match the draft. Ethanol flex-fuel vehicles get a separate 22.3 per cent discount on declared emissions, and the fleet target falls from 94.76 grams per kilometre in 2027-28 to 78.90 by 2031-32.
source: Electric vehicles count 3.0 times their actual sales volume in the compliance maths, plug-in hybrids 2.5 times, and strong hybrids 1.6 times.

prompt: Carmakers that missed India's CAFE-II fuel economy targets in FY23 argued that penalty provisions which took effect on 1 January 2023 could not apply retrospectively. Under which law are these penalty provisions?
options: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
explain: The makers said the Energy Conservation Act's penalty provisions began three quarters of the way through the assessment year. Eight carmakers missed the 113 gram cap in FY23, no penalty was ever levied, and by July 2026 the Centre had dropped the matter.
source: The companies argued the Energy Conservation Act's penalty provisions only took effect on January 1, 2023, three quarters of the way through the assessment year, so applying them across all of FY23 would be retrospective.

prompt: In July 2026, the Indian Navy announced the commissioning of Malvan. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It is the second vessel of the Mahe class of Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft.
It was built at Cochin Shipyard Limited in Kochi with over 80 per cent indigenous content.
It is designed mainly for anti-submarine operations in deep ocean waters.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. Malvan is built for anti-submarine work in shallow coastal waters, where larger warships cannot operate effectively. It was scheduled to be commissioned on 22 July 2026.
source: Built at Cochin Shipyard Limited in Kochi with over 80 per cent indigenous content, the craft is designed for anti-submarine work in shallow coastal waters, where larger warships cannot operate effectively.

prompt: In July 2026, the Codex Alimentarius Commission adopted international quality standards for large cardamom, coriander and vanilla. Consider the following statements:
items: The standards were adopted at the Commission's session held in Geneva.
The Codex Alimentarius Commission is run jointly by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Health Organization.
The standards were finalised at a meeting of the India-hosted Codex Committee on Spices and Culinary Herbs in Kochi.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because the India-hosted committee finalised the standards at a meeting in Guwahati in October 2025, not Kochi. Codex sets food safety benchmarks that governments and importers reference, so harmonised standards ease market access for Indian spice exporters.
source: The standards were finalised at the Codex Committee on Spices and Culinary Herbs, which India hosts, at a meeting in Guwahati in October 2025.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the amendment to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) taken up for debate in Parliament's Monsoon Session in July 2026:
items: It cuts the maximum prison sentence for FCRA violations from five years to one year.
It allows a government-appointed authority to control and dispose of foreign contributions, and assets created from them, when an organisation's FCRA registration ends.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The amendment both lowers the maximum prison term to one year and lets a government-appointed authority take over foreign-funded assets once registration ends. The FCRA governs how Indian organisations receive and use overseas donations.
source: The proposed amendment cuts the maximum prison sentence for violations from five years to one.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Constitution Amendment Bill on removing ministers held in custody, as it stood in July 2026:
items: It would apply to the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers as well as other ministers.
It applies to custody over an alleged offence carrying a maximum sentence of at least five years.
The parliamentary committee examining it submitted its final report just before the Monsoon Session opened.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. On 17 July 2026 the committee deferred its report for further consultation, after a draft that proposed suspension in place of removal. The bill would remove ministers, including the PM and CMs, after 30 consecutive days in custody over such an offence.
source: The Constitution Amendment Bill would remove ministers, including the Prime Minister and Chief Ministers, after 30 consecutive days in custody over an alleged offence carrying a maximum sentence of at least five years.

prompt: In July 2026, Skyroot Aerospace launched Vikram 1, India's first privately developed orbital rocket. Consider the following statements:
items: Vikram 1 was launched from the Indian Space Research Organisation's Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
On its maiden Mission Aagaman, Vikram 1 placed its payloads in a 450 kilometre low Earth orbit.
Skyroot's earlier Vikram S test in 2022 also achieved orbit.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. The 2022 Vikram S test reached space but did not enter orbit, which is why Vikram 1 counts as India's first private orbital launch. The launch makes India the third country after the US and China where a private company has achieved orbital launch capability.
source: The launch goes beyond Skyroot’s Vikram S test in 2022, which reached space but did not enter orbit, and makes India the third country after the US and China where a private company has achieved orbital launch capability.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) batteries, as updated to Parliament in July 2026:
items: It has a budget of INR 18,100 crore and targets 50 GWh of domestic capacity.
Four firms hold capacity allocations totalling 40 GWh.
Two of the beneficiary firms have already claimed incentives under the scheme.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because none of the four firms has claimed an incentive, since payouts require the production and sale of qualifying Indian-made cells. Beneficiaries reported only INR 5,180 crore of investment by May 31, 2026, against the INR 45,000 crore originally envisaged.
source: Four firms hold allocations totalling 40 GWh, but none has claimed an incentive, which requires the production and sale of qualifying Indian-made cells.

prompt: In July 2026, the government updated Parliament on the PLI scheme for automobiles and auto components. Consider the following pairs:
items: Scheme outlay — INR 18,100 crore
Jobs created by March 31, 2026 — 67,820
Investment by manufacturers by March 31, 2026 — INR 5,180 crore
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Only pair 2 is correct. The scheme's outlay is INR 25,938 crore, not INR 18,100 crore (the budget of the ACC battery programme), and manufacturers had invested INR 44,326 crore, not INR 5,180 crore (the investment reported by ACC beneficiaries). The government had disbursed INR 2,386 crore in incentives across 225 units.
source: Under the INR 25,938-crore (USD 2.7-billion) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto components, manufacturers had invested INR 44,326 crore (USD 4.6 billion) and created 67,820 jobs by March 31, 2026.

prompt: According to a February 2026 update, how much installed capacity had been set up under the PLI scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell batteries?
explain: The February 2026 update reported just 1 GWh of installed capacity, all of it belonging to Ola. Beneficiaries had been given two years to set up factories when capacity was awarded in March 2022, against a scheme target of 50 GWh.
source: A February 2026 update reported just 1 GWh of installed capacity, entirely belonging to Ola.

prompt: In July 2026, India lodged a protest with Russia after a missile strike killed four Indian crew members aboard the cargo vessel MV Golden Leo. The ship was departing which port when it was attacked?
explain: The Golden Leo was attacked on the evening of 19 July 2026 while leaving Ukraine's Odessa port. Five of its 17 crew were Indian nationals, and one survivor is in a critical condition.
source: On the evening of July 19, 2026, the cargo vessel Golden Leo was attacked while departing Odessa.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's response to the July 2026 missile strike on the MV Golden Leo:
items: The Ministry of External Affairs summoned Russia's Chargé d'Affaires in New Delhi.
Ukraine's Navy said Russian forces launched three cruise missiles at the ship.
It was the first time in 2026 that India had protested to a foreign power over the deaths of seafarers.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because this was the third such protest in six weeks. India had earlier summoned the United States twice and Iran once over crew losses during the Iran war. The MEA conveyed its 'grave concerns and unequivocal condemnation' to Chargé d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov, a notable step given that Russia is one of India's closest partners.
source: This is the third time in six weeks India has protested a foreign power over dead seafarers.

prompt: In July 2026, which body granted marketing authorisation to Qdenga, the first dengue vaccine cleared for use in India?
options: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
explain: The CDSCO, India's drug regulator, authorised the vaccine on 20 July 2026 for people aged 4 to 60. The Indian Council of Medical Research is instead among the domestic developers with its own dengue candidate in trials.
source: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), India's drug regulator, authorised the Dengue Tetravalent Vaccine (Live, Attenuated), manufactured by Germany's Takeda GmbH and imported by its Indian arm.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Qdenga, the dengue vaccine approved in India in July 2026:
items: It is a live, attenuated tetravalent vaccine manufactured by India's Panacea Biotec.
It is administered as a single dose to people aged 4 to 60.
It holds approval in 24 countries.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the vaccine is manufactured by Germany's Takeda GmbH, the schedule is two doses given three months apart, and it holds approval in 42 countries (24 million is the number of doses distributed). Panacea Biotec is a domestic developer with its own dengue candidate still in trials.
source: Qdenga already holds approval in 42 countries and World Health Organization (WHO) prequalification, with more than 24 million doses distributed globally.

prompt: In July 2026, President Droupadi Murmu visited Skopje and met North Macedonian President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova. Consider the following statements about the visit:
items: It was the first visit to North Macedonia by an Indian president.
The two sides agreed to double bilateral trade by 2030.
India agreed to double North Macedonia's training places under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) programme.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the leaders agreed to double bilateral trade without setting any deadline. India also welcomed North Macedonia's interest in three India-backed climate and infrastructure groupings, though no binding deals were announced.
source: The leaders agreed to double bilateral trade, without setting a deadline.

prompt: In July 2026, President Droupadi Murmu toured Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania. Which of these countries is already a member of the European Union?
explain: Romania, the final stop of the tour, is already an EU member, while Moldova and North Macedonia are EU candidates. Murmu's stops in Moldova and North Macedonia were both firsts for an Indian president.
source: Moldova and North Macedonia are EU candidates, while Romania, Murmu’s final stop, is already a member.

prompt: In July 2026, India deposited its instrument of acceptance for the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies. Consider the following statements about the agreement:
items: It is the first WTO pact with an environmental sustainability objective.
It bans subsidies tied to illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and to overfished stocks.
Aquaculture and inland fisheries fall outside its scope.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The agreement is the first WTO pact with an environmental sustainability objective, and it bans subsidies tied to illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and to overfished stocks. It leaves aquaculture and inland fisheries out, which shields India's shrimp exports, the bulk of its seafood trade.
source: Aquaculture and inland fisheries stay outside its scope, which shields India's shrimp exports, the bulk of its seafood trade.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's Trade Policy Review at the World Trade Organization (WTO), which opened in July 2026:
items: It was India's eighth Trade Policy Review and covered the period 2021 to 2025.
India's Trade Policy Review at the WTO is conducted every two years.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The review is India's 8th and covers 2021 to 2025, but it is held every five years, not every two. Members filed more than 900 written questions, and Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal led India's delegation.
source: The review, conducted every five years, covers 2021 to 2025.

prompt: Consider the following statements in the context of US-India trade developments in July 2026:
items: Section 301 investigations by the United States cover unfair trade practices and can trigger tariffs.
The United States buys nearly 38% of India's pharmaceutical exports.
President Trump said generic drugs would face 100% tariffs from 1 August 2026.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. Generic drugs stay tariff-free for two years from 1 August, then face 100% tariffs for a year and 200% after that, a schedule meant to push manufacturers to reshore. The US buys USD 9.7 billion of India's USD 25.8 billion in pharmaceutical exports.
source: The United States buys USD 9.7 billion of Indian pharmaceutical exports, nearly 38% of India’s USD 25.8 billion in pharmaceutical exports.

prompt: In July 2026, in which city was the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Foreign Ministers' meeting held?
explain: A senior US official spoke on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' meeting in Manila. The official said the US-India trade deal was effectively complete and could be signed within three to four months.
source: Speaking anonymously on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Foreign Ministers' meeting in Manila, the official said "The deal... is there. We literally have the paper."

prompt: In July 2026, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting held in which city?
explain: The two ministers met in Manila on 22 July 2026 on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting. Jaishankar raised fair market access, supply-chain predictability and the trade imbalance.
source: The two met in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on Wednesday.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's trade with China in fiscal year 2025/26:
items: India's imports from China reached USD 112 billion, its highest from any nation.
Total India–China trade stood at USD 151.10 billion.
India's trade deficit with China was above USD 100 billion.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: India's imports from China hit USD 132 billion, not USD 112 billion, though they were its highest from any nation. In July 2026, Jaishankar raised this lopsided trade balance with Wang Yi in Manila, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting.
source: India's imports from China still hit USD 132 billion in fiscal year 2025/26, its highest from any nation, leaving a deficit above USD 100 billion within total trade of USD 151.10 billion.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the recovery in India–China relations as described in July 2026:
items: Ties began recovering after Prime Minister Modi met President Xi in October 2024.
The friction that preceded the recovery dated to the 2020 border clash.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct: the Modi–Xi meeting of October 2024 ended friction dating to the 2020 border clash. Since then direct flights have resumed and business visas for Chinese professionals have been eased.
source: Ties began recovering after Modi met President Xi in October 2024, ending friction that dated to the 2020 border clash.

prompt: In July 2026, the Atomic Energy Commission approved which site for India's first 220 MW and 55 MW small modular reactors?
explain: The Atomic Energy Commission approved Tarapur in Maharashtra for both small modular reactor designs. The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre is developing both models.
source: The Atomic Energy Commission approved Tarapur in Maharashtra for India’s first 220 MW and 55 MW small modular reactors.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's 2025 nuclear law, the SHANTI Act, as reported in July 2026:
items: It permits licensed private participation in nuclear equipment manufacturing.
Nuclear waste management remains under government control.
Fuel-cycle activities remain under government control.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the Act permits licensed private participation in plant operation, generation and manufacturing, while fuel-cycle activities, nuclear waste and security remain under government control. Adani, Tata Power and Reliance have shown interest, although none has joined the Tarapur projects.
source: But fuel-cycle activities, nuclear waste and security remain under government control.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's nuclear energy targets, as reported in July 2026:
items: Indigenous small reactors to be operating by 2033 — at least five
Funding backing the small reactor programme — INR 200 billion
Nuclear capacity goal for 2047 — 100 GW
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: India wants at least five indigenous small reactors running by 2033, backed by INR 200 billion (USD 2.3 billion). Its wider goal is to lift nuclear capacity from 8.8 GW to 100 GW by 2047.
source: India wants at least five indigenous small reactors operating by 2033, backed by INR 200 billion (USD 2.3 billion).

prompt: In July 2026, the Ministry of Civil Aviation reprimanded which body for failing to stop its officials influencing jobs for their relatives in the aviation sector?
explain: The ministry rebuked the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), India's aviation safety body, over weak conflict-of-interest controls. As of January 31, 51 DGCA officials had disclosed 59 relatives working in aviation.
source: India's Ministry of Civil Aviation has reprimanded the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) for failing to stop officials influencing jobs for their relatives in the sector.

prompt: In July 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced fast-track courts to prosecute those behind exam paper leaks. Consider the following statements:
items: Fast-track courts are dedicated benches designed to bypass India's overburdened judicial system.
Such courts have previously been used for terrorism, money laundering, and crimes against women and children.
The announcement was accompanied by a published court count, start date and draft legislation.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because no start date, court count or draft legislation was published. Modi also promised a tougher law against paper leaks and said the Cabinet would take up the issue.
source: Fast-track courts are dedicated benches designed to bypass India's overburdened judicial system, previously used for terrorism, money laundering, and crimes against women and children.

prompt: In July 2026, after mobile internet was suspended around Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site, the Internet Freedom Foundation cited an earlier Supreme Court ruling. What does that ruling require of internet suspension orders?
options: Each order must be published with written reasons
Each order must be approved by Parliament
Each order must be signed by the President
Each order must be issued by a High Court
explain: The ruling requires every suspension order to be published with written reasons. The Internet Freedom Foundation noted that no such order had been published by the Home Ministry, the Department of Telecommunications, the Delhi government or Delhi Police.
source: An earlier Supreme Court ruling requires every such order to be published with written reasons.

prompt: In July 2026, the Union government announced it would continue supplying E20 petrol nationwide. Consider the following statements about the decision:
items: The government said it will not restore E10 or ethanol-free petrol.
The government decided to move to ethanol blends above 20%.
The government conceded a 3% to 5% mileage loss in some vehicles designed for E10.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because no decision has been made on moving above 20% ethanol. The government said supplying several blends nationwide would be too costly and complex, and cited service records of over 200 million two-wheelers and 30 million cars showing no widespread engine damage.
source: The government stated that it will not restore E10 or ethanol-free petrol and says supplying several blends nationwide would be too costly and complex.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's ethanol blending programme as of July 2026:
items: E20 — 20% ethanol and 80% petrol
E10 — 10% ethanol
Foreign exchange saved by the programme — INR 1.97 lakh crore
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: E20 contains 20% ethanol and 80% petrol, E10 contains 10% ethanol, and the programme has saved INR 1.97 lakh crore in foreign exchange. It has also displaced 31.6 million tonnes of crude and transferred INR 1.66 lakh crore to farmers.
source: The programme has saved INR 1.97 lakh crore (USD 20.5 billion) in foreign exchange, displaced 31.6 million tonnes of crude, and transferred INR 1.66 lakh crore (USD 17.3 billion) to farmers.

prompt: India's 2021 ethanol blending roadmap recorded the automobile industry's insistence that which fuel remain available as a "protection grade" during the transition?
explain: The 2021 roadmap noted the industry wanted E10 kept available as a protection grade. In July 2026 the government declined to restore E10, after blending reached 20% between November 2025 and June 2026, five years ahead of the original target.
source: India’s 2021 roadmap recorded the automobile industry’s insistence that E10 remain available as a “protection grade” during the transition.

prompt: In July 2026, Gautam Adani asked the government to dilute rules on airport operators owning airlines. Consider the following statements about India's aviation sector as reported at the time:
items: Airport operators are capped at a 10% stake in scheduled airlines.
The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority sets aeronautical tariffs and also oversees slot coordination and ground handling.
IndiGo and Air India together control roughly 60% of domestic air traffic.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority sets aeronautical tariffs, but slot coordination and ground handling sit outside its remit, and IndiGo and Air India control roughly 90% of domestic traffic, not 60%. Adani has asked New Delhi to dilute the clause capping airport operators at a 10% stake in scheduled airlines.
source: Adani has asked New Delhi to dilute a clause capping airport operators at a 10% stake in scheduled airlines.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Kusha missile, which had its maiden flight-test in July 2026:
items: It is a long-range surface-to-air missile developed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO).
Its maiden flight-test was conducted from APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the coast of Odisha.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: DRDO flight-tested the Kusha long-range surface-to-air missile from APJ Abdul Kalam Island off Odisha on 23 July 2026, intercepting an electronic target that simulated a high-speed, high-altitude threat. DRDO says the system can engage fighter jets, missiles, drones and large aircraft, and its missiles, radars and command centre were developed by DRDO laboratories and industry partners.
source: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted the maiden flight-test of the Kusha long-range surface-to-air missile from APJ Abdul Kalam Island off Odisha on July 23, 2026, intercepting an electronic target simulating a high-speed, high-altitude aerial threat.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the response to the exam paper leak protests in July 2026:
items: The Prime Minister named Nandan Nilekani to head a six-member task force on examination reform.
Former Intelligence Bureau director Tapan Deka is a member of the task force.
The report of the 2019 Supreme Court-appointed panel on the Staff Selection Commission's 2017 recruitment exams, on which Nilekani sat, was made public.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first two statements are correct. The third is wrong because the 2019 panel's report was never made public. Former ISRO chairman S. Somanath is also on the new task force.
source: Nilekani sat on a Supreme Court-appointed panel in 2019 after alleged irregularities in the Staff Selection Commission's 2017 recruitment exams, and that report was never made public.

prompt: In July 2026, after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Education Minister, who took charge of the education ministry?
explain: Pralhad Joshi took charge on 26 July 2026, a day after President Droupadi Murmu accepted Pradhan's resignation. Joshi also continues to hold Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy.
source: Pralhad Joshi took charge of the education ministry on Sunday and opened with a review meeting.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the additional duty imposed by the United States on imports in July 2026 over forced-labour enforcement:
items: The duty followed an investigation under Section 301 of the US Trade Act, 1974.
India was placed in the 10% tier after its Directorate General of Foreign Trade notified a prohibition on forced-labour imports.
Generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones from India fall outside the new duty.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: USTR acted under Section 301, India got the 10% tier after the DGFT notified a forced-labour import prohibition on 13 July 2026, and generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones are among the roughly 45% of India's US exports outside the duty. USTR set 10% for economies that prohibit forced-labour imports and 12.5% for those that do not.
source: India's Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) notified such a prohibition on July 13, four days after the hearings closed.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the treatment of economies under the US forced-labour duty announced in July 2026:
items: Indonesia — 12.5% duty tier
India — Tariff-rate quota linked to purchases of American cotton and textile inputs
Sri Lanka — Tariff-rate quota linked to purchases of American cotton and textile inputs
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: None of the pairs is correct: Indonesia is among the 17 economies in the 10% tier, not the 12.5% tier, and the tariff-rate quotas go only to Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia, so neither India nor Sri Lanka has one. India's Commerce Ministry says it is pursuing the quota mechanism inside Bilateral Trade Agreement talks.
source: USTR will set up tariff-rate quotas for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, and Malaysia, running an initial three years.

prompt: In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved funding under Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan). How many chemical parks does the approval cover?
explain: The Cabinet cleared INR 30.3 billion on 24 July 2026 for three chemical parks. States compete for the three slots through a Challenge Route.
source: The Union Cabinet cleared INR 30.3 billion (USD 314 million) on July 24 for three chemical parks under Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan).

prompt: Consider the following statements about the terms of the BHAVYA Rasayan chemical parks scheme approved in July 2026:
items: The Centre grants up to INR 10 billion per park.
The Central grant is conditional on the host state contributing at least INR 5 billion.
Each site needs a minimum of 8 sq km of contiguous, encumbrance-free land.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three conditions are set out in the scheme's terms, and 8 sq km equals about 2,000 acres. TBB notes that the land and funding gates together favour states that already host chemical capacity.
source: The Centre grants up to INR 10 billion (USD 104 million) per park, conditional on the host state contributing at least INR 5 billion (USD 52 million).

prompt: Consider the following statements about the BHAVYA Rasayan scheme cleared by the Union Cabinet in July 2026:
items: Of the approved outlay, INR 30 billion is allocated for common infrastructure and utilities inside the parks.
The scheme runs until 2035.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The scheme runs until 2031, not 2035. Besides the INR 30 billion for shared infrastructure, INR 300 million is earmarked for administration, and the scheme was announced in the 2026 Union Budget.
source: The scheme runs until 2031, and was announced in the 2026 Union Budget.

prompt: In July 2026, UNESCO inscribed the Ancient Buddhist Site of Sarnath on the World Heritage List. Consider the following statements:
items: It was inscribed at the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee held in Busan, South Korea.
It became India's 45th property on the World Heritage List.
With this inscription, India ranks 2nd globally by number of UNESCO World Heritage sites.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong. India ranks 6th globally and 2nd in the Asia-Pacific. The site, in Varanasi, includes the Chaukhandi Stupa, the Dhamekh Stupa and the Ashokan Pillar, and is where the Buddha delivered his first sermon.
source: India now ranks 6th globally and 2nd in the Asia-Pacific by number of UNESCO World Heritage sites.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the proposed India–Israel free trade agreement (FTA) negotiations as of July 2026:
items: The second round of negotiations was held in New Delhi and concluded in July 2026.
The talks are framed by terms of reference signed in November 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The second round ended on 23 July 2026 after four days in New Delhi, and the November 2025 terms of reference continue to frame the talks. Both sides committed to an early conclusion but set no date, with merchandise trade at USD 3.93 billion in the last financial year.
source: The terms of reference signed in November 2025 continue to frame the talks, and both sides committed to an early conclusion without setting a date.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the bill on public examination malpractices introduced by the Centre in July 2026:
items: It was introduced in the Lok Sabha and proposes amendments to the Public Examinations Act of 2024.
Individual cheaters would face 5–10 years in prison, up from 3–5 years.
Complicit service providers would face a ban from public-examination work of eight years, double the current period.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The story supports all three statements. The bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 27 July 2026, raising prison terms for individuals and doubling the ban on service providers from four to eight years. It follows years of high-profile paper leaks, including the alleged NEET-UG leak.
source: Complicit service providers would face fines of up to INR 5 crore (~USD 518 thousand) and an 8-year ban from public-examination work, double the current four.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Public Examinations Act amendment bill introduced in July 2026:
items: Maximum fine for individual offenders — INR 50 lakh
Maximum fine for organised offences — INR 5 crore
Deadline for completing investigations — three months
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Only pair 1 is correct, as the individual fine ceiling rises fivefold to INR 50 lakh. Pair 2 is wrong because organised offences carry fines of up to INR 10 crore (INR 5 crore applies to complicit service providers), and pair 3 is wrong because investigations must finish within two months. Three months is the deadline from charge sheet to verdict in Special Fast Track Courts.
source: Investigations would have to finish within two months, with Courts of Session designated as Special Fast Track Courts running day-to-day trials and a three-month deadline from charge sheet to verdict.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Indian government measures for seafarers in July 2026:
items: The Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) barred the deployment of Indian seafarers on any vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz until further orders.
A Ministry of External Affairs advisory said attacks on commercial vessels around the Black Sea had killed five Indians since April 2026.
The DGMA's Black Sea circular did not impose a deployment restriction equivalent to its Hormuz order.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The DGMA's July 15 order bars deployment on vessels transiting Hormuz, the MEA's July 26 advisory cited five Indian deaths since April 2026, and the DGMA's July 23 Black Sea circular carries no equivalent restriction. For the Black Sea, sailors are instead told to weigh the risks and secure contracts covering medical care, evacuation, repatriation and compensation.
source: The same regulator's Black Sea circular, dated July 23, carries no equivalent restriction.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's Ethanol Blending Programme, as reported in July 2026:
items: The programme was launched in 2003.
It is administered by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
E20 refers to petrol blended with 20 per cent ethanol.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas administers the programme, not the Road Transport ministry that Nitin Gadkari has headed since 2014. In July 2026 the Centre ruled out any return to E10.
source: He argues the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas administers the Ethanol Blending Programme, launched in 2003, and issues its own statements on progress.

prompt: In July 2026, which High Court granted Union minister Nitin Gadkari leave to sue Meta, Google and X over deepfakes linking him to the ethanol-blending programme?
explain: The Bombay High Court granted leave on 27 July 2026. Gadkari flagged at least 24 posts as defamatory and sought INR 11 crore in damages plus their removal.
source: On Monday, the Bombay High Court granted Nitin Gadkari leave to sue Meta, Google, X, and unnamed accounts over deepfakes he says brand him the architect and beneficiary of India's ethanol-blending programme.

prompt: In July 2026, Gyan Bharatam, the Ministry of Culture's manuscripts mission, reported logging more than 11.9 million manuscripts. Consider the following pairs of tools on its AI-enabled portal and their functions:
items: Gyan Mitram — Interpretation and exploration of manuscripts
Pandulipi Darpan — Transliteration and translation of uploaded pages
BharatiyaGPT — Text, audio and voice queries via a Talk to Manuscript feature
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs match the functions the story gives for the portal's tools. The portal combines optical character recognition, handwritten text recognition, script identification, semantic search and machine translation. The 11.9 million texts were logged through a national survey covering every state and union territory.
source: Three tools sit on it: Gyan Mitram for interpretation and exploration, Pandulipi Darpan for transliteration and translation of uploaded pages, and BharatiyaGPT, which takes text, audio, and voice queries through a Talk to Manuscript feature.

prompt: In July 2026, the Supreme Court heard petitions alleging excess force against student protesters at Jantar Mantar. Consider the following statements about its order:
items: It ordered the release of every protester under the age of 18.
It barred coercive action against demonstrators.
It required police to preserve recordings from drones, body cameras and closed-circuit television.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three were part of the order. Chief Justice Surya Kant also told authorities to hold protesters' personal data without publishing it.
source: India's Supreme Court has ordered every under-18 protester released, barring coercive action against demonstrators and requiring police to preserve all footage of the crackdown.

prompt: In July 2026, an internal inquiry found that which federal anti-riot unit deployed at Jantar Mantar had issued pellet guns to its personnel?
explain: The Rapid Action Force issued pellet guns to at least a dozen personnel on 20 July and stopped using them on 23 July. Delhi Police denied issuing them, and the RAF sits under separate central command.
source: The Rapid Action Force (RAF), the federal anti-riot unit deployed at Jantar Mantar, issued pellet guns to at least a dozen personnel on the morning of July 20, according to an internal inquiry.

prompt: Consider the following statements about police surveillance of protesters in India as of July 2026:
items: A petition seeking to have the surveillance declared unconstitutional and the data destroyed is before the Delhi High Court.
India has a law specifically governing police use of facial recognition technology.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Student activist Aishe Ghosh moved the Delhi High Court, but India currently has no law governing police use of facial recognition. Demonstrators had photographed a police van, branded Ikshana, fitted with 360-degree cameras.
source: India currently has no law governing police use of facial recognition.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's first direct commercial container freight train to Nepal, which arrived in July 2026:
items: Its cargo had to be transshipped at the India–Nepal border before entering Nepal.
It ran from Kolkata Port to Biratnagar, Nepal's industrial hub near the border with Bihar.
It used the Jogbani–Biratnagar broad-gauge link inaugurated in 2023.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. The story says the 40-wagon train, carrying canola, travelled under the revised India–Nepal Rail Transit Protocol without requiring transshipment at the border. The service follows a revised bilateral agreement signed in November 2025, and New Delhi expects it to cut cargo handling, transit times and logistics costs.
source: The 40-wagon train, carrying canola, travelled under the revised India–Nepal Rail Transit Protocol without requiring transshipment at the border.

prompt: In July 2026, the Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. Consider the following statements about the bill:
items: Appeals against a Special Fast Track Court order lie only to the High Court, heard by a bench of three judges.
It sets a two-month limit for investigation and a three-month deadline for trial.
Despite its passage by the Lok Sabha, the bill still needs the Rajya Sabha and presidential assent to become law.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first statement is wrong because appeals against a Special Fast Track Court order go only to the High Court and are heard by a bench of two judges, not three. Such appeals must be disposed of within three months, and no other appeal or revision is available.
source: Appeals against a Special Fast Track Court order will go only to the High Court, heard by a bench of two judges and disposed of within three months.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Left Wing Extremist insurgency in India:
items: It began in 1967 with a peasant uprising in Naxalbari, a village in West Bengal.
The Communist Party of India (Maoist) was formed in 2004 through a merger of the two largest armed groups.
Violence peaked in 2004, the year the Communist Party of India (Maoist) was formed.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because violence peaked in 2010, when more than a thousand civilians and security personnel were killed. After the first wave was crushed, the movement regrouped across a forested belt of eastern and central India, drawing cadre largely from tribal communities.
source: The violence peaked in 2010, when more than a thousand civilians and security personnel were killed.

prompt: In July 2026, Misir Besra, the last absconding politburo member of the CPI (Maoist), was arrested by state police and the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA). CoBRA is a unit of which force?
explain: CoBRA belongs to the Central Reserve Police Force. Besra was flushed out of the Saranda forest in West Singhbhum, Jharkhand, and carried a bounty of more than INR 10 million.
source: State police and the Central Reserve Police Force's Commando Battalion for Resolute Action flushed him out of the Saranda forest in West Singhbhum in Jharkhand.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the status of Naxal-affected areas reported by the Home Ministry to the Rajya Sabha in July 2026:
items: No district is now classed as Naxal-affected, down from eight in December 2025.
Thirty-seven cleared districts are on a watch list the Centre calls Legacy and Thrust.
West Singhbhum is the only district still listed as a District of Concern.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the Home Ministry's reply. In the Legacy and Thrust districts security and development spending continues, and two-thirds of the security camps in cleared areas are staying.
source: The Home Ministry told the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday that no district is now classed as Naxal-affected, down from eight in December 2025.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the amendment to India's anti-paper-leak law passed by Parliament in July 2026:
items: It was passed by the Lok Sabha a day before the Rajya Sabha passed it.
It creates a new judicial system of specially constituted courts with newly appointed judges.
It requires every state and union territory to designate an existing Sessions Court and appoint special prosecutors.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the bill does not create a new judicial system; it relies on existing Sessions Courts designated by each state and union territory. The Lok Sabha passed it on 29 July 2026 and the Rajya Sabha on 30 July 2026, and the government says six special fast-track courts are already operating.
source: It requires every state and union territory to designate an existing Sessions Court and appoint special prosecutors.

prompt: After both Houses of Parliament passed the tougher anti-paper-leak amendment bill in July 2026, which step remained before it could become law?
explain: With the Rajya Sabha passing the bill on 30 July 2026, a day after the Lok Sabha, it needed only presidential assent to become law. TBB notes the bill shifts the caseload to states and high courts, since designating existing courts as fast track adds no judges.
source: It now requires presidential assent.

prompt: Consider the following statements about solar power curtailment in India, as reported in July 2026:
items: Transmission bottlenecks led to over 8,000 GWh, or about 11%, of solar output being wasted between April and June 2026.
About 21 GW of India's solar capacity relies on temporary grid hookups while dedicated transmission lines are built.
India's USD 83 billion transmission roadmap is meant to close the gap between generation and grid capacity by 2030.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the USD 83 billion transmission roadmap runs through 2036, while 2030 is the deadline for reaching 500 GW of non-fossil capacity. Solar parks are being commissioned far faster than high-voltage lines can be built to evacuate the power.
source: New Delhi is deploying an USD 83 billion transmission roadmap through 2036 to address the gap between generation and grid capacity.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP):
items: In July 2026, New India Assurance issued the first sovereign-backed Protection and Indemnity (P&I) policy under BMIP to Shipping Corporation of India.
Protection and Indemnity (P&I) insurance primarily protects the physical hull of the insured vessel.
The Union Cabinet approved BMIP in April 2026 after the West Asian war drove insurers from Gulf routes.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Hull insurance protects the ship, while P&I covers third-party liabilities such as crew injuries, cargo damage, pollution and wreck removal. The pool aims to bring maritime risk onto India's own balance sheet, with the sovereign guarantee carrying the catastrophic layer.
source: New India Assurance issued the first sovereign-backed Protection and Indemnity (P&I) policy under the Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) to Shipping Corporation of India on Thursday.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India's maritime insurance, as of July 2026:
items: Cover provided by the first BMIP P&I policy — up to USD 1.5 billion
Cargo and hull war-risk policies issued under BMIP since May 2026 — 1,608
War-risk premiums on some Red Sea routes after renewed Houthi attacks — 35–40% of vessel value
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong. Red Sea war-risk premiums have climbed to 1–2% of vessel value; 35–40% is the fall in BMIP premiums from the conflict peak that the government claims, without disclosing its benchmark.
source: War-risk premiums on some Red Sea routes have climbed to 1–2% of vessel value following renewed Houthi attacks.

prompt: In August 2026, India's power regulator proposed reinstating a waiver for renewable energy and battery storage projects stalled by grid delays. The waiver concerned which of the following?
options: Basic customs duty on battery cells
Goods and services tax on solar modules
explain: The draft policy would bring back interstate transmission fee waivers, reversing a planned phase-out. It is meant to help developers who missed deadlines because of grid delays, provided they hold long-term power sale contracts through 2026.
source: India’s power regulator has proposed reinstating interstate transmission fee waivers for renewable energy and battery storage projects stalled by grid delays

prompt: In August 2026, a draft notification proposed mandatory Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication systems in new vehicles in India. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It was issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways as an amendment to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.
It proposes that fitment of V2V systems becomes compulsory from October 1, 2027.
The technology it specifies, Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X), runs on the 5.9 GHz band that the Department of Telecommunications had exempted from licensing.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because compulsory fitment starts from October 1, 2028. October 1, 2027 is only the date from which vehicles that carry a V2V system must conform to AIS-230. The system broadcasts position, speed, direction and braking status over radio, so it reaches vehicles that cameras and radar cannot see.
source: From October 1, 2028, fitment becomes compulsory.

prompt: In August 2026, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways proposed a first regulatory framework for two-wheeled road ambulances. Which Automotive Industry Standard does the framework adopt?
explain: The framework adopts AIS-209 for L2-category machines fitted with a stretcher or patient-conveyance unit, from October 1, 2027. AIS-230 is the standard for the separate V2V communication mandate. The ambulances are aimed at rural, remote and hilly areas, and each state decides where they may operate.
source: The same day, the ministry proposed a first regulatory framework for two-wheeled road ambulances, adopting standard AIS-209 for L2-category machines fitted with a stretcher or patient-conveyance unit, also from October 1, 2027.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, introduced in Parliament in August 2026:
items: It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
The government may extend its framework to other financial entities by notification.
Certificates issued by banks under it may use manual, digital or electronic signatures.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced the Bill in the Lok Sabha on 3 August 2026. The Bill would let digital, cloud, backup and disaster-recovery records serve as evidence through certified copies, as paper records already can.
source: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman introduced the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha on Monday.

prompt: The Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2026, would replace an Act governing the use of bank records in legal proceedings. In which year was that Act passed?
explain: The Bill would replace the 135-year-old Act of 1891 on how bank records are used in legal proceedings. It remains a pending bill and would take effect only after passage and notification.
source: It would replace the 1891 Act governing how bank records are used in legal proceedings.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Uzbekistan economic relations, as discussed at the India-Uzbekistan Business Forum in New Delhi in August 2026:
items: The India–Uzbekistan Bilateral Investment Treaty entered into force in May 2024.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal called for doubling bilateral trade within five years.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements are wrong: the Bilateral Investment Treaty entered into force in May 2025, not May 2024, and Goyal called for doubling bilateral trade within three years, not five. He put current trade at about USD 1.5 billion and named mining, textiles, pharmaceuticals, food processing and digital public infrastructure for co-investment.
source: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal called for doubling bilateral trade with Uzbekistan within three years

prompt: In August 2026, the Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had been invited to the outreach session of the September 2026 BRICS Summit in his capacity as chair of which grouping?
explain: Rahman was invited as chair of BIMSTEC, the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation. India had already extended a separate invitation in February, addressed to him as prime minister, even as it distanced itself from Sheikh Hasina's address from New Delhi.
source: Jaiswal also confirmed Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has been invited to the outreach session of September's BRICS Summit as chair of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation).

prompt: Consider the following statements about former Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, as of August 2026:
items: She was sentenced to death in November 2025 over her crackdown on the uprising.
India has kept Bangladesh's request for her extradition under examination since Bangladesh's first note verbale in December 2024.
A December 2024 order of Bangladesh's International Crimes Tribunal bars media outlets from broadcasting her statements.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. India has kept the extradition request under examination since December 2024, citing due judicial and legal process without committing to an outcome. Hasina has said she plans to return around December to face trial.
source: India has kept the request "under examination" since Bangladesh's first note verbale in December 2024, citing due judicial and legal process without committing to an outcome

prompt: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced in Parliament in August 2026, extends the tax holiday for foreign suppliers of machinery and tooling to Indian factories through which year?
explain: The Bill extends the tax holiday for foreign suppliers of machinery and tooling through 2040-41. It was initially valid only until 2031, and the extension is a long-term win for electronics makers like Apple.
source: Foreign suppliers delivering machinery and tooling to Indian factories get their tax holiday extended through 2040-41, a long-term win for tech giants like Apple.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, introduced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in August 2026:
items: Skilled fund managers can relocate to India without their entire offshore fund becoming subject to Indian corporate taxation.
Data centre facilities used by global cloud providers gain flexibility to operate on a leased basis.
Tax-free dividend perks for investors in real estate investment trusts and infrastructure investment trusts are withdrawn.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the Bill restores tax-free dividend perks for REIT and InvIT investors, protecting yields as operating firms move to the new tax regime. The Bill aims to attract foreign capital by removing niche friction points in industries such as cloud services and fund management.
source: Tax-free dividend perks for real estate investment trust and infrastructure investment trust investors are restored, protecting yields even as operating firms transition to the new tax regime.

prompt: In August 2026, the Supreme Court issued nationwide directions to combat digital arrest scams. Consider the following statements about these directions:
items: The Reserve Bank of India was directed to frame a Standard Operating Procedure on mule accounts within four weeks.
States and Union Territories must operationalise grievance redressal and money restoration modules under the Ministry of Finance's cyber fraud portal.
The Centre's Inter-Departmental Committee was asked to examine a shared liability and victim compensation framework.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the grievance redressal and money restoration modules sit under the Ministry of Home Affairs' cyber fraud portal, not a Ministry of Finance portal. States and Union Territories must also set up State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres within the same four-week window.
source: States and Union Territories must operationalise grievance redressal and money restoration modules under the Ministry of Home Affairs' cyber fraud portal, and set up their State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres within the same window.

prompt: In August 2026, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) unveiled India's first indigenous vaccine against African Swine Fever. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It was developed by ICAR's National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal.
It is produced using the MA-104 cell line.
It is recommended for pigs above eight weeks, with a booster dose after 28 days.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because the vaccine is given to pigs above eight weeks as a single dose with a booster after 14 days, not 28. African Swine Fever has spread across India since 2020.
source: Built by ICAR's National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (ICAR-NIHSAD) in Bhopal, the vaccine uses the widely available MA-104 cell line and is recommended for pigs above eight weeks as a single dose with a booster after 14 days.

prompt: In August 2026, the government operationalised a framework on inventory holding by foreign-invested e-commerce companies in India. Consider the following statements about it:
items: Foreign-invested e-commerce companies may hold inventory in India only if every unit is bound for export.
The framework also relaxes the domestic ban on foreign-owned inventory-led e-commerce.
Exporters-on-Record must pay Indian sellers on a fixed timeline regardless of whether the overseas buyer has paid.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
