explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the framework applies to exports alone and the domestic ban on foreign-owned inventory-led e-commerce is unchanged. It follows an earlier amendment to India's FDI policy, with Amazon and Flipkart seen as the main beneficiaries.
source: This follows an earlier amendment to India's foreign direct investment (FDI) policy and applies to exports alone; the domestic ban on foreign-owned inventory-led e-commerce is unchanged.

prompt: Under the e-commerce export inventory framework operationalised in August 2026, which entity buys goods from Indian sellers after an overseas order is confirmed and exports them under its own name?
explain: The registered Exporter-on-Record buys from Indian Sellers-on-Record only after an overseas order is confirmed and exports the goods in its own name. It handles customs paperwork and destination-country compliance, and can also offer testing, certification, packaging, labelling and returns.
source: Companies must route exports through a registered Exporter-on-Record (EOR), which buys from Indian Sellers-on-Record (SORs) only after an overseas order is confirmed, then exports the goods under its own name.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the export-only e-commerce inventory framework operationalised in India in August 2026:
items: Export rebates must be passed through to Indian sellers in proportion to each seller's free-on-board (FOB) value.
Export inventory must be kept in a separate, digitally tracked repository and cannot be diverted into the Indian market.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both safeguards are part of the framework, which also gives sellers visibility into final sale prices, order status and shipment tracking. Returned goods must be re-exported, sent back to the seller or disposed of under the rules, and Exporters-on-Record face annual compliance certification.
source: Export inventory must be kept in a separate, digitally tracked repository and cannot be diverted into the Indian market.

prompt: In August 2026, the Finance Minister tabled amendments in Parliament to create a legal framework for reintroducing a Merchant Discount Rate on UPI transactions. Which Act was being amended?
explain: Nirmala Sitharaman tabled amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act on 4 August 2026 to allow an MDR on UPI. Industry players such as PhonePe and Google Pay argue the zero-fee model cannot cover their infrastructure costs.
source: tabled amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act in parliament on Tuesday

prompt: Consider the following statements about digital payment fees in India, as of August 2026:
items: The Merchant Discount Rate is a processing fee that merchants pay to banks and payment service providers.
UPI has been free of merchant fees since 2019.
Regulations cap the Merchant Discount Rate on debit cards at a maximum of 0.9%.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: MDR is a fee merchants pay to banks and payment service providers, UPI has been free of merchant fees since 2019, and debit card fees are capped by regulation at 0.9%. By contrast, credit card MDR can reach as high as 3%, and officials are weighing a 0.3% to 0.5% MDR on UPI transactions above INR 2,000.
source: In contrast, credit card MDR can reach as high as 3%, whereas debit card fees are capped by regulations at a maximum of 0.9%.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's E20 ethanol-blended petrol programme, as reported in August 2026:
items: E20 replaced the older E10 blend nationwide in 2025, five years ahead of a 2030 target.
E20-ready cars first reached showrooms in 2023.
The Centre's precautionary ceiling for chloride in blending ethanol is 350 parts per million.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The Centre's precautionary chloride ceiling for blending ethanol is 3 ppm. The 350 ppm figure is what SIAM's letter reported at the pump. Because E20-ready cars arrived only in 2023, most vehicles on the road were built for weaker blends.
source: E20 replaced the older E10 blend nationwide in 2025, five years ahead of a 2030 target

prompt: In August 2026, the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) withdrew a letter on E20 fuel quality. Consider the following statements:
items: The letter had been sent to the petroleum ministry and linked part failures to high chloride levels in E20.
In withdrawing the letter, SIAM retracted its claim that contaminated fuel was corroding vehicle parts.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: SIAM did not take back the contamination claim. It pulled the letter so that the reported figures could be authenticated through wider data collection. The July 28 letter had blamed chloride corrosion for failures in fuel injectors, fuel pumps and EGR valves.
source: SIAM did not take back the contamination claim.

prompt: In August 2026, a parliamentary panel threatened to withdraw Meta's legal immunity in India over Facebook's removal of a video posted by Prime Minister Modi. Consider the following statements:
items: The demand came from the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology, which sought an unconditional apology from Meta's chief executive.
The committee was chaired by Nishikant Dubey.
Meta publicly confirmed an apology that specifically named the removed video.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong: the apology, as reported, names no video, and Meta has issued no public confirmation. The committee met on August 3 and gave Zuckerberg three days to apologise, failing which safe harbour immunity may be withdrawn.
source: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Communications and Information Technology met on August 3 and sought an unconditional apology from Zuckerberg within three days over Facebook's brief removal of a video posted by Prime Minister Modi.

prompt: In August 2026, a parliamentary committee warned that Meta could lose its 'safe harbour' protection in India. What does safe harbour protection provide to online platforms?
options: Exemption from liability for content posted by their users
Exemption from income tax on digital advertising revenue
Exemption from rules requiring local storage of data
Exemption from competition law scrutiny of their mergers
explain: Safe harbour shields platforms from liability for content their users post. The committee argued that removing the Prime Minister's post was a publisher's act, and officials told a Meta delegation the company no longer qualifies as an intermediary because it selects who receives content.
source: Safe harbour shields platforms from liability for content posted by users.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the overseas oil assets of Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), as reported in August 2026:
items: ONGC regained its 20 per cent stake in Russia's Sakhalin-1 project in December 2025 after four years.
ONGC's overseas arm holds 40 per cent of the San Cristobal field in Venezuela.
ONGC retained its Sakhalin-1 stake by paying into the project's abandonment fund in US dollars.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because ONGC paid into the Sakhalin-1 abandonment fund in rubles, using dividends frozen in Russia. Regaining the stake lifted ONGC's quarterly revenue from the asset to roughly INR 10 billion (USD 105 million), from INR 5 billion to 6 billion earlier.
source: ONGC retained the stake by paying into the project's abandonment fund in rubles using dividends frozen in Russia.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Air India, as reported in August 2026:
items: Tata Sons own about 75 per cent of Air India, with Singapore Airlines holding the rest.
Air India has turned a profit in every year since Tata regained control in 2022.
Since April 2025, Pakistan has barred Indian carriers from its airspace.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Air India has not turned a profit since Tata regained control in 2022. Air India Group posted a record loss of more than USD 2 billion in fiscal 2025-26. Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran has said the turnaround could take up to a decade.
source: Tata Sons own about 75 per cent of Air India, with Singapore Airlines holding the rest, and Chairman N. Chandrasekaran has said the turnaround could take up to a decade.

prompt: Consider the following statements about GOBARdhan, the national compressed biogas scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2026:
items: It runs from 2026-27 to 2035-36 under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
It fixes an administered compressed biogas price of INR 2,110 per million BTUs for at least ten years.
It aims to raise domestic compressed biogas output nearly tenfold over the coming decade.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the scheme runs under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, not the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Its INR 237 billion outlay rests on offtake certainty, with a fixed price and a notified blending obligation guaranteeing producers a buyer.
source: runs from the 2026-27 financial year to 2035-36 under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

prompt: Which scheme, launched in 2018, targeted 5,000 compressed biogas plants producing 15 million tonnes a year by 2023-24?
explain: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) was the largest earlier compressed biogas programme but delivered only a fraction of its target. About 200 CBG plants operated when GOBARdhan was approved in August 2026.
source: The largest, the 2018 SATAT scheme (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation), had targeted 5,000 plants producing 15 million tonnes a year by 2023-24, and delivered only a fraction of that.

prompt: Under the GOBARdhan scheme approved in August 2026, City Gas Distribution companies must take a rising share of compressed biogas. Consider the following pairs of financial year and blending obligation:
items: 2026-27 — 3 per cent
2027-28 — 4 per cent
2028-29 onwards — 5 per cent
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The obligation starts at 3 per cent in 2026-27, rises to 4 per cent the next year and reaches 5 per cent from 2028-29. Because compressed biogas costs more than the gas it displaces, the mandate effectively relies on continued government support to bridge the price gap.
source: 3 per cent in 2026-27, 4 per cent the next year, and 5 per cent from 2028-29.

prompt: In August 2026, critics of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill pointed to a 2024 review by which international body that had urged a narrower, risk-based approach to regulating NGOs' foreign funding?
options: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
explain: Critics cited the Financial Action Task Force's 2024 review, which urged a narrower, risk-based approach, alongside earlier warnings on the FCRA from United Nations Special Rapporteurs. The bill, which tightens rules on NGOs' foreign funding, was again not tabled on 6 August 2026 amid Opposition protests.
source: Critics also point to the Financial Action Task Force's (FATF) 2024 review, which urged a narrower, risk-based approach, and earlier United Nations (UN) Special Rapporteur warnings on the FCRA.

prompt: In August 2026, the US Senate passed a bill authorising tariffs on buyers of Russian oil. Consider the following statements about the bill:
items: As first proposed, the bill sought a blanket 500 per cent tariff on any country doing business with Russia's energy sector.
The version passed by the Senate narrows its scope to the five largest importers of Russian oil and gas.
The applied tariff on the named countries is to be reassessed every 180 days.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct. The bill began as a blanket 500 per cent tariff, but the Senate version narrows it to the five largest oil and gas importers, with the US Trade Representative setting a rate from zero to 100 per cent that is reassessed every 180 days. The bill passed the Senate 86-11 and still needs to pass the House in identical form before it goes to Trump for assent.
source: What passed the Senate narrows that to the five largest oil and gas importers, with a separate carve-out shielding countries that account for less than 15 per cent of Russia's total gas exports and are actively cutting that share.

prompt: The Russian oil tariff bill passed by the US Senate in August 2026 named five countries as targets, India among them. Which of the following countries was NOT one of the five?
explain: The five named targets are India, China, Slovakia, Hungary and Azerbaijan. The bill's sponsors framed a high tariff as necessary specifically to discourage Chinese and Indian purchases.
source: India is one of five named targets, alongside China, Slovakia, Hungary, and Azerbaijan

prompt: In August 2026, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a trilateral collective defence agreement. In which city was it signed?
explain: The agreement was signed in Mecca on Friday 7 August 2026. New Delhi said it is following the agreement closely, having earlier warned that Saudi-Pakistani defence cooperation could affect Indian security.
source: Signed in Mecca on Friday, the agreement says an armed attack on one will be treated as an attack on all three.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the defence agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan in August 2026:
items: It provides that an armed attack on any one of the three will be treated as an attack on all three.
The precise military obligations of each signatory have been made public.
It builds on a bilateral defence pact that Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed in September 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the story says the precise military obligations remain undisclosed. Turkey's entry adds NATO's second-largest military and a defence industry already supplying Saudi drones.
source: The precise military obligations remain undisclosed.

prompt: In August 2026, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) issued directions to Meta on content moderation. Consider the following statements:
items: Meta was directed to submit a roadmap to curb deepfakes, propaganda and synthetic content across its platforms.
Meta was asked to strictly adhere to data-localisation rules and speed up the execution of government takedown requests.
In talks with ministry officials, Meta acknowledged technical gaps in handling child sex abuse material and deepfakes.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. MeitY also wants Meta to re-engineer its algorithms to throttle the reach of manipulated media, though TBB notes such automated filters can also catch legitimate speech, news and satire.
source: Meta must strengthen moderation, accelerate the execution of government takedown requests, strictly adhere to data-localization rules, and re-engineer algorithms to actively throttle the reach of manipulated media.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed by Parliament in August 2026:
items: It mandates that mediation in delayed-payment disputes must be completed within 90 days.
If a buyer's challenge to an arbitral award is pending for more than six months, courts must release at least 50 per cent of the awarded amount to the MSE supplier.
Even before the amendment, a buyer challenging an arbitral award had to deposit 75 per cent of it with the court, but its release to the supplier was left to judicial discretion.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the bill mandates that mediation be completed within 90 days and adds a floor of 50 per cent release once a challenge has been pending for over six months. The 75 per cent deposit requirement already existed, but release of that money was previously at judicial discretion.
source: Buyers challenging an arbitral award already had to deposit 75 per cent of it with the court, but release of that money to the supplier was left to judicial discretion.

prompt: Under the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed in August 2026, all Central Public Sector Enterprises must route their payments to MSMEs through which platform?
explain: The bill requires all CPSEs to pay MSMEs through TReDS, an invoice-discounting platform. It also nudges state governments to put their own enterprises on it.
source: It also requires all Central Public Sector Enterprises to route their MSME payments through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), an invoice-discounting platform, and nudges state governments to put their own enterprises on it too.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha in August 2026:
items: It allows a mediated settlement or arbitral award to be recovered as an arrear of land revenue through the district administration.
It makes registration on the Udyam Registration Portal mandatory and fee-based for all MSMEs.
It retains criminal conviction as a penalty for failing to register or supply information.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only statement 1 is correct. The Udyam portal gets statutory permanence as a free, voluntary platform, and failures to register or supply information are decriminalised into graded penalties, starting with a warning for a first instance of wrong information.
source: The amendment also gives statutory permanence to the Udyam Registration Portal as a free, voluntary digital platform, and formally incorporates the twin criteria of "investment in plant/machinery" and "turnover" for MSME classification into the Act.

prompt: In August 2026, the Reserve Bank of India issued new directions on loan recovery practices. Consider the following statements about these directions:
items: Lenders may remotely disable a defaulting borrower's device only if the loan was taken out to purchase that device.
Where a device lock is permitted, lenders may impose it in full at once.
Lenders must fully restore device functionality within one hour of the borrower clearing pending dues.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because lenders cannot impose hardware locks all at once (ab initio). They must take a gradual approach and cannot cut off incoming calls, SMS or emergency SOS features. The directions also widen harassment to cover social media shaming and intimidation of a borrower's friends, relatives and co-workers.
source: The only exception is if the loan was specifically taken out to purchase that exact device.

prompt: The RBI's loan recovery directions issued in August 2026, which ban social media shaming of borrowers by recovery agents, take effect from which date?
explain: The directions take effect on 1 January 2027. They apply to banks, NBFCs and recovery agents, and add to existing bans on odd-hour calls and physical threats.
source: The rules take effect on January 1, 2027.

prompt: Consider the following statements about household debt in India, as reported in August 2026:
items: Indian household debt reached a record 45.5 per cent of GDP as of September 2025.
The RBI's Financial Stability Report attributes the rise largely to a surge in secured home loans.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Financial Stability Report links the rise largely to a surge in unsecured consumer lending, not home loans. Smartphone financing alone is projected to reach 42 per cent of all sales in 2026, up from 35 per cent in 2025.
source: RBI's Financial Stability Report shows that the rise is driven largely by a surge in unsecured consumer lending.

prompt: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha in August 2026, establishes which new body to standardise member selection, salaries and oversight of tribunals?
explain: The bill sets up a new National Tribunals Commission, headed by a retired Supreme Court judge or High Court Chief Justice, to bring uniformity to member selection, salaries and oversight. TBB notes that a central selection commission aligns with Supreme Court mandates to shield tribunal appointments from executive influence.
source: It establishes a new National Tribunals Commission, headed by a retired Supreme Court judge or High Court Chief Justice, to standardize member selection, salaries, and oversight.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha in August 2026:
items: It repeals the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, after the Supreme Court struck down key provisions of that Act for violating judicial independence.
The Lok Sabha passed it through a recorded division after a detailed debate.
The new commission it creates is to be headed by a sitting Chief Justice of India.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Only the first statement is correct. The Lok Sabha passed the bill by voice vote without debate on 10 August 2026 amid Opposition protests, and the commission is to be headed by a retired Supreme Court judge or High Court Chief Justice, not a sitting Chief Justice of India. Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal cleared the bill through the noise, and TBB warns that passing it without discussion risks fresh legal challenges.
source: The Lok Sabha passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, by voice vote without debate on Monday as Opposition members drowned out the floor demanding answers on student protests.

prompt: In August 2026, the Jharkhand government responded to protests over alleged irregularities in state recruitment examinations. Consider the following statements about the measures it agreed to:
items: It agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination.
It agreed to seek an Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigation into alleged financial irregularities.
It agreed to set up a fast-track court to file charge sheets within 90 days.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the minister said the state agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary examination, seek an ED investigation into alleged financial irregularities and set up a fast-track court to file charge sheets within 90 days. The protesters' central demand, a CBI probe rather than the state-run CID one, remains unmet.
source: Jharkhand's higher education minister, Sudivya Kumar Sonu, said on Sunday the state has agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC preliminary examination and the 2023-25 backlog exams, open a Criminal Investigation Department (CID) probe, seek an Enforcement Directorate (ED) investigation into alleged financial irregularities, and set up a fast-track court to file charge sheets within 90 days.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Periodic Labour Force Survey bulletin for the April to June 2026 quarter, released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation in August 2026:
items: The overall Labour Force Participation Rate for persons aged 15 and above declined from the previous quarter.
The share of regular wage or salaried employees rose in both rural and urban areas.
The share of rural workers employed in agriculture rose from the previous quarter.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because rural employment in agriculture fell to 52.9% from 55.8%. The overall LFPR slipped to 54.6% from 55.5%, and regular wage or salaried employment rose to 16.1% in rural areas and 49.3% in urban areas, while urban unemployment held broadly stable at 6.7%.
source: The share of regular wage or salaried employees rose in both rural areas, to 16.1 percent, and urban areas, to 49.3 percent, while rural employment in agriculture fell to 52.9 percent from 55.8 percent.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Bangladesh relations as of August 2026:
items: On 10 August 2026, Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met Dinesh Trivedi, India's newly appointed High Commissioner to Dhaka.
Former Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina has lived in India since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Hasina fled to India in August 2024, not 2025. At the meeting Rahman renewed Dhaka's call for her extradition and, for the first time, explicitly tied warmer ties to conditions being met.
source: Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman told India's newly appointed High Commissioner to Dhaka, Dinesh Trivedi, on Monday that a "conducive environment" is needed to boost bilateral ties.

prompt: In August 2026, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) directed telecom providers to roll out 1601-series numbers for more sectors. Consider the following statements about this direction:
items: It covers service and transactional calls made by utilities, courier and logistics companies, with onboarding to be completed within 90 days.
The numbers will be allocated to aggregators, who may route calls on behalf of several businesses.
The 1601-series framework was already in use by banking, financial services and insurance firms.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The numbers go directly to verified entities, not to intermediaries or aggregators, and cannot be used for promotional calls. The aim is to help consumers tell legitimate business calls apart from fraudsters who impersonate firms using ordinary 10-digit numbers.
source: Numbers will be allocated directly to verified entities rather than intermediaries or aggregators, and cannot be used for promotional calls.

prompt: In August 2026, Fitch Ratings affirmed India's long-term sovereign credit rating at "BBB-" with a stable outlook. Consider the following statements about its assessment:
items: Fitch's FY27 growth projection is higher than India's average growth over the prior three years.
Fitch projected India's GDP growth for FY27 at 6.4%, roughly triple the median for "BBB"-rated peers.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the 6.4% projection is a slight moderation from the prior three-year average of 7.4%. Statement 2 is correct. Fitch said policy credibility, resilient corporate and bank balance sheets and structural tax reforms insulate the economy from external risks such as energy shocks.
source: The rating agency projected India's GDP growth at 6.4% for FY27, noting that while this marks a slight moderation from the prior three-year average of 7.4%, it remains roughly triple the median for "BBB"-rated peers.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill as of August 2026:
items: In August 2026, the Lok Sabha referred the bill to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee.
The committee is due to submit its report in the first week of the Budget Session.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The Lok Sabha referred the bill to a 31-member JPC on 12 August 2026, but the committee is due to report in the first week of the Winter Session, not the Budget Session. The bill, introduced in March, had drawn objections from Opposition parties and Christian civil society groups.
source: On Wednesday, the Lok Sabha referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) amid Opposition protests.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the asset provisions under Section 14B and Chapter IIIA of the FCRA Amendment Bill referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee in August 2026:
items: A routine delay on the FCRA Online Portal can trigger automatic cessation of an NGO's certificate.
On cessation, a Designated Authority takes provisional control of the NGO's foreign contributions and assets, including assets funded only partly by them.
Places of worship covered by these provisions must retain their religious character.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. Without restored registration, the Designated Authority's control becomes permanent and it may transfer or sell the assets. Current rules already allow seizure on licence cancellation, and the bill extends this to expired registrations.
source: That instantly hands a Designated Authority provisional control of an NGO's foreign contributions and assets, including those funded only partly by them.

prompt: In August 2026, Russia received its first-ever fuel import from India. Which refinery shipped the cargo?
explain: The 42,000-tonne shipment came from the Vadinar refinery of Rosneft-backed Nayara Energy, according to data provider Kpler. Nayara has been under European Union sanctions since July 2025.
source: A 42,000-tonne petroleum shipment from Nayara's Vadinar refinery reached Russia in early August, according to data provider Kpler.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the 2024 Supreme Court judgment on mineral royalty:
items: The Centre's review petition against the judgment succeeded.
The Court ruled by an 8–1 majority that royalty is not a tax.
The judgment left Parliament a route to restrict state taxation of mineral rights through the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first statement is wrong: the Centre lost its review attempt and filed a curative petition before turning to legislation. Because courts had long treated royalty as a tax, reclassifying it removed the cap on what states could separately charge.
source: The Centre lost a review attempt and filed a curative petition before turning to legislation.

prompt: In August 2026, the Union Coal and Mines Minister introduced a bill on state taxation of minerals. Consider the following statements about the bill:
items: It would prohibit states from taxing mineral rights.
It would void state taxes and cesses on minerals that remain unpaid or unrecovered once it takes effect.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The bill bars states from taxing mineral rights and voids dues still unpaid when it takes effect. Money already collected stays with the states.
source: The bill would void state taxes and cesses left unpaid or unrecovered once it takes effect.

prompt: Following the 2024 Supreme Court ruling on mineral royalty, which state raised its coal cess from INR 100 to INR 250 per tonne in 2025?
explain: Jharkhand raised its coal cess to INR 250 per tonne and its iron ore cess from INR 100 to INR 400 in 2025. Karnataka had instead projected INR 30 billion from a proposed levy in 2026-27 that was awaiting central approval.
source: Jharkhand raised its coal cess from INR 100 (USD 1.05) to INR 250 (USD 2.62) per tonne

prompt: In August 2026, NASA invited ISRO to join its Moon Base programme. Consider the following statements:
items: The invitation was extended at the ninth meeting of the India-US Civil Space Joint Working Group, held at NASA headquarters in Washington, DC.
The Moon Base programme aims to establish a sustained human presence near the south pole of the moon.
NISAR, a joint NASA-ISRO Earth observation satellite, was launched in July 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the ninth meeting of the India-US Civil Space Joint Working Group was held at ISRO headquarters in Bengaluru on 5 and 6 August 2026, not at NASA headquarters in Washington. The two sides also agreed to advance talks on sharing open scientific data under the Artemis Accords.
source: The invite was extended at the ninth meeting of the India-US Civil Space Joint Working Group at ISRO headquarters in Bengaluru on August 5 and 6.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Terms of Reference signed by India and the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) in August 2026:
items: They set out negotiations towards a Free Trade Agreement between India and SACU.
They are India's first such framework with an African region.
The negotiations will cover eight chapters, including rules of origin and a bilateral safeguard mechanism.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the talks are towards a Preferential Trade Agreement, not a Free Trade Agreement. SACU comprises South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Eswatini and Lesotho, and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal cited scope for India to supply affordable medicines and IT talent to the bloc.
source: The Terms of Reference (ToR) mark India's first such framework with an African region.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) tender issued by the Ministry of Defence in August 2026:
items: It seeks 60 transport aircraft with an 18-30 tonne cargo capacity.
The tender is valued at INR 1 trillion.
It invites Indian companies to partner with global manufacturers to build the aircraft.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the tender issued on 12 August 2026. Selection could take more than two years given the scale of the technical and commercial evaluation.
source: Issued on August 12, the Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme invites Indian companies to partner with global manufacturers to build 60 transport aircraft with an 18-30 tonne cargo capacity.

prompt: The Medium Transport Aircraft programme, for which a tender was floated in August 2026, is intended to replace which Indian Air Force fleet?
explain: The new aircraft will replace the Antonov An-32 fleet, which has been in service for three decades. An An-32 was involved in a fatal crash in June 2026 that killed five personnel.
source: The aircraft will replace the Indian Air Force's Antonov An-32 fleet, in service for three decades and involved in a fatal crash in June that killed five personnel.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to partnerships announced for India's Medium Transport Aircraft tender in August 2026:
items: Tata Advanced Systems Limited — Embraer
Mahindra Defense — Lockheed Martin
KC-390 Millennium — Lockheed Martin
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: None of the pairs is correct: TASL has tied up with Lockheed Martin, Mahindra Defense has teamed up with Embraer, and the KC-390 Millennium is Embraer's aircraft. Lockheed Martin is pitching the C-130J Super Hercules for the INR 1 trillion tender to build 60 transport aircraft.
source: TASL has tied up with Lockheed Martin to pitch its C-130J Super Hercules, and Mahindra Defense has teamed up with Embraer, which has pitched its KC-390 Millennium aircraft to India.

prompt: In August 2026, China extended anti-dumping duties on Indian single-mode optical fibre for another five years. Consider the following statements:
items: China first imposed these duties in 2020, and the August 2026 extension is their first renewal.
The extended duties apply at rates that vary by exporter, with Sterlite Technologies facing a lower rate than Aksh Optifibre and Finolex Cables.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because China first imposed the measures in 2014 and previously renewed them for five years in 2020. Statement 2 is correct, as Sterlite Technologies faces 7.4 percent while Aksh Optifibre and Finolex Cables each face 30.6 percent. China's Ministry of Commerce said a year-long expiry review found that removing the duties could allow dumping and harm to domestic producers to continue or recur.
source: The measures will remain in force from Friday at rates ranging between 7.4 percent and 30.6 percent depending on the exporter, with Sterlite Technologies subject to 7.4 percent and Aksh Optifibre and Finolex Cables each facing 30.6 per cent.

prompt: In his Independence Day address of August 2026, Prime Minister Modi promised free online coaching for competitive examinations. The existing SATHEE platform, which already offers such coaching, is run with which institution?
explain: The Self Assessment Test and Help for Entrance Exams (SATHEE) platform is run with IIT Kanpur. It provides free coaching for engineering, medical and civil service examinations. Modi attached no budget or launch date to the new coaching pledge.
source: The Self Assessment Test and Help for Entrance Exams (SATHEE) platform, run with the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, provides free coaching for engineering, medical, and civil service examinations, and the AI pledge scales up the IndiaAI Mission that has run since 2024.

prompt: Consider the following statements about goals mentioned in Prime Minister Modi's Independence Day address of August 2026:
items: Lakhpati Didis are rural women who earn at least INR 100,000 a year through village savings groups.
The government's standing target is 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047.
The IndiaAI Mission, which the new AI training pledge scales up, has run since 2024.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: Lakhpati Didis earn at least INR 100,000 a year through village savings groups, the nuclear target is 100 GW by 2047, and the pledge to train 10 million young people in AI scales up the IndiaAI Mission that has run since 2024. Modi also reaffirmed a target of 60 million Lakhpati Didis.
source: Modi reaffirmed his administration's standing goals: 60 million Lakhpati Didis, rural women who earn at least INR 100,000 (USD 1,050) a year through village savings groups; 100 GW of nuclear power by 2047; and more semiconductor plants.

prompt: Census 2027 will include caste enumeration for the first time since independence. Which body cleared this decision in 2025?
explain: The Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs cleared caste enumeration for Census 2027 in 2025. The move followed Opposition pressure after Bihar's state-level caste survey suggested backward communities make up two-thirds of its population.
source: The decision, cleared by the Cabinet Committee on Political Affairs last year

prompt: Consider the following statements about the rollout of Census 2027:
items: Enumeration began on 17 August 2026 in Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh.
The nationwide survey is scheduled for February 2027 and will use a new mobile application for digital data collection.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements match the story: the first phase began on 17 August 2026 in Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh, and the nationwide survey follows in February 2027. Data will be collected digitally through a new mobile application.
source: The nationwide survey follows in February 2027, utilizing a new mobile application for digital data collection.

prompt: As of August 2026, India's Tejas fighter relies on engines supplied by which company?
explain: Decades of Indian effort to build a high-thrust jet engine have fallen short, so even the Tejas depends on General Electric (GE) engines. This gap is why the AMCA engine contest between Reliance–Rolls-Royce and Safran–GTRE matters.
source: India builds airframes, missiles, and radar, but decades of effort to produce a high-thrust jet engine have fallen short, leaving even the current Tejas fighter reliant on engines from General Electric (GE).

prompt: In August 2026, India signed contracts worth INR 1,577 crore with Tata Advanced Systems and NIBE for the Army under Atmanirbhar Bharat rules. What were these contracts for?
explain: Loitering munitions are drones that hover over a battlefield before diving into a target. Separately, the Ministry of Defence floated a INR 1 trillion tender to replace its ageing Soviet-era airlifters.
source: On the same day, India inked INR 1,577 crore (USD 165 million) in contracts with Tata Advanced Systems and NIBE for loitering munitions, drones that hover over a battlefield before diving into a target, for the Army under its Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) rules.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), launched in August 2026:
items: It was launched by the Central Board of Direct Taxes and was first announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.
Online declarations under the scheme are open until 31 March 2027.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The CBDT launched FAST-DS on 16 August 2026, and online declarations are open until 31 December 2026, not March 2027. The scheme targets students, young professionals, technology employees and relocated non-resident Indians who may have failed to disclose overseas holdings.
source: launched the Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), first announced in the 2026-27 Budget, on Sunday, with online declarations open until 31 December.

prompt: In August 2026, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence dismantled a syndicate that passed off South-East Asian areca nuts as Bangladeshi-origin goods. The duty exemptions of which trade agreement were fraudulently claimed?
explain: The syndicate falsely declared the nuts as Bangladeshi to claim SAFTA duty exemptions. It evaded over INR 2,500 crore in customs duties, and the DRI's operation across Kolkata and Visakhapatnam led to nine arrests.
source: by mislabeling South-East Asian areca nuts as Bangladeshi-origin to fraudulently claim SAFTA duty exemptions

prompt: Consider the following statements about the August 2026 security operation against the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN):
items: Forces detained 253 people across 14 states in a coordinated sweep on 12 August 2026.
The Ministry of Home Affairs said the operation was timed to pre-empt attacks around Republic Day.
Grenades seized in the operation bore Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, which the Ministry of Home Affairs cited as evidence of cross-border links.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the MHA said the sweep was timed to pre-empt attacks around the 15 August Independence Day holiday. The seizures also included IEDs, pistols and live cartridges, and the SBN now faces more than 80 FIRs.
source: On August 12, forces detained 253 people across 14 states in a coordinated sweep against the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN).

prompt: In August 2026, under which law were arrests made in the crackdown on the Shahzad Bhatti Network, a Pakistan-based terror network?
explain: The arrests were made under the UAPA, under which charges against the accused are deemed prima facie true and bail is an exception. The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad says the network recruits young people through online radicalisation.
source: The arrests were made under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), where charges against the accused deem to be prima facie true, and bail is an exception.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the MQ 9B Sea Guardian lease contract signed by India's defence ministry in August 2026:
items: The two drones were leased for the Indian Air Force.
The drones will provide maritime surveillance for 18 months.
India has separately purchased 31 MQ 9B drones from the United States, with first deliveries expected in January 2027.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong. The drones were leased for the Navy, not the Air Force; they will provide surveillance for 30 months, not 18; and first deliveries of the 31 purchased drones are expected in January 2029, not January 2027. The lease expires around February 2029, making it a bridge to the permanent fleet.
source: The high altitude, long endurance aircraft will provide maritime surveillance for 30 months.

prompt: In August 2026, India's defence ministry signed a contract to lease two MQ 9B Sea Guardian drones for the Navy from which company?
explain: The INR 1,943 crore (USD 203 million) contract was signed with General Atomics. The high altitude, long endurance drones can stay airborne longer than ships or crewed aircraft, giving more continuous coverage of Chinese activity in the Indian Ocean.
source: On Monday, the defence ministry signed an INR 1,943 crore (USD 203 million) contract with General Atomics to lease two MQ 9B Sea Guardian drones for the Navy.

prompt: In August 2026, customers in Qatar became able to send money from Qatar Post outlets directly to UPI-enabled bank accounts in India. Apart from Qatar Post, India Post and NPCI International Payments, which international body helped develop this service?
explain: The Universal Postal Union was one of the four parties that developed the service, alongside Qatar Post, India Post and NPCI International Payments. Senders give the recipient's UPI ID, and recipients must activate foreign inward remittances in their UPI app. India Post is working on similar corridors with other postal operators.
source: The service was developed by Qatar Post, India Post, the Universal Postal Union and NPCI International Payments.

prompt: In August 2026, India's power regulator allowed clean energy developers that miss project deadlines to retain their transmission access by paying a fee. Consider the following statements about this decision:
items: Developers facing land or financing delays pay INR 1,000 per megawatt each day to retain access.
Developers can receive up to six additional months for financing delays.
Missing the extended deadlines could still cost developers their grid access and bank guarantees.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: land or financing delays cost INR 1,000 per megawatt each day, financing delays get up to six additional months, and missing the extended deadlines could still cost developers their grid access and bank guarantees. Delayed commercial operations carry a higher fee of INR 3,000 per megawatt each day, with up to 12 additional months for commissioning.
source: Developers can receive up to three additional months for land, six for financing and 12 for commissioning.

prompt: In August 2026, the deep-water port of Vizhinjam flagged off its first export containers. In which state is this port located?
explain: Vizhinjam is in Kerala, where Chief Minister V D Satheesan flagged off its first export containers. Exporters can now ship directly to overseas markets instead of routing cargo through hubs like Colombo, Singapore and Dubai.
source: Kerala’s Vizhinjam port has begun handling India's own imports and exports.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Vizhinjam port, as of August 2026:
items: It is owned by the Kerala government and operated by Adani Ports.
It has played a transshipment role since it opened in December 2024.
In July 2026, the shipping line MSC acquired a majority stake in the port's operating company.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because MSC, the world's largest shipping line, bought a 49 per cent stake, not a majority. The port was built under a public-private partnership at INR 88.67 billion (USD 927 million).
source: In July, the world's largest shipping line, MSC, bought a 49 per cent stake in the operating company (we covered it here).

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to Kerala's Mission Samudra, launched in August 2026:
items: Catalytic fund — INR 4 billion
Industrial clusters planned — eight
New cities planned — five
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: The third pair is wrong because the plan envisages three new cities, not five. Mission Samudra is a port-led industrial plan that casts Vizhinjam as a port city anchoring a maritime economic region along Kerala's 600-kilometre coastline.
source: It casts Vizhinjam as a port city anchoring a maritime economic region of eight industrial clusters, three new cities, and Kerala's 600-kilometre coastline

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Positive Indigenisation List notified by the Ministry of Defence in August 2026:
items: It was notified by the Department of Defence Production.
It was the fifth such Positive Indigenisation List.
Of the 405 items it covers, 16 are used by the Coast Guard and the rest by defence public sector companies.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because this was the sixth Positive Indigenisation List. It covers 389 items for defence public sector companies and 16 for the Coast Guard, with an estimated business potential of INR 30.7 billion, and once developed domestically these items will be bought from Indian suppliers.
source: It includes 389 items used by defence public sector companies and 16 used by the Coast Guard, spanning aircraft, armoured vehicles, warships, missiles, and defence electronics.

prompt: In August 2026, President Droupadi Murmu granted assent to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026. Consider the following statements about the Act:
items: It bars states from imposing taxes, cesses or other levies on mineral rights and mineral bearing land except under conditions set by the Centre.
States must refund levies on mineral rights that they had already received before the law took effect.
It overturns a 2019 Supreme Court ruling that let states tax mineral rights.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because payments already received by states will not be refunded, and statement 3 is wrong because the Act overturns a 2024 Supreme Court ruling, not a 2019 one. Only statement 1 is correct, as the Act bars state levies on mineral rights except under conditions set by the Centre.
source: The Act overturns a 2024 Supreme Court ruling that let states tax mineral rights

prompt: In August 2026, Bangladesh said it would seek a guarantee clause in the renegotiated Ganges Water Sharing Treaty with India. Consider the following statements:
items: The 1996 Ganges Water Sharing Treaty expires in December 2026.
The 1996 treaty carries a minimum-flow guarantee for Bangladesh.
The 1977 predecessor treaty assured Bangladesh a fixed share regardless of how much water India drew upstream.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the 1996 treaty dropped the minimum-flow guarantee that the 1977 treaty carried. Dhaka wants that guarantee restored and says it is ready to take the dispute to international forums.
source: The 1996 Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between India and Bangladesh, which expires in December, dropped the minimum-flow guarantee that its 1977 predecessor carried.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the 1992 United Nations Water Convention, as reported in August 2026:
items: Bangladesh joined it in June 2025, becoming the first South Asian country to do so.
India is a signatory to the convention.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: India is not a signatory, so the convention gives Dhaka an international platform but no legal claim over how India uses shared water. India insists shared-river disputes stay bilateral.
source: Dhaka also joined the 1992 United Nations Water Convention in June 2025, the first South Asian country to do so.

prompt: India's National River Linking Project, cited in August 2026 as a concern behind Bangladesh's demand for a water guarantee, plans to divert Himalayan waters, including the Ganges, towards which part of India?
explain: The project plans to move Himalayan waters towards southwestern India. The links affecting Ganges flows remain at the feasibility-study stage, held up by protected forests and the absence of water-sharing deals with Nepal and Bhutan.
source: Underlying the demand is India's National River Linking Project, which plans to divert Himalayan waters, including the Ganges, towards southwestern India.

prompt: In August 2026, India requested consultations at the WTO over a US safeguard measure on quartz surfaces. Consider the following statements:
items: India has been exempted from the safeguard duties.
The safeguard followed a finding by the US International Trade Commission that rising imports had seriously injured domestic manufacturers.
According to the Global Trade Research Initiative, the US bought 72.5 per cent of India's quartz-surface exports in the 2026 financial year.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the story states that India is not exempt. Statements 2 and 3 are correct. First-year imports face an additional 25 per cent tariff within the quota and 50 per cent above it, and India's quartz-surface exports to the US were worth USD 233.3 million in FY2026.
source: The US International Trade Commission found rising imports had seriously injured domestic manufacturers.

prompt: Before its August 2026 WTO request on quartz surfaces, India had sought consultations over US tariffs on steel, aluminium, automobiles and copper. On what ground did Washington reject those requests?
explain: Washington treated those tariffs as national-security measures, not safeguards. Because the quartz measure is explicitly a safeguard, India has cleaner procedural ground at the WTO this time.
source: Washington rejected them as national-security measures, not safeguards.

prompt: After Go First's 2023 bankruptcy earned India a risky-jurisdiction label among aircraft lessors, which law did New Delhi enact in 2025 to speed up repossession of leased aircraft?
explain: The story says New Delhi responded to the Go First episode with the 2025 Aircraft Objects Act to speed repossession. Go First's bankruptcy had trapped more than 50 leased aircraft under a court moratorium.
source: New Delhi responded with the 2025 Aircraft Objects Act to speed repossession.

prompt: Consider the following statements about insolvency proceedings involving Indian airlines, as reported in August 2026:
items: In August 2026, the National Company Law Tribunal ordered seven lessor petitions against SpiceJet to be reheard from scratch.
The lessor petitions against SpiceJet concern the repossession of leased aircraft rather than unpaid debts.
Go First's 2023 bankruptcy trapped more than 50 leased aircraft under a court moratorium.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: SpiceJet's cases concern unpaid debts, not repossession, though they expose a parallel enforcement problem. The NCLT's order left SpiceJet's management in control, whereas an admitted petition could have put the airline under an independent insolvency professional.
source: On Wednesday, the National Company Law Tribunal ordered seven lessor petitions reheard from scratch, leaving management in control.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Japan maritime defence framework signed in August 2026:
items: It was signed by the two defence ministers, Rajnath Singh and Shinjiro Koizumi.
It covers maritime-domain awareness, information sharing and closer naval operations.
It grants the two navies immediate reciprocal access to each other's ports and repair facilities.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the two sides will only work towards reciprocal access to ports and repair facilities. The navies will also expand exercises, ship visits, logistics and coordination protecting sea routes.
source: On Thursday, defence ministers Rajnath Singh and Shinjiro Koizumi signed a framework covering maritime-domain awareness, information sharing, and closer naval operations.

prompt: At their July 2026 summit, India and Japan signed their first defence co-development agreement. Which system did it cover?
explain: The July 2026 summit produced the first defence co-development agreement, for the Unified Complex Radio Antenna system, with a commitment to explore more projects. In August 2026 the defence ministers sought further cooperation in mine countermeasures, unmanned systems and naval shipbuilding.
source: The statement follows July’s summit, where the two countries signed their first defence co-development agreement for the Unified Complex Radio Antenna system

prompt: In August 2026, India leased two drones to provide persistent surveillance over the Indian Ocean. Which drones were these?
explain: India leased two MQ-9B Sea Guardian drones in the same week that it signed the maritime framework with Japan. Together they reflect a model that combines national surveillance hardware with information from chosen partners.
source: This week, India leased two MQ-9B Sea Guardian drones to provide persistent surveillance over the Indian Ocean

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's sugar import decision of August 2026:
items: Mills and refiners were allowed to import 1 million metric tons of raw sugar duty-free until 31 October.
The duty-free window replaced the usual 100% tariff on sugar imports.
It marked India's first sugar import in nearly a decade.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct: on 20 August 2026 New Delhi allowed 1 million metric tons of raw sugar in duty-free until 31 October, in place of the usual 100% tariff. India went from exporting sugar to importing it within a single harvest.
source: On Thursday, New Delhi allowed mills and refiners to import 1 million metric tons of raw sugar duty-free until October 31, replacing the usual 100% tariff.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's sugar supply position as reported in August 2026:
items: Before halting exports in May 2026, India had shipped the entire 1.59 million metric tons of sugar it had approved for export.
The harvest forecast of 27.9 million metric tons is below India's annual consumption of 28.5 million metric tons.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong: India approved 1.59 million metric tons of exports but shipped only more than 600,000 before halting trade in May. Output was initially expected at 30.95 million metric tons before the forecast was cut.
source: The harvest is now forecast at 27.9 million, below annual consumption of 28.5 million.

prompt: As reported in August 2026, Indian sugar mills diverted sugar into ethanol as India locked in petrol containing what share of ethanol?
explain: India locked in petrol blended with 20% ethanol, and mills diverted around 3 million metric tons of sugar equivalent into ethanol. This diversion contributed to the shortfall that forced sugar imports.
source: Mills diverted around 3 million metric tons of sugar equivalent into ethanol as India locked in petrol containing 20% ethanol.

prompt: In August 2026, India changed how rupee-settled exports are treated under its Foreign Trade Policy (FTP). Consider the following statements:
items: Exports paid for in rupees through approved banking channels now earn FTP benefits but still do not count towards export obligations.
The change covers rupee-paid exports to all countries, including Nepal and Bhutan.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) administers India's Foreign Trade Policy.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong. Rupee-paid exports now both earn FTP benefits and count towards export obligations, the change applies to any country other than Nepal and Bhutan, and the FTP is administered by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), not the RBI. The RBI's role was setting up Special Rupee Vostro Accounts in July 2022, which made rupee settlement legal.
source: Exports to any country other than Nepal and Bhutan, if paid for in rupees through approved banking channels, now earn FTP benefits and count towards export obligations, just as foreign-currency exports do.

prompt: Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs), which allow overseas banks to hold Indian rupees for trade settlement, were set up in July 2022 by which institution?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
explain: The RBI set up SRVAs in July 2022, making rupee settlement of trade legal. Until the DGFT's August 2026 move, exporters could not be sure whether such rupee receipts qualified for trade-policy benefits.
source: Rupee settlement has been legal since July 2022, when the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) set up Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVAs) for overseas banks to hold rupees, but until now exporters could not be sure if those receipts qualified.

prompt: In August 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh broke ground on a new Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE) yard able to build warships up to 200 metres long. Where is this yard located?
explain: GRSE's new 32-acre yard is at Raichak in West Bengal. It will let GRSE bid for next-generation destroyers alongside commercial vessels. Ishapore is where Yantra India Limited is adding forging presses.
source: GRSE's new 32-acre yard at Raichak in West Bengal will build warships up to 200 metres long, letting it bid for next-generation destroyers alongside commercial vessels.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the defence-industrial expansion projects launched in West Bengal in August 2026:
items: The five projects, worth about INR 35 billion, are at Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers and Yantra India Limited.
Yantra India Limited's new forging presses at Ishapore will produce gun barrels and naval-weapon components.
Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers has built over 800 vessels to date, most of them for the Indian Coast Guard.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: most of GRSE's more than 800 vessels were built for the Indian Navy, not the Coast Guard. Rajnath Singh called ship repair and overhaul the low-hanging fruit and urged India to become a maintenance hub for the Indian Ocean region.
source: GRSE has built over 800 vessels to date, most for the Indian Navy.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme, whose detailed rules were notified in August 2026:
items: The rules were notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology for a five-year scheme with an outlay of INR 625 billion.
To qualify under the Indian-brand track, a company needs an annual turnover of at least INR 100 billion.
Companies in both tracks can earn an additional 1.5% by using Indian components in at least 25% of their phones.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Indian brands need INR 10 billion in turnover, while the INR 100 billion threshold applies to large manufacturers. The Cabinet approved the broad framework alongside Semicon 2.0 in July 2026, and the notification sets the turnover, ownership, design and sourcing requirements.
source: On Friday, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology notified detailed rules for the five-year, INR 625 billion (USD 6.5 billion) Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme.

prompt: Under the Indian-brand track of the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme notified in August 2026, what additional incentive is offered for domestic design and research, over the base 5%?
explain: Indian brands receive 5% on eligible sales plus 3% for domestic design and research. To count as Indian brands, they must be majority-owned and controlled by citizens and hold their trademarks and intellectual property locally.
source: Indian brands need INR 10 billion (USD 104 million) and receive 5%, plus 3% for domestic design and research.

prompt: In August 2026, Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) signed a long-term agreement to supply fuel to Mauritius. Consider the following statements about it:
items: IOCL replaces Mauritius's State Trading Corporation as the importer of fuel into Mauritius.
The agreement locks in roughly 750,000 tonnes of annual demand for five years.
It is India's first such long-term fuel supply deal outside South Asia.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Mauritius's State Trading Corporation remains the importer. IOCL becomes the sole supplier under a Sales and Purchase Agreement tied to a government-to-government MoU, which replaces STC's old competitive tenders.
source: Mauritius's State Trading Corporation (STC) remains the importer, but the new Sales and Purchase Agreement, tied to a government-to-government MoU, locks in roughly 750,000 tonnes of annual demand for five years, replacing STC's old competitive tenders.

prompt: MAHASAGAR, India's Indian Ocean doctrine, was unveiled in March 2025 in which country?
explain: MAHASAGAR was unveiled in Mauritius in March 2025. The August 2026 fuel deal, together with a 27,500-tonne bunker-fuel facility at Port Louis and a joint biofuels policy, sits under this doctrine.
source: It all sits under MAHASAGAR, India's Indian Ocean doctrine, unveiled in Mauritius in March 2025.

prompt: In August 2026, India signed a telecom and technology Memorandum of Understanding with Brazil, covering artificial intelligence, 5G and 6G, and cybersecurity, at the BRICS Communications Ministers' meeting held in which Indian city?
explain: Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia signed the MoU with Brazil at the BRICS Communications Ministers' meeting in Pune. Separately, India and Mexico finalised the Terms of Reference for a preferential trade agreement after Mexico imposed tariffs of up to 50 per cent on goods from non-preferential partners.
source: signed a telecom and technology Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Brazil, covering artificial intelligence, 5G and 6G, and cybersecurity, at the BRICS Communications Ministers' meeting in Pune.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's revised foreign direct investment (FDI) rules for land-bordering countries, as reported in August 2026:
items: Investors from land-bordering countries holding non-controlling stakes of up to 10 per cent can use the automatic route without prior government approval.
The investment proposals reported under the revised rules up to August 20, 2026 came from investors based in land-bordering countries.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Commerce Ministry said the reported investors are based in third countries such as Mauritius, the United States, Singapore and the Cayman Islands. The 29 proposals, worth nearly INR 49 billion, span IT, artificial intelligence, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals and data centres.
source: The reform, which we covered here, lets investors with non-controlling stakes of up to 10 per cent from land-bordering countries use the automatic route, dropping the prior government approval that was required for such investment.

prompt: In August 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar visited Russia to co-chair the 27th session of which bilateral mechanism?
options: India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC)
Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Council of Foreign Ministers
explain: Jaishankar travelled to Russia on 23-24 August 2026 to co-chair the 27th IRIGC-TEC at the invitation of First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov. During the visit he was also to meet Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on regional and global issues.
source: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar will visit Russia on August 23-24 to co-chair the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation (IRIGC-TEC), at the invitation of First Deputy Prime Minister Denis Manturov.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the 25th round of India–China Special Representatives talks held in August 2026:
items: India was represented by its National Security Advisor and China by its Foreign Minister.
The talks were held in New Delhi, weeks ahead of the BRICS summit.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: NSA Ajit Doval met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing, not New Delhi. New Delhi is where Xi Jinping was expected for the BRICS summit on 12-13 September 2026. The Special Representatives mechanism is the main forum for the unresolved border, and this was the first such meeting in a year.
source: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval arrives in Beijing on Monday for the 25th round of Special Representatives (SR) talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, the first such meeting in a year and the main forum for the two countries' unresolved border.

prompt: In August 2026, Chhattisgarh's State Geological Programming Board cleared 45 mineral exploration projects for 2026-27. Consider the following statements:
items: The projects were cleared at the board's 26th meeting, held in Raipur.
The minerals covered include lithium, rare earth elements, niobium and tantalum.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both are correct. The board cleared the projects at its 26th meeting in Raipur on 19 August 2026, covering lithium, graphite, rare earth elements, niobium, tantalum, titanium and iron ore. Several projects lie in the Bastar belt, which until 2026 was the heart of India's Maoist insurgency.
source: cleared 45 mineral exploration projects for 2026-27 at its 26th meeting in Raipur on August 19, covering lithium, graphite, rare earth elements, niobium, tantalum, titanium, and iron ore

prompt: In August 2026, India lifted its ban on wheat exports. Consider the following statements about the ban and its background:
items: The ban on wheat exports was first imposed in May 2022.
The export curbs were extended to wheat flour in August 2022.
India's last wheat harvest before the lifting of the ban, at 120.6 million tonnes, fell short of the country's previous record.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first two statements are correct. The third is wrong because the 120.6 million tonne harvest was an all-time high, rebuilding the buffer that the heatwave-hit 2022 crop had drained.
source: India's last harvest hit an all-time high of 120.6 million tonnes, rebuilding the buffer the 2022 crop had drained.

prompt: In August 2026, India scrapped its ban on exports of wheat, durum wheat, flour and related products. Which body issued the notifications clearing these shipments?
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
explain: The DGFT notifications cleared shipments of wheat, the durum variety, flour and related products. The ban had been in place since May 2022, after a price spike following Russia's invasion of Ukraine pulled record volumes of Indian wheat abroad.
source: clearing shipments of wheat, the durum variety, flour, and related products through notifications from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).

prompt: In August 2026, attacks on commercial vessels and ports in which sea disrupted grain flows from major exporters and pushed Chicago wheat futures to a two-year high?
explain: Escalating Russia-Ukraine attacks in the Black Sea disrupted grain flows from some of the world's top exporters. Indian shipments could ease pressure on import-dependent countries across Asia, Africa and West Asia.
source: Escalating Russia-Ukraine attacks on commercial vessels and ports in the Black Sea have disrupted grain flows from some of the world's top exporters and pushed Chicago wheat futures to a two-year high.

prompt: In August 2026, the Tamil Nadu government scrapped a proposed greenfield airport meant to serve as Chennai's second airport. Where was this airport to be built?
explain: Chief Minister Joseph Vijay told the Assembly on 24 August 2026 that the state was scrapping the INR 274 billion Parandur project, a site he had opposed while campaigning. The state has named alternative areas but no final site or timetable.
source: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay told the Assembly on Monday that the state is scrapping the INR 274 billion (USD 2.86 billion) Parandur project, a site he had opposed on the campaign trail before becoming Chief Minister in May.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Parandur airport project, which Tamil Nadu scrapped in August 2026:
items: It was designed to handle 100 million passengers a year.
It had not yet received central clearance when it was scrapped.
Nearly half of the proposed site was irrigated farmland.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the project had central clearance secured, with land acquisition underway and a dedicated metro line planned. It drew sustained farmer protests because nearly half the site was irrigated farmland and about a quarter water bodies.
source: Parandur was designed for 100 million passengers a year, with central clearance secured, land acquisition underway, and a dedicated metro line drawn to reach it.

prompt: In August 2026, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare notified amendments to the Medical Devices Rules, 2017. Consider the following statements about these amendments:
items: Manufacturers that outsource product sterilisation no longer need a separate licence.
The European Union was added to the list of regulatory jurisdictions whose approvals qualify a device for a waiver of local clinical investigation.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both changes were notified together. Dropping the separate licence for outsourced sterilisation is meant to reduce duplication and paperwork. Adding the EU places it alongside the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Japan, whose approvals already qualified for the clinical investigation waiver.
source: A second change adds the European Union (EU) to the list of regulatory jurisdictions whose approvals qualify a device for a waiver of local clinical investigation, joining the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, and Japan.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the decision on DRDO missile technology announced in August 2026:
items: The Defence Minister approved transfers of DRDO technology for every conventional missile to qualified Indian companies.
The announcement did not name the specific missile systems, manufacturers or timetable for the transfers.
DRDO had transferred Astra Mk-I and its associated systems to Bharat Dynamics Limited in 2022.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the approval covers every conventional missile, the announcement names no systems, manufacturers, timetable or selection process, and Astra Mk-I went to Bharat Dynamics Limited in 2022. Until now, missile production after development has typically gone through state-owned Bharat Dynamics Limited.
source: The announcement names no systems, manufacturers, timetable or selection process.

prompt: In August 2026, the United States sanctioned four India-based firms for allegedly facilitating Iranian petroleum and petrochemical imports. Consider the following statements about these sanctions:
items: The sanctions were imposed by the US State Department.
Washington alleged that all four firms together imported Iranian products worth USD 119 million.
The measures formed part of Operation Economic Outcast, which targeted nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Washington attributes the USD 119 million in imports to three of the firms, not all four. Three Indian nationals were also sanctioned, as part of a wider campaign against Iran's military and energy trade.
source: The measures form part of Operation Economic Outcast, which targeted nearly 60 entities, individuals and vessels linked to Iran’s military and energy trade.

prompt: In August 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met Russian President Vladimir Putin. Consider the following statements:
items: Putin assured India that Russia would increase fertiliser shipments amid disruptions in West Asia.
India's bilateral trade deficit with Russia exceeded USD 50 billion in 2025–26.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Putin promised to sustain energy supplies and step up fertiliser shipments, and Jaishankar pressed Moscow to narrow a deficit that topped USD 50 billion in 2025–26. India sought better market access, payment mechanisms and business ties to close the gap.
source: Jaishankar meanwhile pressed Russia to narrow a bilateral trade deficit that exceeded USD 50 billion in 2025–26, calling for better market access, payment mechanisms and business ties.

prompt: In August 2026, India and China reopened all three Himalayan border trade posts between them. Which of the following was not among them?
explain: The three reopened trade posts are Nathu La, Shipki La and Lipulekh. Their reopening, alongside the Kailash Mansarovar pilgrimage, is part of the thaw that followed the 2024 patrolling deal.
source: reopened all three Himalayan border trade posts, at Nathu La, Shipki La, and Lipulekh, from early August

prompt: In August 2026, Rolls-Royce offered India a full transfer of technology on the engine for the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA). Consider the following statements about the offer:
items: India would keep the intellectual property rights on the engine.
The offer runs through a UK inter-governmental agreement and falls outside the US International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR).
The rival bidder, France's Safran, has proposed co-development with the Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE), India's state engine lab.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: India would keep the intellectual property rights, the offer runs through a UK inter-governmental agreement outside ITAR, and Safran has proposed co-development with GTRE. Staying outside ITAR matters because those rules let Washington block the export, sale or upgrade of any weapon carrying American technology.
source: Rolls-Royce is up against France's Safran, which has proposed co-development with the Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE), India's state engine lab.

prompt: In August 2026, during talks on an engine for the AMCA fighter, India was pressing Rolls-Royce for the hardest jet-engine technology of all, which lets an engine run hotter and so produce more thrust. Which technology is this?
explain: The story names the single-crystal turbine blade as the piece India wants most, because it lets an engine run hotter and push harder. India builds airframes, missiles and radar, but has long struggled to build a high-thrust jet engine, and the Tejas relies on GE engines whose deliveries have run late.
source: India is pressing for the hardest piece of all: the single-crystal turbine blade which lets an engine run hotter and therefore push harder.
