prompt: In August 2026, Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) and France's Safran Helicopter Engines signed to co-develop the 'Aravalli' engine for the Indian Multi-Role Helicopter. Consider the following statements about this engine:
items: It is being co-developed through the SAFHAL joint venture.
The helicopter it will power is meant to replace the Russian Mi-17 helicopters in use.
It falls in the 1,500 to 2,000 shaft-horsepower class.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the Aravalli engine is in the 3,500 to 4,000 shaft-horsepower class. The deal covers design, manufacture and lifecycle support for the engine of the under-development 13-tonne Indian Multi-Role Helicopter.
source: The engine covers design, manufacture, and lifecycle support in the 3,500 to 4,000 shaft-horsepower class, and would power a domestic replacement for the Russian Mi-17 helicopters currently in use.

prompt: In August 2026, a glacial collapse in Tibet's Gyirong county sent catastrophic flash floods into Nepal. Down which river valley did the mud and debris travel?
explain: The debris crashed down the Bhote Koshi River valley from Gyirong county after a glacier gave way on 26 August 2026. The US Geological Survey first logged the event as a 4.4 magnitude earthquake and later revised its assessment to a glacial collapse.
source: A wall of mud and debris crashed down the Bhote Koshi River valley from Tibet's Gyirong county early on Wednesday morning after a glacier gave way.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India–Uzbekistan summit held in August 2026:
items: The two countries elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
The two countries set a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030.
Negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement began after a feasibility study was completed.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: A feasibility study has been completed and could lead to a Preferential Trade Agreement, but negotiations have not begun. The USD 5 billion target for 2030 compares with trade of USD 1.3 billion and needs roughly 31 per cent annual growth for five years.
source: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev elevated ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership on Sunday and reported progress on a long-term uranium supply arrangement.

prompt: Under an agreement signed between India and Uzbekistan in August 2026, Indian Unified Payments Interface (UPI) apps will be able to scan which payment codes?
explain: The agreement allows Indian UPI apps to scan Uzbekistan's UZQR payment codes. It was one of 11 instruments signed, alongside deals on mineral resources and financial dialogue.
source: Among 11 signed instruments were deals on mineral resources and financial dialogue, plus an agreement allowing Indian Unified Payments Interface apps to scan Uzbekistan’s UZQR payment codes.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to India–Uzbekistan economic ties, as reported in August 2026:
items: 2019 uranium supply contract — 1,100 metric tonnes through 2030
Uzbekistan's imports from India — USD 164.6 million
Growth in bilateral trade in 2025 — 31 per cent
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: None of the pairs is correct: the 2019 contract covers 1,100 metric tonnes through 2026, not 2030; Uzbekistan imported USD 1.15 billion from India, while USD 164.6 million is the value of its exports to India; and trade grew 33.3 per cent in 2025, with 31 per cent being the annual growth needed to reach USD 5 billion. The leaders set a 2030 target of USD 5 billion in trade and elevated ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
source: Trade grew 33.3 per cent in 2025, but reaching USD 5 billion requires roughly 31 per cent annual growth for five years.

prompt: In August 2026, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) proposed warning labels for packaged food and drinks in a filing before the Supreme Court. Consider the following statements about the proposal:
items: A warning would apply to any product high in just one of saturated fat, sugar or salt.
Single-ingredient foods are exempt from the proposed labelling.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the red hexagon applies only to products high in two or more of saturated fat, sugar or salt. Single-ingredient foods are exempt, and the rollout is phased. The Supreme Court had floated a one-nutrient trigger, so a drink high only in sugar escapes the warning under FSSAI's version.
source: In a Supreme Court filing on Friday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) called for a red hexagon on products high in two or more of saturated fat, sugar, or salt.

prompt: Consider the following pairs of jurisdictions and front-of-pack food labelling systems:
items: United Kingdom — Traffic-light ratings
Europe — Nutri-Score
India (FSSAI proposal, August 2026) — Red hexagon warning
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three are correctly matched: the UK uses traffic-light ratings, Nutri-Score is used across Europe, and FSSAI proposed a red hexagon for India. Industry groups that opposed labels in India as confusing use such systems abroad.
source: Coca-Cola, Nestle, and PepsiCo industry groups have long opposed labels as confusing, though many use them abroad, from traffic-light ratings in the UK to Nutri-Score across Europe.

prompt: In August 2026, India's Commerce Secretary held trade talks in Chile and Argentina. Consider the following statements:
items: State-owned miner KABIL's Catamarca lithium project is the first by an Indian company in Argentina.
India and Chile are negotiating a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement to upgrade a preferential pact in force since 2007.
The fourth India-Argentina Joint Trade Committee was held in Santiago.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong. The fourth India-Argentina Joint Trade Committee was held in Buenos Aires, while Santiago was where the Commerce Secretary advanced the CEPA talks with Chile. India's trade with Argentina topped USD 6.5 billion in 2025, up 17 per cent.
source: Days earlier in Buenos Aires he led the fourth India-Argentina Joint Trade Committee, where state-owned miner KABIL reported progress on its Catamarca lithium project, the first by an Indian company in Argentina.

prompt: In August 2026, the Government of India notified rules making Indian Standard Time (IST) the common reference for legal, administrative, commercial and official purposes. Consider the following statements:
items: Organisations have been given 180 days to adapt their systems to the rules.
The government is building domestic time-distribution infrastructure using NavIC and other Indian sources to reduce reliance on foreign satellites.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements match the story. Organisations get a 180-day window to comply, and the government is building time-distribution infrastructure on NavIC, India's satellite navigation system, and other Indian sources. The aim is to cut critical systems' dependence on foreign satellites for timing.
source: The government is also building domestic time-distribution infrastructure using NavIC, India's satellite navigation system, and other Indian sources, reducing critical systems' reliance on foreign satellites.

prompt: In August 2026, Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan launched 'Gnani Artha'. Which of the following best describes it?
options: A sovereign AI stack combining a language model with a workflow platform
A satellite constellation built for secure government communications
A semiconductor fabrication unit for making indigenous AI chips
A digital public platform for settling cross-border rupee payments
explain: Gnani Artha is a homegrown sovereign AI stack. It pairs the large language model Evon 3.3 with Plexus, a platform that connects AI tools to institutional workflows. It was developed by Bengaluru-based GNANI AI.
source: The stack combines Evon 3.3, a large language model, with Plexus, a platform connecting AI tools to institutional workflows.

prompt: In September 2026, the Prime Minister of which European country was scheduled to visit India from 2 to 4 September, and to meet stakeholders in Mumbai's diamond, ports and logistics sectors?
explain: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever was due to visit India from 2 to 4 September 2026. It was his first trip since taking office in February 2025, and Defence Minister Theo Francken was to accompany him. He was also to give a keynote at a CII business event linked to the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement.
source: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever will visit India from September 2 to 4, 2026, his first trip since taking office in February 2025, and will be accompanied by Defence Minister Theo Francken.

prompt: In September 2026, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) automated the issuance of Free Sale and Commerce Certificates. Consider the following statements:
items: Exporters use these certificates to prove that a product is sold freely in India.
Under the new system, applications that fail the risk checks are rejected automatically without review by an officer.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. Cases that fail the system's risk checks are not rejected; they still go to a regional officer for review. Eligible applications now clear the DGFT portal without manual scrutiny, which cuts processing time.
source: Eligible applications will now clear the DGFT portal without manual scrutiny, cutting processing time, while cases that fail the system's risk checks still route to a regional officer for review.

prompt: In September 2026, Kenya's President William Ruto ordered Tata Chemicals to exit its natural soda ash operation at Magadi. Through which acquisition had Tata gained this operation?
options: Its 2008 purchase of Jaguar Land Rover
explain: Tata acquired Magadi in 2005 when it bought the British company Brunner Mond, which gave it access to low-cost natural soda ash. The operation dates to 1911. Tata's lease runs to 2053, and the licensing fight remains in court.
source: Tata acquired Magadi through its 2005 purchase of Britain’s Brunner Mond, gaining low-cost natural soda ash.

prompt: In September 2026, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) chargesheeted a US citizen and six Ukrainian nationals accused of training ethnic armed groups in Myanmar in drone warfare. Consider the following statements:
items: The accused allegedly entered India through Mizoram before crossing into Myanmar.
The chargesheet against the seven includes charges under the anti-terror law (UAPA).
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The accused allegedly entered through Mizoram and crossed into Myanmar. They were arrested under the UAPA in March 2026, but the chargesheet carries only immigration charges, though the NIA says the terror probe stays open.
source: Arrested in March under the anti-terror law (UAPA), the seven now face only immigration charges, though the NIA says the terror probe stays open.

prompt: In September 2026, India joined a US-led multi-country initiative announced by the US Department of Commerce. What is the initiative meant to guide the development of?
explain: The initiative aims to guide the development of 6G telecom networks so that future networks stay aligned on shared security interests and competitiveness. The deal was sealed when US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick met Minister of State for Commerce Jitin Prasada on the sidelines of the G20 Innovation Ministerial.
source: India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in a global initiative to guide the development of next-generation 6G telecom networks, the US Department of Commerce announced on September 8.

prompt: In September 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake. Consider the following statements about the outcomes:
items: India agreed to upgrade six Indian-supplied L70 guns in Sri Lanka under an Indian grant.
The two sides inaugurated three bridges built by Indian defence forces.
The agreements were signed at a meeting held in New Delhi.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The third statement is wrong because the meeting and signing took place in Colombo, not New Delhi. The agreements also expand cooperation between the two countries' cadet corps and defence colleges, and Dissanayake said Sri Lankan territory would not be used against India's security interests.
source: On Wednesday, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo, and the two countries signed agreements to upgrade six Indian-supplied L70 guns under an Indian grant

prompt: Consider the following statements about steel trade under the draft India–EU Free Trade Agreement published in September 2026:
items: India would receive annual steel quota access of approximately 1.64 million tonnes.
The EU's new steel regime, introduced in July 2026, reserves half its import quota for free-trade partners.
Steel shipments exceeding applicable quotas face a 25% additional duty.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Shipments exceeding applicable quotas face a 50% additional duty, not 25%. India's quota splits into roughly 947,000 tonnes under ordinary trading terms and 695,000 tonnes through the agreement.
source: Shipments exceeding applicable quotas face a 50% additional duty.

prompt: With reference to Indian steel exports to the European Union under the draft India–EU Free Trade Agreement, as of September 2026, consider the following statements:
items: Quota access under the agreement exempts Indian steel from the EU's separate carbon levy.
Brussels has recognised India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) for deductions against the carbon levy.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Quota access leaves the separate carbon levy in place, and India's CCTS had yet to gain recognition from Brussels. The EU already allows deductions for eligible carbon prices paid abroad, so recognition of the CCTS would lower the carbon bill for Indian steel.
source: But Delhi’s Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) has yet to gain recognition from Brussels.

prompt: In September 2026, India approved electricity exports to Nepal after floods damaged Nepal's hydropower infrastructure. Consider the following statements about this approval:
items: India's Ministry of Power approved exports of up to 654 megawatts for 18 hours a day.
The supplies will flow through newly built cross-border transmission lines.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The Ministry of Power approved up to 654 MW daily from midnight to 6 pm, between 13 September and 31 December 2026. Statement 2 is wrong because the supplies use two existing cross-border transmission lines, not new ones. The ministry will review volumes for January 2027 in December.
source: On Monday, India’s Ministry of Power approved exports of up to 654 megawatts to Nepal for 18 hours daily, from midnight to 6 pm, between 13 September and 31 December.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India's merchandise trade data for August 2026, released by the Commerce Ministry in September 2026:
items: Goods exports rose by more than 25% compared with August 2025.
Gold imports fell compared with August 2025.
Excluding petroleum and gems and jewellery, the trade deficit narrowed compared with August 2025.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Exports rose 26.1% and gold imports fell 57.75% year on year, but the deficit excluding petroleum and gems and jewellery widened to USD 14.54 billion from USD 13.13 billion, because imports grew from a larger base. The overall deficit of USD 26.86 billion narrowed by just USD 360 million year on year.
source: Imports started from a larger base, so the deficit in those goods widened to USD 14.54 billion, from USD 13.13 billion a year earlier.

prompt: In September 2026, the US House of Representatives passed a bill targeting buyers of Russian oil. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It would let the US President impose a tariff of up to 100% on India for buying Russian oil.
An amendment naming India and nine other countries as explicit targets was adopted on the House floor.
The version passed applies only to the top five buyers of Russian oil and gas by volume.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The House Rules Committee voted down Steny Hoyer's amendment naming India and nine other countries before it reached the floor. The passed bill keeps the Senate's version, which covers the top five buyers, a group India tops alongside China.
source: The House Rules Committee voted down both before either reached the floor.

prompt: The Russia and Iran sanctions bill passed by the US House in September 2026 was renamed in honour of which US lawmaker?
explain: The bill's Republican co-author, Lindsey Graham, died in July 2026, days after securing the White House's backing, and colleagues renamed it the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. Hoyer and Meeks moved the amendments that the House Rules Committee rejected.
source: Graham, the bill's Republican co-author, died in July days after securing the White House's backing; colleagues renamed the bill in his honour.

prompt: In September 2026, India summoned Pakistan's Charge d'Affaires in New Delhi after a Pakistan Navy vessel collided with an Indian Navy ship on a routine surveillance mission. Where did the collision take place?
explain: The collision happened in the Arabian Sea on 15 September 2026, during a routine Indian Navy surveillance mission. The Ministry of External Affairs called the Pakistani vessel's conduct unacceptable and unprofessional, saying it was manoeuvring at high speed. No major damage was reported.
source: a Pakistan Navy vessel collided with an Indian Navy ship during a routine surveillance mission in the Arabian Sea on Tuesday, September 15.

prompt: In September 2026, the European Commission proposed excluding India from permissions to import European Union metal scrap. Consider the following statements about this proposal:
items: It falls under EU waste-export rules that apply from May 2027.
The Commission's assessment cites insufficient evidence of pollution controls and enforcement in India's recycling system.
It follows Brussels' abandonment of a separate 15 per cent export duty on aluminium scrap.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the rules apply from 21 May 2027, the assessment cites insufficient evidence of pollution controls and enforcement, and the proposal follows Brussels' abandonment of a separate 15 per cent aluminium-scrap export duty. India had sought an exemption in June 2026, warning that restrictions could raise manufacturers' costs and undermine gains from the bilateral trade agreement.
source: The proposal follows Brussels’ abandonment of a separate 15 per cent aluminium-scrap export duty.

prompt: In September 2026, US President Donald Trump signed the Russia and Iran sanctions legislation into law. Consider the following statements about this law:
items: It provides for additional tariffs of up to 50 per cent on qualifying buyers of Russian energy, a list that includes India.
Its signing immediately imposed a 100 per cent tariff on Indian goods.
The President has no authority to waive the duties once they are imposed.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are wrong: the law provides for additional tariffs of up to 100 per cent (not 50 per cent), the signing does not itself establish a 100 per cent tariff on Indian goods, and the President retains authority to waive duties after submitting a national-interest certification and explanation to Congress. The law was signed on Friday 18 September 2026, following its passage in the House.
source: The President retains authority to waive duties after submitting a national-interest certification and explanation to Congress.

prompt: In September 2026, India more than doubled its weekly bilateral air-seat cap, raising it to over 16,000 seats a week, with which country?
explain: India and Vietnam lifted their bilateral air-seat cap from 8,000 to over 16,000 seats a week. The increase came as airlines in both countries had used up, or were close to exhausting, their existing flying rights.
source: India and Vietnam have lifted their bilateral air-seat cap to over 16,000 a week, more than double the existing 8,000.

prompt: In September 2026, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) issued a mandate on mobile tariff plans. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It requires operators to offer more voice-and-text-only postpaid plans at reduced tariffs.
Operators must offer such an option matching every validity period of 30 days or less in their bundled voice, text and data plans.
Operators must also provide a calendar-month renewal option and at least one longer-duration plan.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because TRAI mandated more voice-and-text-only prepaid plans at reduced tariffs, not postpaid plans. The rules target low-income consumers and those who do not need mobile data, who had limited short-term choices.
source: the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) mandated more voice-and-text-only prepaid plans at reduced tariffs.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the uniform design guidelines issued by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in September 2026:
items: They apply to four- and six-lane access-controlled highways, including expressways.
They link lane configurations to traffic volumes.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the guidelines explicitly exclude expressways. They cover new roads and upgrades and prescribe ramp-based interchanges and one-metre boundary walls to keep out unauthorised access and stray cattle.
source: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has issued uniform design guidelines for upcoming four- and six-lane access-controlled highways, excluding expressways.

prompt: In September 2026, the US President signed a law allowing tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil. What is the name of this law?
options: Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act
explain: President Donald Trump signed the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act in September 2026. It allows tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil and exposes India to further trade pressure. India's Russian oil imports fell 16.5 per cent in August to about 2.1 million barrels a day, though Russia remains its largest supplier.
source: President Donald Trump signed the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, allowing tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian oil

prompt: In September 2026, India ordered 112 coal-fired captive power plants to maximise generation from October to December and sell surplus electricity to the grid. Consider the following statements in this context:
items: The order covers plants supplying industries such as steel mills and aluminium smelters.
Weaker rainfall reduced hydroelectric generation, forcing coal plants to compensate.
Nighttime electricity shortages in September 2026 exceeded the shortfalls of the preceding summer.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements are correct: the order covers plants supplying steel mills and aluminium smelters, weaker rainfall cut hydroelectric output, and nighttime shortages reached 7.7 gigawatts in September, exceeding the summer shortfalls. Power-station coal stocks also fell 24% between end-August and 26 September, leaving roughly seven days' supply.
source: Nighttime electricity shortages reached 7.7 gigawatts in September, exceeding this year’s summer shortfalls.

prompt: By late September 2026, power-station coal stocks in India had fallen sharply since the end of August. Roughly how many days' supply did they hold without replenishment?
explain: Coal stocks at power stations fell 24% between end-August and 26 September, leaving roughly seven days' supply. Relief was uneven: cooler weather and extra power purchases helped Kerala avoid cuts on September 24–25.
source: Power-station coal stocks fell 24% between end-August and 26 September, leaving roughly seven days’ supply without replenishment.

prompt: In September 2026, the Union health ministry ordered state governments to crack down on the illegal sale of nicotine pouches. Consider the following statements:
items: Nicotine pouches are unapproved and illegal under Indian drug laws.
An Indian court accepted the defence that airport duty-free shops are immune from domestic laws.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Nicotine pouches remain unapproved and illegal under Indian drug laws, even though they are sold online, in local shops and at duty-free outlets. Statement 2 is wrong because the court quashed the Adani Group's argument that its airport duty-free shops were immune from domestic laws. The federal drug advisory panel has also recommended a complete ban on approving any new nicotine formulations.
source: Despite growing global popularity and availability via online channels, local shops, and duty-free outlets, nicotine pouches remain unapproved and illegal under Indian drug laws.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–US trade relations as of September 2026:
items: The US Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs in February 2026.
The US Trade Representative is investigating alleged excess capacity in Indian manufacturing under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.
Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said India is waiting for Washington to guarantee it lower tariffs than competing economies.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The Supreme Court struck down reciprocal tariffs in February, the USTR has opened a Section 301 probe into Indian manufacturing, and Goyal said on September 24 that the terms were almost done. Washington is still settling a new legal basis for tariffs.
source: Separately, the US Trade Representative (USTR) is investigating alleged excess capacity in Indian manufacturing under Section 301 of the US Trade Act.

prompt: In September 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said India–China ties had improved following Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to New Delhi. Which summit did Xi attend during that visit?
explain: Xi Jinping visited New Delhi for the BRICS summit, and Jaishankar said ties have improved since then. He summed up India's approach to China as not getting locked into a problem that benefits others.
source: Jaishankar said ties with China have improved since 2025, and even more since 2024, following President Xi Jinping’s visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit.

prompt: In September 2026, the Ministry of Steel announced a Steel Industry Safety Council. Consider the following statements:
items: The council will be chaired by the Union Minister of Steel.
A separate Steel Industry Safety Directorate will run safety audits and investigate serious incidents.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The council will be chaired by the steel secretary, not the minister. It will approve industry safety standards and review serious accidents and near misses. A new directorate will handle audits and investigations.
source: The Ministry of Steel will set up a Steel Industry Safety Council, chaired by the steel secretary, to approve industry safety standards and review serious accidents and near misses.

prompt: Consider the following statements about phase three of the Green Energy Corridor Scheme, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2026:
items: It has an outlay of INR 1.9 trillion to upgrade state power grids and integrate renewable energy.
It aims to move 135 gigawatts of renewable capacity from remote areas to the main grid by 2032-33.
Its implementation will be overseen by a central public sector transmission company rather than state utilities.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: state transmission utilities will oversee implementation, and new transmission projects will be competitively tendered. The corridor builds lines and substations to connect renewable generation to the grid.
source: State transmission utilities will oversee implementation.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Green Energy Corridor Scheme as reported in October 2026:
items: Renewable capacity targeted by phase two — 20 gigawatts
Battery storage included in phase three — 50 gigawatt-hours
Direct central financial support for phase three — INR 540 billion
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs match the story. Phase two, approved in 2022, targeted 20 GW, while phase three adds 50 GWh of battery storage to ease congestion and supply power outside solar hours, backed by INR 540 billion of central support to keep tariffs low.
source: That’s a big jump compared to the 20 gigawatts targeted by phase two, approved in 2022.

prompt: According to reporting on the Green Energy Corridor phase three approval in 2026, what is India's target for non-fossil power capacity by 2035-36?
explain: India targets 900 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2035-36, and the corridor expansion is meant to support it. In July 2026, transmission bottlenecks left about 12 GW of solar capacity unable to run at full output.
source: The expansion aligns with India’s target of hitting 900 gigawatts of non-fossil capacity by 2035-2036, while boosting domestic battery manufacturing and grid management supply chains.

prompt: In September 2026, the Ministry of Power notified the Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE)-III norms for passenger cars. Consider the following statements about them:
items: They apply from April 2027 to March 2032 and tighten fleet targets by 16.7 per cent over the period.
The UN-developed Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP) is stricter than India's Modified Indian Driving Cycle (MIDC).
The factor for converting targets between the MIDC and WLTP tests was notified along with the norms.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because the conversion factor between the two tests has yet to be notified. From April 2027, carmakers must report results under both the MIDC, India's standard fuel-economy test, and the stricter WLTP.
source: The rules apply from April 1, 2027, to March 31, 2032, and tighten fleet targets by 16.7 per cent over the period.

prompt: As reported in October 2026, Apple Pay launched in India through Axis Bank. Its initial launch covered Axis credit cards on which card networks?
explain: The launch initially covers Axis credit cards on the Visa and Mastercard networks. Cards on RuPay, India's domestic network, are ineligible. Axis is India's fourth-largest credit card issuer, with 16.3 million of the country's 124 million cards as of August.
source: It initially covers Axis credit cards on the Visa and Mastercard networks, and cards on RuPay, India's domestic network, are ineligible.

prompt: In October 2026, the Ministry of Mines opened bidding for the Sewell Rise-01 and West Sewell Ridge-01 offshore mineral blocks. In which sea are these blocks located?
explain: The two blocks offered on 1 October 2026 lie in the Andaman Sea. An earlier offer of seven blocks near Great Nicobar in 2024 failed to attract sufficient qualifying bids.
source: The Ministry of Mines opened bidding for two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea on Thursday, with submissions due by 28 December.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the offshore mineral blocks put up for bidding by the Ministry of Mines in October 2026:
items: The two blocks together cover more than 1,632 square kilometres.
According to the ministry, their seabed nodules and crusts contain cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements.
Bid submissions are due by 28 December 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. The ministry says these minerals are used in batteries, electronics and advanced manufacturing, and the bids cover both exploration and mining extraction rights.
source: Mineral exploration and mining extraction rights over Sewell Rise-01 and West Sewell Ridge-01, which cover more than 1,632 square kilometres.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Andaman Sea offshore mineral auction launched in October 2026:
items: The two blocks on offer are a re-auction of the blocks near Great Nicobar offered in 2024.
The launch announcement gives no estimate of how much mineral can be recovered or at what cost.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because a government official said the two blocks cover different areas and are not a re-auction of the seven blocks offered in 2024. Government surveys have established mineral occurrences in both areas, but India's domestic miners lack deep-sea experience, so success hinges on foreign partnerships.
source: These two are different areas, rather than a re-auction, according to a government official.

prompt: In September 2026, US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. Consider the following statements about it:
items: It allows Washington to impose tariffs of up to 50 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas.
Its tariff provisions apply to countries buying Russian gas as well as Russian oil.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the Act permits tariffs of up to 100 per cent, not 50 per cent, and it covers buyers of both Russian oil and gas. Days after it was signed, Prime Minister Modi spoke with Trump by phone on 30 September 2026, their first call since June.
source: which lets Washington impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas.

prompt: In September 2026, the Ministry of External Affairs issued an advisory warning Indians travelling to Russia against joining the Russian armed forces. Consider the following statements about it:
items: The ministry noted that some Indians had asked to give up their citizenship so they could take a Russian passport and enlist.
The advisory urged Indians to vet any job offer from agents not registered with the ministry.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both points appear in the advisory, which called enlisting a dangerous path that the government strongly discourages. The ministry said many Indians were seeking such offers willingly for the money and expected the government to secure their release later.
source: It urged Indians to vet any job offer from agents not registered with the ministry.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise that opened in September 2026:
items: It is the second edition of the exercise.
It is being held at Subic Bay, on the Philippines' South China Sea coast.
INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish are the Indian warships taking part.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The second edition opened on 28 September 2026 at Subic Bay in the Philippines, with INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish representing India. A harbour phase of expert exchanges comes before joint manoeuvres at sea, and the Ministry of Defence placed the drill under India's Act East Policy.
source: Indian warships INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish are exercising with maritime forces of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) at Subic Bay, on the Philippines' South China Sea coast, in the second edition of the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise.

prompt: In October 2026, India and Pakistan lodged protests with each other over a shooting by India's Border Security Force on 2 October. Consider the following statements:
items: The shooting took place in the Ferozepur sector of Rajasthan.
Each government lodged its protest with the other country's high commissioner.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The Ferozepur sector is in Punjab, not Rajasthan. The protests were made to each other's chargé d'affaires, because neither country has had a high commissioner in the other's capital since 2019.
source: On Saturday, each government protested to the other's chargé d'affaires over the October 2 killing of two Pakistani men by India's Border Security Force (BSF) in Punjab's Ferozepur sector.

prompt: As of October 2026, since which year have India and Pakistan been without a high commissioner in each other's capitals?
explain: Pakistan expelled India's envoy in 2019 after New Delhi revoked Jammu and Kashmir's special constitutional status. Since then, the two countries have dealt with each other through chargé d'affaires.
source: Neither country has had a high commissioner in the other's capital since 2019, when Pakistan expelled India's envoy after New Delhi revoked Jammu and Kashmir's special constitutional status.

prompt: In October 2026, the Centre assigned standard names to 28 places and geographical features in Ladakh. Consider the following statements about this exercise:
items: The names were placed on the official Survey of India map.
The places named included Gogra and Hot Spring, flashpoints during the 2020 India–China military standoff.
All the named sites lie on the Indian-held side of the Line of Actual Control.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong because several of the named sites lie across the LAC in Aksai Chin, which China has controlled since the 1950s. India says the aim is accurate identification and public awareness.
source: Several of the sites named lie across the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Aksai Chin, which China has controlled since the 1950s.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the India–China boundary dispute:
items: Zangnan — Chinese name for Arunachal Pradesh
Kumarayana Point — Located on China's G219 highway
G219 highway — Links Tibet with Xinjiang
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correct. China calls Arunachal Pradesh Zangnan, or South Tibet, and Kumarayana Point, named by India in October 2026, sits on the G219, a key military route linking Tibet with Xinjiang.
source: They include Guru Rinpoche Lake, east of China's G219 highway, and Kumarayana Point, on the highway itself.

prompt: Consider the following statements about India–Canada trade relations as of October 2026:
items: Bilateral trade between India and Canada rose 8.2% to $7.95 billion in fiscal year 2025-26.
The fifth round of trade negotiations began in October 2026, with a final deal targeted by December 2026.
The diplomatic freeze between the two countries began in 2023 after then-PM Justin Trudeau alleged Indian involvement in the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because bilateral trade fell 8.2% to $7.95 billion, not rose. Canadian Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu was due to visit New Delhi in October 2026 with a 300-strong business delegation, ahead of Prime Minister Modi's planned December visit.
source: Bilateral trade between India and Canada fell 8.2% to $7.95 billion last fiscal year, but momentum is shifting fast.

prompt: In October 2026, India and Canada began the fifth round of talks on which type of trade agreement?
explain: The talks are for the India–Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), with a final deal targeted by December 2026. TBB reads the speed of these talks as a signal to US negotiators that India has viable alternative export destinations.
source: Fifth-round talks for the India–Canada Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) kick off today, aiming for a final deal by December.

prompt: Consider the following statements about export support measures extended by the Department of Commerce in September 2026:
items: The Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) scheme was extended to December 31, 2026, with rates and value caps unchanged.
RoDTEP refunds central, state and local taxes built into the price of exported goods.
Component II of the Resilience and Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation (RELIEF) offers 95 per cent risk cover through the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation on shipments to West Asia.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the story. RELIEF was launched in March 2026 after freight and insurance costs spiked on West Asian shipping routes, and its Component II also holds premiums at pre-disruption levels.
source: The component offers 95 per cent risk cover through the state-run Export Credit Guarantee Corporation (ECGC) on shipments to the region and holds premiums at pre-disruption levels.

prompt: In October 2026, India and Switzerland signed agreements during Swiss President Guy Parmelin's state visit. Consider the following statements about them:
items: The Migration and Mobility Partnership provides for multiple-entry visas valid for up to ten years.
A separate agreement lets 300 young professionals a year from each country take up temporary jobs in the other.
The Migration and Mobility Partnership commits both sides to tackling irregular migration and trafficking.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The multiple-entry visas are valid for up to five years, with stays of up to six months per visit, not ten years. The young professionals route matters because Indian workers otherwise compete for Switzerland's annual cap of 8,500 permits for workers from outside Europe's free-movement zone.
source: The Migration and Mobility Partnership (MMP) provides for multiple-entry visas valid for up to five years, with stays of up to six months per visit, and renewable one-year student permits.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the commitments of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) countries under the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA):
items: Investment to be mobilised in India — USD 100 billion
Period over which the investment is to be mobilised — 15 years
Direct jobs to be supported in India — one million
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs match the TEPA commitments made by Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. The second India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on 7 October 2026 marked a year since the agreement came into force.
source: Under the agreement, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein aim to mobilise USD 100 billion of investment in India over 15 years and support one million direct jobs in India.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the scientific partnership agreements India signed with Swiss institutions in October 2026:
items: The agreement with the Swiss National Science Foundation supports exploratory joint research.
The agreement with the Zurich University of Applied Sciences provides for training Indian engineers in tunnelling.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: The Zurich University of Applied Sciences agreement is meant to train early-stage Indian startups, not engineers in tunnelling. Tunnelling, ropeways and electric vehicles fall under separate cooperation between India's road transport ministry and Switzerland's economic affairs department.
source: one with the Swiss National Science Foundation to support exploratory joint research, and one with the Zurich University of Applied Sciences to train early-stage Indian startups.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Fleet Support Ships being built for the Indian Navy, the first of which was due to be launched in October 2026:
items: Five such ships are being built, each displacing 43,500 tonnes.
Hindustan Shipyard Limited leads the programme, with Larsen & Toubro contracted for part-construction of two ships.
The ships will carry fuel, water, ammunition and stores to supply warships at sea.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct: five 43,500-tonne ships, led by Hindustan Shipyard with L&T building parts of two, will replenish warships with fuel, water, ammunition and stores. This allows longer deployments between port visits, helping the Navy sustain several missions at once.
source: The ships will carry fuel, water, ammunition, and stores.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Indian Navy's Fleet Support Ship programme as of October 2026:
items: The first ship was due to be launched at Hindustan Shipyard Limited in Visakhapatnam on 6 October 2026.
Deliveries of the ships are scheduled to begin in mid-2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: deliveries are scheduled to begin in mid-2027, and dates for trials and operational service had not been announced. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was also to inaugurate an upgraded slipway and a 300-tonne crane at the yard.
source: The first of five Fleet Support Ships being built for the Indian Navy is due to launch today, 6 October, at Hindustan Shipyard Limited in Visakhapatnam.

prompt: In October 2026, Larsen & Toubro was carrying out part-construction of two Indian Navy Fleet Support Ships at Kattupalli. Kattupalli is located near which city?
explain: L&T's share of the work is at Kattupalli, near Chennai, while Hindustan Shipyard in Visakhapatnam leads the programme. Concurrent construction at the two yards is intended to meet delivery timelines.
source: Hindustan Shipyard leads the programme, with Larsen & Toubro contracted for part-construction of two ships at Kattupalli, near Chennai.

prompt: Consider the following statements about Exercise Mountain Guardian 2026, which India and the UAE began in October 2026:
items: It is being held at Chaubatia in Uttarakhand and focuses on mountain warfare.
Its 92 participants are split equally between the Indian and Emirati armies.
It follows a strategic defence partnership framework agreed during the Indian Prime Minister's visit to the UAE in May 2026.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The two-week drill at Chaubatia runs until 18 October with 92 troops shared equally, and it builds on the framework agreed on 15 May that listed training and exercises among areas of cooperation. The armies' earlier exercise, Desert Cyclone, first held in Rajasthan in January 2024, trained for urban combat in desert terrain.
source: India and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) began Exercise Mountain Guardian 2026, a two-week army drill focused on mountain warfare, at Chaubatia in Uttarakhand on Monday.

prompt: In October 2026, the Centre agreed to fund Project VeerAI, an AI chip for CCTV systems developed by Bengaluru-based BigEndian Semiconductors. Consider the following statements:
items: The Technology Development Board, which is providing the funding, is part of the Department of Science and Technology.
The government funding covers the entire cost of Project VeerAI.
The money comes from the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the INR 1.3 billion covers only half of Project VeerAI's INR 2.6 billion cost. The funding aims to take the camera-focused chip from mid-stage testing to a deployment-ready product, sold first to surveillance buyers in India and the Global South.
source: The Technology Development Board (TDB), part of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), signed an agreement on Monday to give Bengaluru-based BigEndian Semiconductors INR 1.3 billion (USD 13.5 million) from the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.

prompt: In October 2026, Anthropic began processing requests to its Claude AI models inside India. Consider the following statements about this development:
items: The in-country processing is delivered through Microsoft's Azure cloud platform.
The National Payments Corporation of India said it is building its agentic AI platform, AiNxt, on Claude.
An industry technology chief tied the shift to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: The first statement is wrong because the processing runs through Amazon Web Services' Bedrock platform, not Azure. The service targets banks, insurers and public bodies that need data kept in the country, and Mahindra Group's technology chief linked it to the DPDP Act.
source: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), which runs the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), India's real-time mobile payments system, said it is building its agentic AI platform, AiNxt, on Claude.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to cheetahs brought to India under the project to reintroduce the species:
items: Namibia — eight cheetahs in September 2022
South Africa — 12 cheetahs in February 2023
Botswana — nine cheetahs in February 2026
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three pairs are correct. Namibia sent eight cheetahs in September 2022, South Africa sent 12 in February 2023 and Botswana sent nine in February 2026, to restore a species that went extinct in India in 1952. In October 2026, a litter of five at Kuno National Park took India's cheetah count to 60, and the cubs' Botswanan father starts a new genetic line.
source: Botswana's nine cheetahs arrived in February, following eight from Namibia in September 2022 and 12 from South Africa in February 2023, under a project to restore a species that went extinct in India in 1952.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which drew opposition protests in October 2026:
items: The Election Commission of India says the SIR is meant to clean up India's voter rolls.
In October 2026, the Supreme Court declined to hear petitions challenging the SIR and the Chief Election Commissioner's conduct.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because on 5 October 2026 the Supreme Court agreed to hear the petitions and said it would step in if any decisions were found to be unlawful. Opposition parties say the SIR favours the BJP, which the ECI and the BJP deny.
source: On Monday, a day before the march, the Supreme Court agreed to hear petitions challenging the voter drive and Kumar's conduct.

prompt: In October 2026, opposition MPs marched from Parliament to the Election Commission of India headquarters demanding the resignation of which Chief Election Commissioner?
explain: The opposition marched on 6 October 2026 to demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar quit over the Special Intensive Revision. Removing him would still need a special majority in both houses of Parliament, which the opposition lacks.
source: calling for Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to quit.

prompt: Consider the following statements relating to government-backed equity funds for small businesses in India:
items: The Self-Reliant India Fund, set up in 2021, makes direct equity investments in micro enterprises that the government itself selects.
The SME Growth Fund approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2026 was first announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong. The SRI Fund routes money to micro enterprises through private funds that pick the businesses, whereas the Cabinet describes the SME Growth Fund's investments as direct. The SME Growth Fund was first announced in the February 2026 Budget and approved in October 2026.
source: This year's Budget topped up the Self-Reliant India (SRI) Fund, set up in 2021, which routes money to micro enterprises through private funds that pick the businesses.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the SME Growth Fund approved by the Union Cabinet in October 2026:
items: It has an approved outlay of INR 100 billion.
Most of the fund is earmarked for manufacturing firms.
The government's commitment flows into an Alternative Investment Fund set up under the scheme.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three are correct. The Cabinet approved INR 100 billion (USD 1.04 billion), mostly for manufacturing firms, routed through an Alternative Investment Fund. The fund targets SMEs past the startup stage that lack long-term capital to expand, buy technology or enter export markets.
source: The Union Cabinet has approved INR 100 billion (USD 1.04 billion) for a new SME Growth Fund.

prompt: Under the labour law changes that took effect on 21 November 2025, factories need government permission for layoffs only once they employ at least how many workers?
explain: The threshold was raised to 300 workers, up from 100. Together with the SME Growth Fund approved in October 2026, this eases two hurdles mid-sized manufacturers faced when trying to scale.
source: Factories now need government permission for layoffs only once they employ 300 or more workers, up from 100.

prompt: In October 2026, a court granted beverage makers a temporary reprieve over the use of the phrase "energy drink" on their products. Consider the following statements:
items: In June 2026, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) barred high-caffeine beverage makers from using the "energy drink" label.
The court allowed the companies to sell existing inventory manufactured on or before 6 October 2026.
The court permitted fresh production runs carrying the label until the existing stock was cleared.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 3 is wrong: any new production run carrying the banned label faces immediate seizure, and only stock made on or before the date of the order can be sold. The court criticised FSSAI for issuing the order without any transition time.
source: Big Beverage can sell inventory manufactured on or before Tuesday, but any new production run carrying the forbidden label will face immediate seizure.

prompt: In October 2026, which court allowed PepsiCo, Monster, Reliance and Red Bull to clear existing stock labelled "energy drink" after the food regulator banned the phrase?
explain: The Delhi High Court granted the temporary reprieve after state authorities had seized inventory and pulled hundreds of millions of cans off shelves. It said it was "never too late" to fix a mistake.
source: The Delhi High Court granted PepsiCo, Monster, Reliance, and Red Bull a temporary reprieve on Tuesday, permitting them to clear existing stock labeled "energy drink" after the food regulator banned the phrase.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister Gati Shakti National Master Plan, as of 2026:
items: Approval and delivery of projects remain with individual ministries and states.
By August 2026, its Network Planning Group had evaluated 198 projects in all.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Network Planning Group had evaluated 396 projects, of which 198 were under implementation. Gati Shakti brings ministries and states onto a shared digital planning platform, and the new ITLA is meant to complement that framework.
source: By August, its Network Planning Group had evaluated 396 projects, with 198 under implementation.

prompt: In October 2026, a projectile struck the commercial vessel MT On Peace in the Strait of Hormuz, injuring several Indian sailors. Consider the following statements about this incident:
items: The vessel was flagged in Panama.
The Ministry of External Affairs statement identified the attacker.
The injured crew were evacuated to Khasab in Oman for treatment.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the MEA condemned the attack and called the targeting of shipping a cause of deep concern, but its statement did not name an attacker. The strike followed a 13 September 2026 attack on a merchant vessel off Oman with 14 Indians aboard.
source: Omani authorities helped evacuate the injured, who are being treated in Khasab, Oman.

prompt: In October 2026, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) named the countries in preliminary talks to host the 2036 Summer Olympics. Consider the following statements:
items: India is one of seven countries in these talks, alongside Qatar, South Africa and South Korea, among others.
The IOC is scheduled to make its final decision on the 2036 host in March 2027.
Ahmedabad is due to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong. March 2027 is when the IOC draws up a shortlist, with preferred hosts named in 2028 and a final decision in mid-2029. India has never hosted the Games, and the other contenders are Germany, Hungary and Turkey.
source: The IOC will draw up a shortlist in March 2027, name preferred hosts in 2028, and make a final decision in mid-2029.

prompt: In October 2026, the Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate. Consider the following statements about this decision:
items: It was the RBI's first repo rate hike in nearly four years.
The Monetary Policy Committee's decision to change its policy stance was taken by a split vote.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to change its stance. The 25 basis point hike was the first in nearly four years and formally signalled an end to monetary easing.
source: The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 percent on Wednesday, making its first hike in nearly four years and formally signaling an end to monetary easing.

prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the RBI's monetary policy decision of October 2026:
items: Repo rate after the hike — 5.5%
Revised FY27 inflation projection — 5.2%
Revised FY27 real GDP growth forecast — 7.1%
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: All three are correct: the repo rate rose to 5.5%, the FY27 inflation projection was raised to 5.2% from 5.0%, and the FY27 growth forecast was upgraded by 40 basis points to 7.1%. Rising oil prices from West Asia instability and a weak southwest monsoon with El Niño pushed up food and energy costs.
source: The RBI revised its FY27 inflation projection up to 5.2% from 5.0%, with headline CPI expected to average nearly 5.8% over the next three quarters.

prompt: In October 2026, the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee changed its policy stance from "neutral" to which of the following?
explain: The MPC moved from a neutral stance to calibrated tightening. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said rate cuts were off the table for the near term, leaving only further hikes or pauses.
source: The Monetary Policy Committee unanimously voted to alter its stance from "neutral" to "calibrated tightening."

prompt: Consider the following statements about the Black Sea truce proposal India made to Russia and Ukraine in September 2026:
items: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar presented the plan during a visit to Moscow.
Besides halting attacks on energy facilities, the plan seeks to end strikes on commercial shipping in the Black Sea.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Jaishankar presented the plan in Kyiv, not Moscow. Its three parts cover stopping attacks on energy and other infrastructure, keeping grain and energy moving through Black Sea ports, and ending strikes on commercial shipping, though neither side had formally accepted it as of October 2026.
source: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar presented the plan during his visit to Kyiv last month.

prompt: In October 2026, Ukraine was weighing four truce proposals linked to the Black Sea. Consider the following pairs of proposing country and main focus of its proposal:
items: Egypt — Grain shipments
United States — Energy ceasefire
Türkiye — Energy ceasefire
ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
explain: Türkiye's proposal, like Egypt's, focuses mainly on grain shipments; only the US plan centres on an energy ceasefire. India's plan covers both, and Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called it the broadest of the four.
source: Egypt and Türkiye focus mainly on grain shipments, and the US on an energy ceasefire.

prompt: The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, signed into US law in September 2026, allows the US President to impose tariffs of up to what level on major buyers of Russian energy such as India?
explain: The Act lets the US President impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major buyers of Russian energy, whose purchases Washington says fund Russia's war. India's Black Sea plan gives it an argument against these tariffs, since its Russian oil purchases now come with a push to stop attacks at sea.
source: The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, signed into law last month, lets US President Donald Trump impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on India and other major buyers of Russian energy, whose purchases Washington says fund Russia's war.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the recommendations made by the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council in October 2026:
items: The Council recommended scrapping tax officers' arrest powers entirely.
The Council recommended raising the prosecution threshold from INR 10 million to INR 100 million.
The recommendations require legal amendments and notifications before taking effect.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the prosecution threshold is to rise from INR 10 million to INR 50 million, not INR 100 million. The arrest powers would go entirely, but nothing changes until the laws are amended and notifications are issued.
source: The Council recommended scrapping arrest powers entirely and raising the prosecution threshold from INR 10 million (USD 103,200) to INR 50 million (USD 516,100).

prompt: In October 2026, the GST Council recommended reforms to refunds and enforcement. Consider the following statements:
items: Exporters, and firms whose inputs attract higher tax than their finished products, would have 90 percent of their refund claims paid provisionally after an automated risk check.
Prosecution would remain for fraudulently claiming input tax credit without receiving goods, services or an invoice.
ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explain: Both statements match the Council's recommendations. Input tax credit offsets tax paid on purchases against tax owed on sales, and fake credit claims are the one offence the Council chose to keep prosecuting.
source: Exporters, and firms whose inputs attract higher tax than their finished products, would have 90 percent of their refund claims paid provisionally after an automated risk check.

prompt: In October 2026, the Centre capped trade margins on anti-cancer drugs outside India's existing price-control list. Consider the following statements about this move:
items: The cap applies only to generic and off-patent anti-cancer medicines.
Trade margins are capped at 30 percent of the maximum retail price.
It followed a September 2026 Supreme Court hearing in which judges flagged hospitals marking up cancer drugs tenfold.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the cap covers branded and generic, domestic and imported, and patented and off-patent medicines alike. Official sources estimate prices could fall by up to 70 percent, saving patients INR 25 billion a year, while the Supreme Court had pushed for a uniform 16 percent margin on all medicines.
source: On Thursday, the Centre capped trade margins, the markup added between manufacturer and patient, at 30 percent of the maximum retail price (MRP) for all anti-cancer drugs outside India's existing price-control list.

prompt: In October 2026, the Ministry of Communications responded to a claim that Starlink was being unfairly blocked in India. Consider the following statements about satellite broadband operators in India at that time:
items: All three licensed satellite operators had been assigned spectrum and had begun commercial operations.
The Ministry said security assessments were under way for each of the licensed satellite operators.
Eutelsat OneWeb, one of the licensed operators, is backed by Bharti Airtel.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Reliance's Jio-SES venture were all still awaiting spectrum assignment and final clearances before commercial launch. The Ministry called the suggestion of a discriminatory framework baseless and said all three were at broadly the same stage.
source: Starlink, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb, and Reliance's Jio-SES venture still await spectrum assignment and final clearances before launching commercial operations

prompt: In October 2026, the Defence Minister approved a revised procedure for Indian defence firms to use government test facilities. Consider the following statements about it:
items: Testing charges are waived for projects under the Innovations for Defence Excellence (iDEX), the Technology Development Fund (TDF) and the Make category.
Proof ranges will reserve a three-day slot each month for government-sponsored and self-funded development projects.
The procedure covers facilities run by the DRDO, government quality assurance agencies and the armed forces.
ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statement 2 is wrong: proof ranges will reserve a three-day slot each quarter, not each month. The revision opens proof ranges, field firing ranges and laboratory test facilities to Indian defence firms and waives charges for projects under the ministry's development schemes.
source: Proof ranges will now reserve a three-day slot each quarter for government-sponsored and self-funded development projects.

prompt: Consider the following statements about the India Mobile Congress (IMC) opened by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi in October 2026:
items: It was the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress.
At a side session, the government reiterated a target of at least 10 percent of global 6G patents and standards for India.
The Communications Minister set a goal of 1 billion 5G users in India by 2027.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because Jyotiraditya Scindia said India aims for 1 billion 5G users by 2030, up from 550 million. Minister of State Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani also called for Indian alternatives to imported network technologies such as chipsets, radios, routers and optical systems.
source: Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India has 550 million 5G users and aims for 1 billion by 2030.

prompt: In October 2026, the Union Renewable Energy Minister opened the Windergy India conference in Chennai. Consider the following statements about India's wind energy sector:
items: India's installed wind capacity stood at 59.2 GW as of 30 September 2026.
India added a record 6.05 GW of wind capacity in the financial year to March 2026.
India's target is 100 GW of installed wind capacity by 2030.
ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
explain: All three statements match the figures Pralhad Joshi gave at the conference. He said annual additions would beat the 6.05 GW record this year and that India is on track for 100 GW by 2030, which leaves about 40.8 GW still to be added.
source: India added a record 6.05 GW in the financial year to March 2026, and Joshi said annual additions would beat that record this year and that India is on track to meet its target of 100 GW of installed wind capacity by the year 2030.
